articles.title: Trump says envoys taking plan to ‘end the war’ to Moscow, Kyiv
articles.summary: WASHINGTON — US President Donald Trump said Friday that he was sending envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to Moscow and Kyiv with a plan to end the four-year-old Ukraine war. It will be the…

blocks.text: WASHINGTON — US President Donald Trump said Friday that he was sending envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to Moscow and Kyiv with a plan to end the four-year-old Ukraine war.
It will be the first time that Trump’s son-in-law Kushner and businessman friend Witkoff have visited war-torn Kyiv since Trump returned to office last year with a vow to solve the conflict.
Both US envoys have previously visited Moscow, leading to accusations that they have taken Russia’s side in negotiations.
“They’re bringing with them a proposal to end the war,” Trump told reporters when asked about the trip.
Trump would not say whether the plan involved Ukraine ceding territory as he has previously suggested but added: “We have an idea for peace.”

“I sent Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, two great negotiators. They’ve done a great job, and we sent them over to see whether or not we can get something done. And there may be a good chance that we’ll do it,” he said.
The US leader blamed the war that began with Russia invading Ukraine in February 2022 on a “personality problem” between Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
Zelensky earlier said he had proposed observing a ceasefire with Russia while the US envoys visit Moscow and Kyiv.

“There will be no airstrikes on our part, and Russia must reciprocally ensure a ceasefire — without its own airstrikes — for the duration needed to conduct these talks,” Zelensky said in his evening address.
A senior Ukrainian official told AFP the two envoys would visit Kyiv on Sunday. The Kremlin declined to comment on the matter.
A report in the US news outlet Axios said Kushner and Witkoff would travel on Friday, meet Putin at the Kremlin on Saturday, and then Zelensky in Kyiv on Sunday.
The two men have also been involved in negotiations for ceasefires in Gaza and Iran.
Trump meanwhile played down Germany’s move earlier this week to blame Russia for an attempted drone attack on an airport.
“I speak to him. I know him very well. Putin’s not looking to attack NATO territory,” Trump said in the Oval Office when an AFP reporter asked him about the German allegation.

Trump has long been skeptical about maintaining support for Ukraine and had a televised row with Zelensky in the Oval Office in February 2025. With Putin, he has veered between friendliness and frustration.
The US leader said on Thursday that he would ask Europeans to repay the American aid provided to Ukraine under the administration of his predecessor Joe Biden.
Trump has long demanded that Europeans shoulder more of the cost of Western support for Ukraine. /mr

articles.title: Federal Tories launch 'Conservatives for Canada' campaign ahead of Alberta referendum
articles.summary: The federal Conservatives have launched a campaign to engage their supporters and encourage them to vote to stay in Canada in the upcoming Alberta referendum.

image.caption: Conservative MP for Parkland Dane Lloyd rises during Question Period on Parliament Hill in Ottawa, Friday, April 17, 2026. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Calgary·New
The federal Conservatives have launched a campaign to engage their supporters and encourage them to vote to stay in Canada in the upcoming Alberta referendum.
Party launches website with info on how to vote, submit donations
· The Canadian Press
· Posted: Sep 04, 2026 6:10 PM EDT | Last Updated: 20 minutes ago
Albertans are set to vote on Oct. 19 on whether they want to remain a province or begin the legal process to hold a binding referendum on leaving the country.

In a speech he delivered in Calgary this summer, Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre called for Albertans to stay united and argued that separatists have a problem not with Canada but with the Liberal government.
"We don't need a different country in Alberta, we need different government policies in Ottawa," Poilievre said on June 8.
Edmonton area MP Dane Lloyd was named the caucus lead on the remain campaign.
"We are engaging conservative Albertans with a message, and the message is not that everything's all right," Lloyd said in an interview on Friday.
"We know the status quo needs to change. But our problem is not with Canada."
He said Albertans feel like "their voice isn't being heard, that their values are not being respected" by the federal government.

That feeling persists, he said, in spite of the fact that Prime Minister Mark Carney's Liberals cancelled the consumer carbon price, signed a memorandum of understanding with Alberta Premier Danielle Smith on resource development and referred a West Coast pipeline for approval as a project in the national interest.

Lloyd said the people he's spoken with at roundtables "still view themselves as patriotic Canadians" but they're frustrated with the way the province has been treated by federal governments dating back decades — with the exception of former prime minister Stephen Harper's Conservatives.
At a time when national pride is growing stronger across the country as a result of the trade war with the United States, "we need to engage that patriotism," Lloyd said.
The government for its part appointed a senior adviser on Alberta earlier this year. Morgan Breitkreutz was chosen to help co-ordinate the federal response to the Alberta referendum.
Conservatives launch website
Polls suggest the vast majority of Albertans want to remain in Canada.
Some of the groups actively lobbying for people to vote to begin the referendum process are arguing that a yes vote would create leverage with Ottawa.
Polling also suggests that separatism is primarily a right-wing issue and that a sizable amount of support for separation is coming from supporters of Smith's United Conservative Party.
Poilievre said earlier this summer that "all Conservatives will be campaigning for Canadian unity in Alberta."
Poilievre has been in Alberta over the summer to attend the Calgary Stampede and a slate of events in his riding of Battle River-Crowfoot.

items: Poilievre says those who vote for Alberta separation 'are not our enemies'

blocks.text: The Conservatives for Canada group launched a website on Friday and released a statement on social media.

Asked why the campaign was launched six weeks before the vote, and just over two weeks before MPs are set to return to Ottawa, Lloyd said he spent the summer meeting with people and it became clear that a concerted campaign was needed.

"As you know, during referendums the voter turnout can be very low. And I think it's critically important that we engage at least the 1.4 million Albertans that voted Conservative in the last election to get out and vote for a stronger Alberta within a United Canada," he said.
Elections Alberta said this week it is anticipating high turnout.
The provincial elections agency said it's received 290,000 requests for mail-in ballots so far, and that its polling suggests voter turnout could reach a record-breaking 85 per cent.
Lloyd said the "grassroots campaign" is operating within Elections Alberta's rules.
The campaign website prominently features donation buttons and offers information about how to vote and to volunteer.
With files from CBC News

articles.title: PQ leader says he's worried Ottawa is meddling in Quebec election
articles.summary: Parti Québécois Leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon says he's worried the Canadian government is meddling in the Quebec provincial election, saying there is a “possibility that we are facing the greatest…

image.caption: Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, leader of the Parti Québécois, says the federal government is trying to prevent his party from taking power in Quebec. (Radio-Canada)

blocks.text: Montreal

Parti Québécois Leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon says he's worried the Canadian government is meddling in the Quebec provincial election, saying there is a “possibility that we are facing the greatest federal interference in our affairs and our election since 1995.”
Paul St-Pierre Plamondon says recent federal announcements suggest unprecedented interference

St-Pierre Plamondon says during the eight years the Coalition Avenir Québec (CAQ) government was in power, the federal government quietly rejected every request from the province, but “for the past few months, the federal government has been multiplying announcements.”

Speaking during a news conference Friday while on the campaign trail ahead of the Oct. 5 election, St-Pierre Plamondon cited examples such as the $11-billion investment in the Davie shipyard, unveiled a few days before the campaign, and the recent agreement between Newfoundland and Quebec on Churchill Falls.
Then, he added, there was Wednesday’s announcement of a $4.7-billion investment to construct train cars in La Pocatière.

The PQ leader also suggested co-ordination between CAQ Leader Christine Fréchette’s campaign and Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government on the issue of the tariff war between Canada and the United States.
“The federal government and the CAQ are collaborating,” he said. “We cannot deny that the federal government is interested in the outcome of the Quebec election.”

He said the federal Liberal party doesn’t want a sovereignist government taking shape, but the PQ has been leading in the polls. He said “you have to connect the dots” when you see the federal government taking sudden interest in files that have stagnated for years.
“I am worried, and I have the right to voice that worry,” said St-Pierre Plamondon.
Fréchette denies allegations
But the CAQ leader and province’s premier isn’t hearing it.

“Absolutely not,” Fréchette retorted when asked about possible interference from Ottawa in the campaign. She said the announcements over recent weeks are good for Quebec and would not have occurred under a Parti Québécois government.
“It is essential to have partnerships with the federal government when it is good for Quebec, and then to stand our ground when necessary.”
Repeating a phrase she has used several times before, she said, “I don’t work for Ottawa. I don’t work against Ottawa. I work for Quebec.”
While the PQ has asked Élections Québec to investigate, the province’s Liberal Leader Charles Milliard accused St-Pierre Plamondon of seeing a conspiracy.
“But I don’t think there is a grand scheme behind all of this. In any case, no matter how many consultants the CAQ buys, they aren’t federalists. They are opportunists,” Milliard said.
Group's involvement challenged
St-Pierre Plamondon also called attention to alleged ties between the CAQ campaign and Mission Leadership Québec.

The group describes itself as a non-profit organization whose objective is to promote citizen participation, democratic dialogue and political awareness. It promotes itself as a non-partisan group that advocates for strengthening Quebec's place within the Canadian federation.

St-Pierre Plamondon described the group as a covert organization hijacked by figures linked to the federal Liberal Party. As proof, he cited a recent Journal de Montréal report stating that Mission Leadership Québec, which advocates for Canadian unity, received contracts to run campaign events for Fréchette’s team.

items: Parti Québécois leader's donations to federal Liberals in spotlight on Quebec campaign trail
'We are all in the same boat': PQ leader reaches out to anglophones ahead of election

blocks.text: The PQ asked Quebec’s chief electoral officer on Friday to investigate allegations of interference and illegal contributions by the group to benefit the CAQ campaign.
Asked Friday about her party’s ties to Mission Leadership Québec, Fréchette brushed off concerns, saying she doesn’t analyze how every group or company her party deals with runs its operations.
She said the CAQ has a contract with Mission Leadership Québec to organize two town halls and “that’s it. We don’t go beyond that.”
CBC reached out to Carney's office for comment and is awaiting a response.
Report by Radio-Canada's Jean-François Thériault, translated by Isaac Olson

articles.title: Nepal bet nearly everything on hydropower - the floods show why that's a problem
articles.summary: More than 10% of Nepal's energy generation capacity was knocked out by last week's floods.

blocks.text: Almost 100% of Nepal's electricity comes from hydropower, and it produces so much it earns nearly $200m (£147m) each year exporting hydroelectricity to India and Bangladesh.

But the very glaciers and mountains giving Nepal this massive natural advantage are succumbing to global warming - and last Wednesday's deadly floods have laid bare the risks to the nation's hydropower ambitions.
More than 1,300 people were killed, while thousands more are still missing.

The floods, which destroyed entire villages near the border of Nepal and Tibet, severely damaged 12 hydropower plants in the Trishuli River basin and knocked out more than 10% of Nepal's total power generation capacity. Operators tell the BBC they don't yet know if any of these facilities can be brought back to operation.

The state-owned Nepal Electricity Authority, which owns six of the 12 damaged facilities, has assured Nepalese households that supply remains adequate. But its spokesman Rajan Dhakal acknowledges that with climate-related disasters becoming more frequent, "the time has come for a rethink of our hydropower policy".
Only two-thirds of people in Nepal had access to electricity in 2010, and even connected households would face power cuts for up to 16 hours a day.

An expansion of hydropower infrastructure alongside efforts to tackle corruption and boost energy imports from India to fill seasonal gaps meant that by 2018, most of Nepal was enjoying 24 hours of power supply per day.

At present, there are 225 hydropower plants across Nepal with more than 3,900MW of installed capacity, according to the Nepal Electricity Authority - capable of powering some three million households simultaneously.

Hundreds more such facilities are either being constructed or in the pipeline. Most of them are built high up in the mountains, where they can seize fast-flowing currents to generate power. These projects require little to no storage system.

However, with the high-altitude regions of the Himalayas warming 50% faster than the global average, they face greater environmental risks. Preliminary investigations have pointed to a collapsed glacier and its bedrock as the cause of last week's flash flood.

While scientists say it is too soon to draw any firm links to climate change, Nepal's Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority previously said more than nine in 10 disaster events recorded between 2018 and 2024 were "related to climate".
Nepal's former Energy Minister Kulman Ghising, who called the catastrophic deluge a "once-in-a-century" event, says it holds lessons for designing plants and picking sites where they are built.

"We need to design the plants [to be more] resilient to the floods and, most importantly, adopt early-warning systems as well as robust emergency evacuation measures," he told environmental news outlet Mongabay.
Potentially hundreds of hydropower labourers, engineers and residents are thought to be trapped inside the mud-filled tunnels of these plants since the floods hit.

A "rethink" of Nepal's hydropower strategy could involve reservoir-based plants that need not be situated up in the mountains, says Dhakal from the Nepal Electricity Authority. These could allow water to be stored and released as needed, but would also involve significant economic and environmental costs.
Some question if Nepal has been too reliant on hydropower.
"We should not be putting all our eggs in one basket in these dangerous times," says renewable energy expert Kushal Gurung, who founded the clean tech firm WindPower Nepal.
"We need to seriously embrace other alternatives as well, like solar and wind. And for that we will need to revise our energy policy that is at the moment very pro-hydropower," he says.

The claim is echoed by Vivek Shastry, researcher at Columbia University's Center on Global Energy Policy, who argues that "meaningful additions of wind and solar generation is a resilience strategy that can limit single-point or interconnected electricity system failures in the future".
A report from the German aid agency suggests the technical potential for energy production from solar power in Nepal is around 10 times larger, external than that of hydropower.

Puspa Sharma, a senior research fellow at the National University of Singapore's Institute of South Asian Studies, agrees Nepal has to diversify its energy sources, but warns this can be done "only to a limited extent".

"While there is untapped capacity in wind and solar, hydropower really is the one that gives Nepal massive competitive advantage vis-a-vis its South Asian neighbours," he says, citing various studies comparing renewable energy potential in the region.
Hydropower continues to dominate large-scale investments in Nepal, and some climate activists say the funding has continued despite known disaster risks.

The Upper Trishuli-1 project, which has been all but destroyed after last week's floods, was one of Nepal's largest foreign direct investment ventures, valued at about $647m. Its backers include the Asian Development Bank and the International Finance Corporation.
The Upper Trishuli 3A, which has also been severely hit, was funded by China's Export-Import Bank.

Himanshu Thakkar, coordinator of the South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers & People, says international lenders were "acutely aware of the extreme danger to which they were exposing thousands of labourers, officials, residents, rivers, infrastructure and landscape".

"Their own reports repeatedly highlighted it. But they did not take any preventive steps, did not demand stringent checks and balances, nor were they prepared for a calamity they knew could occur," he says.

History has already shown the Trishuli River basin to be volatile, Thakkar says, pointing to how it had been hit by floods in the last two years. In September 2024, an unprecedented cloudburst over the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi river basins sparked flash floods in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading - settlements by the river that are also among the hardest hit from last week's floods.

Then in July 2025, a glacial lake in Tibet's Gyirong county burst and swept down this very same stretch of river into Nepal, killing at least 11 people. That flood damaged critical infrastructure and halted trade along the busy Nepal-China corridor. The border crossing was shut for nearly six months and had only reopened on 1 January this year.
Dhakal from the Nepal Electricity Authority admits that even if climate risk assessments were carried out correctly, "the designing of the plants may not have been done accordingly".
"Clearly we will need to improve in the way we build and operate our hydropower plants," he adds.

Private operators are already feeling the financial impact. Insurers have paid out around $40m for flood-related damage to more than 20 privately owned plants over the past three years, according to Uttam Bhlon Lama from the Independent Power Producers' Association of Nepal.
He warns insurance premiums are rising significantly and making the cost of doing business "unfeasible".

articles.title: ‘Trafficking’ raps vs Leviste, 6 others move from NBI to DOJ
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation has filed a complaint for qualified human trafficking against Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste, former Negros Oriental Rep. Jacinto “Jing”…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation has filed a complaint for qualified human trafficking against Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste, former Negros Oriental Rep. Jacinto “Jing” Paras and five others over an alleged plot to offer women and their sexual services to Executive Secretary Ralph Recto in order to set him up for “character assassination.”
This was according to NBI Director Melvin Matibag, who said the bureau had finished its probe of the so-called “honey trap’’ targeting the Malacañang official.
“It’s complete, the evidence is here, all the attachments … We are filing qualified (human) trafficking against seven individuals,” Matibag said in an interview with reporters on Friday.
Qualified human trafficking is a nonbailable offense.

Aside from Leviste and Paras, the respondents include a talent manager given the alias “Ken’’ and the four lawyers from the Rondain & Mendiola Law Firm, who according to the NBI, were supposedly tasked to fabricate statements against Recto using the women.
The NBI identified the four lawyers as Ruy Rondain, Orlando Mendiola, Patrick Criaga and Josemilio Manuel Apostol.
The ‘I’ in NBI
The complaint was filed at the DOJ around 3 p.m. Friday by Emeterio Dongallo Jr., the NBI director for the National Capital Region (NCR).
Matibag said the bureau is also considering filing an ethics complaint against Leviste at the House of Representatives and a disbarment case against the four lawyers next week.
In a Facebook post on Friday reacting to the filing, Leviste mocked the NBI, saying the “I” in the bureau’s initial stands for “imbento” (invention).

“They invent such nonsense using public funds while the country is drenched in floods,” said the congressman, a political nemesis of Recto. Both with roots in the local politics of Batangas province, the two had engaged in a bitter word war, swapping allegations of corruption and attempted bribery, before the honey trap controversy broke out.
Sought for comment, Paras said he is ready to face the charges, also dismissing them as “fabricated.”
Mendiola, one of the four lawyers, declined to comment before seeing a copy of the complaint. There was no reply from Rondain as of press time when the INQUIRER contacted him for an interview.
The NBI investigation began on July 28 with the arrest of Ken, who in a sworn statement revealed the alleged plot against Recto and implicated Leviste, Paras and the lawyers.

In an earlier interview with the Inquirer, Ken said he met with Paras and the lawyers in a restaurant that month about a plan to set Recto up by offering him four of the “female artists’’ being handled by the talent manager.
The plot allegedly involved claiming that Recto forced them to take drugs and have sex with him.

The lawyers, who Ken said introduced themselves as Leviste’s representatives, were tasked with crafting the “script.” Ken also said the Batangas congressman served as the scheme’s financier. —WITH A REPORT FROM GABRIEL LALU

articles.title: PhilHealth’s Top 10: Claims mostly for hemodialysis
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Coverage for hemodialysis treatments accounted for the biggest share of claims made at the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth) during the first six months of the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Coverage for hemodialysis treatments accounted for the biggest share of claims made at the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth) during the first six months of the year, amounting to P48.76 billion.
In a report posted on its Facebook page on Friday, PhilHealth said the kidney treatment was the highest among the top 10 procedures in terms of claims payment as of June.
Second was cesarean section, for which PhilHealth paid P4.88 billion; followed by chemotherapy sessions that amounted to P3.5 billion.
For facility-based emergencies, PhilHealth paid P3.15 billion, while for intensity modulated treatments, the state-run insurer had them covered to the tune of P3.11 billion.

Other procedures included in the list were animal bite treatments at P2.93 billion, followed by expanded newborn package, P2.81 billion; normal spontaneous delivery package, P2.73 billion; outpatient HIV/AIDS package, P2.46 billion; and maternity care package, P2.24 billion.
Medical cases
In another post on Thursday, PhilHealth listed the top 10 medical cases with the biggest share of claims payment from January to June this year.
Topping this list was community acquired pneumonia 3, which accounted for P12.76 billion in claims payment.
Community-acquired pneumonia refers to cases where a person acquires the disease in the community, not inside the hospital.

Cerebral infarction, or stroke, accounted for the second-largest share in claims payment, with PhilHealth paying a total of P2.76 billion. It was followed by acute gastroenteritis with P1.96 billion, dengue with warning signs with P1.78 billion, and urinary tract infection with P1.6 billion.

Other medical conditions included in the list were Stage 2 hypertension, which accounted for P1.1 billion in claims payment; chronic kidney disease stage 5, at P1.05 billion; bronchial asthma, P978.18 million; malignant hypertension, P975.2 million; and acute gastritis, P910.34 million.
‘Z benefits package’

PhilHealth also reported its payment of around P1.82 billion for its “Z benefits package” claims as of June this year, benefitting 34,268 members. The Z package is intended for patients with severe conditions that require expensive and long-term treatments.

Based on the PhilHealth website, some of the conditions covered under the Z package include acute lymphocytic/lymphoblastic leukemia, with a coverage of up to P500,000; breast cancer, up to P1.4 million; and prostate cancer, up to P100,000.
In total, PhilHealth said it has paid P210.09 billion in benefit claims as of June. /cb

articles.title: Gov’t holding census in areas Pax Silica hub may affect
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The government has begun updating the census of communities in Capas, Tarlac, as it seeks to determine “appropriate assistance and safeguards” for residents who may be affected…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The government has begun updating the census of communities in Capas, Tarlac, as it seeks to determine “appropriate assistance and safeguards” for residents who may be affected by the proposed industrial zone under the Pax Silica initiative planned for New Clark City in the town.

According to the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA), the agency leading the project, it has started validating the socioeconomic profile of families and residents, including indigenous peoples (IP), in Sitio Sapang Kawayan, which lies within and around the proposed 1,619-hectare hub.

This census update is being conducted with the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) and comes as the BCDA moves forward with plans for the Pax Silica hub—which it now calls the “Clark Advanced Manufacturing Park.”
The BCDA, however, did not provide the results of the census update, saying it is still consolidating the final figures with the NCIP.

“We want to assure the community that every family receives the exact support, protection, and opportunities they deserve as this vision comes to life,” BCDA president and CEO Joshua Bingcang said in a statement.

The updated census is intended to establish a more accurate community baseline that would guide safeguards, assistance and other measures for families that may be affected as project preparations advance, the BCDA said.
US-led partnership

It is only part of a broader process that includes community identification and validation, joint surveys and documentation, review of existing agreements and the eventual processing and release of appropriate assistance.
“We are building the foundation of the Clark Advanced Manufacturing Park on a principle of shared progress. True development means no community is left behind,” Bingcang said.

First introduced in April, the controversial artificial intelligence (AI) hub planned for New Clark City aims to establish a physical advanced manufacturing ecosystem that could serve as a platform for the Philippines’ participation in the broader Pax Silica initiative.

Pax Silica is the wider, United States-led international partnership focused on building trusted and resilient supply chains for critical minerals, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing and AI infrastructure and logistics.

It was launched in December 2025 as a coalition of seven countries—the United States, Australia, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Singapore and the United Kingdom. Since then, more than 30 countries have signed the Pax Silica Declaration, including the Philippines.

Last April 17, Trade Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo, also the managing head and vice chairperson of the Board of Investments, signed the declaration signifying the Philippines’ joining of Pax Silica.

Through this, the US Embassy in Manila said the Philippines and the United States will establish a 4,000-acre, or 1,600-hectare, industrial zone in the Luzon Economic Corridor (LEC) to serve as the “first AI-native industrial acceleration hub under Pax Silica.”
The US plans to build an industrial hub in the country as Washington seeks to cut reliance on Chinese technology and supply chains for AI, semiconductors and critical minerals.
Consultations

The BCDA said it has been holding consultations with Tarlac government officials, members of the clergy, academe and other stakeholders to discuss the proposed Pax Silica hub and gather concerns and priorities from communities in the area.
Through these engagements, the BCDA said it seeks to ensure that development planning takes into account not only the project’s economic potential but also the needs of affected communities.
The first site tipped to be developed is at New Clark City in Tarlac, projected to attract $40 billion to $70 billion in investments and generate more than 130,000 jobs.

Earlier, Bingcang said that over 50 companies—including several trillion-dollar tech firms—had expressed interest in investing in the first Pax Silica site. The BCDA has already signed a memorandum of understanding with a Korean and a Japanese company.
He noted that only one or two of the interested firms plan to build data centers, which generate relatively few jobs; the bulk of investment is expected to flow into manufacturing and clean energy.

Pax Silica is seen as a boon to the local mining industry as the country is endowed with abundant reserves of copper, nickel, chromite and cobalt. These “critical minerals” could be processed in-country and used in the manufacture of higher value technology products, such as semiconductors at Clark.
Bingcang said contract negotiations are expected this year.
Opposition

The BCDA is aiming to finalize a framework agreement for Pax Silica by November 2026. Bingcang said that if US President Donald Trump visits Manila that month for the 49th Asean Leaders’ Summit, the agreement could be unveiled as one of the major announcements marking the 80th anniversary of Philippines-US relations. Under that timeline, this will be followed by the planning stage in 2027, with construction expected to begin in early 2028.
However, Pax Silica continues to face broad domestic opposition over fears of community displacement and environmental, energy, and water risks.

Earlier, at a Palace press briefing, Bingcang addressed some concerns raised about the project, including its environmental impact, water supply, IP rights, mining, defense-related use, and legal and regulatory requirements.

He clarified that Pax Silica is envisioned as a manufacturing-driven industrial ecosystem rather than a large data center complex, noting that manufacturing offers greater potential for high-quality job creation.

Bingcang also emphasized that the collaboration among the United States and other countries participating in Pax Silica would be commercial, not military, in character. Thus, as a business engagement, there would be no need for Senate ratification which a bilateral treaty would require. —WITH A REPORT FROM INQUIRER RESEARCH

articles.title: Impeachment prosecutors: No need to call Lachica, others
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Saying it already has a strong case against Vice President Sara Duterte, the prosecution panel in her impeachment trial would no longer call three individuals believed to be…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Saying it already has a strong case against Vice President Sara Duterte, the prosecution panel in her impeachment trial would no longer call three individuals believed to be capable of delivering key testimonies.

Prosecution spokesperson and adviser Robert Ace Barbers said on Friday the requirements have already been met with regards to the first of four articles of impeachment against Duterte which alleges misuse of confidential funds (CFs) worth a total of P612.5 million.

“The three allegations in this article have already been substantiated by the previous witnesses presented. That’s misuse, misappropriation and irregular liquidation,” Barbers said in an online press briefing, adding that the prosecution will no longer call to the witness stand former Duterte aide Ramil Madriaga and former Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group (VPSPG) officials Col. Dennis Nolasco and Col. Raymund Dante Lachica.

Lachica, former head of the VPSPG, was identified by former special disbursing officer Gina Acosta as the recipient of the P500 million in confidential funds from the Office of the Vice President (OVP) although he was not a bonded official.
Nolasco played the same role when it came to CFs from the Department of Education (DepEd), according to previous House testimonies of former DepED special disbursement officer Edward Fajarda.
These statements and the fact that neither Lachica nor Nolasco is an OVP or DepEd employee already show violations in the use and liquidation of CFs, Barbers said. /cb

articles.title: SC to Ombudsman: Charge erring judges
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Ombudsman Crispin Remulla should file a complaint against judges if he has proof they had committed misconduct, the Supreme Court said in a rare response on Thursday. During a…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Ombudsman Crispin Remulla should file a complaint against judges if he has proof they had committed misconduct, the Supreme Court said in a rare response on Thursday.

During a budget hearing at the Senate earlier that day, Remulla questioned why some cases dismissed by the Office of the Ombudsman were revived anew by the appellate court, which prompted his broad observation that the judiciary should go on a “soul searching” because of its “issues.”

The high court said in a statement “The Court takes allegations of partiality, misconduct and corruption seriously. It acts on such allegations when proper complaints are filed, evidence is presented and the judges or justices concerned are given the opportunity to respond.”
“This will allow the court to determine the facts and, when warranted, exercise its disciplinary authority,” it added.
IBP weighs in
Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) president Allan Panolong was also prompted to issue a statement saying it is “easy to paint corruption against our courts, but it needs to be substantiated.”

“The proper way is to make a formal complaint before the (Supreme Court) against the judge or justice who is allegedly involved in any corrupt act relative to a pending case before their sala so that appropriate investigation will be made and the judiciary official will be held accountable if found guilty,” Panolong said.
Remulla earlier said the high court should “police the judiciary” for being too lenient on respondents accused of graft.
He expressed frustration as to why court rules allowed them to post bail, at the court’s discretion, even after conviction. /cb

articles.title: Duterte lawyers raise concerns over prosecution microsite
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The defense lawyers of former President Rodrigo Duterte at the International Criminal Court (ICC) are calling for the stricter authentication of prosecution evidence that came…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The defense lawyers of former President Rodrigo Duterte at the International Criminal Court (ICC) are calling for the stricter authentication of prosecution evidence that came from open source materials, as his trial for alleged crimes against humanity draws near.

According to a document released on Friday, Peter Haynes, Duterte’s lead counsel, asked the ICC’s Trial Chamber III to amend the “E-Court Protocol,” the court’s electronic system, by adding an “expert verification field” for the listing of items to be cited as evidence.
The move was made ahead of the trial which starts Nov. 30.
‘New challenge’

Haynes noted that the microsite created by the Office of the Prosecutor (OTP), called “OTPLink” with the URL appeals.icc-cpi.int, for the anonymous submission of materials created a “new challenge” for the defense as it was supposedly vulnerable to tampering.

The prosecution launched the microsite in December 2024 to call for more witnesses and more documentary evidence when Duterte’s case was still at the pretrial stage. It encourages past and present police officers and other members of law enforcement agencies to come forward virtually and help in the investigation of the killings during Duterte’s war on drugs.

“There is also the obvious danger that nefarious actors will use the system to transmit falsified, manipulated, or forged evidence, which might also be circulated online; a risk identified by the Office of the Prosecutor itself,” the defense said in the document dated Aug. 31.

“[W]ith three months until the start of trial, the defense is deeply concerned that the quality and quantity of the evidence in this case risks flooding the record with unreliable and/or irrelevant material. This would be detrimental for the parties and the chamber’s search for the truth, and reputationally damaging for the court,” it noted.
The prosecution, defense and the legal representatives for victims initially agreed to add a “URL” field to identify materials from open sources, which could not be easily attributed to a witness.

But the defense argued that merely providing the URL of an “open source evidence” is not enough to prove its authenticity and avert the risk of collecting false information, adding: “The URL merely records the web location from which a piece of online content was collected; it cannot indicate its source.”

“Aside from the limitations as to what can be inferred about the source from a URL, it further says nothing of: the discovery process, which is vital to confirm its chain of custody; whether an item has been edited in any way; whether the content featured at that URL has been independently verified; whether AI (artificial intelligence) tools were used to filter the evidence, and whether there are any other indicia of authenticity and reliability,” it added.

As a remedy, the defense wants “expert verification reports” alongside the crowdsourced items to indicate information on the source, whether sender or creator if known; its chain of custody and whether it is original or a copy; its metadata, time of capture and other technical details; the steps taken to verify the information; as well as the qualifications and experience of the person who vetted the information.
“Without this information, it would be very difficult for the chamber to come to a view on the evidence’s relevance and admissibility,” it said.

The defense cited the OTP’s annual reports that more than 570,000 electronics had been collected from the microsite as of 2025 to point out the voluminous nature of the materials being gathered by the prosecution.

“Since the first status conference in this case, the prosecution has been on notice that the Trial Chamber wishes to avoid ‘unnecessary and irrelevant evidence’ being ‘dumped into the court record’,” it stressed.
This was one of Korner’s reminders to the parties during the first status conference in May to prevent a “wholesale” of documentary evidence that are deemed not useful to the case.

Based on disclosures publicly available, the prosecution has turned over nearly 7,000 pieces of evidence to the legal team of Duterte in the first seven months of the year. But according to the defense, in its latest filing, more than 25,000 items have been disclosed, with more expected to come.

The latest request by Duterte’s lawyers comes after they also urged the TC III to order the prosecution to amend the scope of the charges in terms of counts for a “more defined scope” of the crimes under the jurisdiction of the ICC.

They also asked for an exhaustive list of “underpinning acts which represent the entirety of the charges against the accused.” Duterte, who is detained in the Scheveningen prison complex in The Hague, is accused of three counts of murder as a crime against humanity in connection with the deaths of 76 people from 2013 to 2018. /cb

articles.title: Bonoan pleads not guilty to graft in flood scam
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan on Friday pleaded not guilty to a graft case, hours after he was released following the dismissal of two separate cases of plunder…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan on Friday pleaded not guilty to a graft case, hours after he was released following the dismissal of two separate cases of plunder and graft in connection with the flood control scandal.
Bonoan’s counsel Stephanie Ong entered the plea during his arraignment before the Sandiganbayan’s Second Division, which is chaired by Presiding Justice Geraldine Faith Econg.
The graft case links him to an alleged conspiracy with Sen. Jinggoy Estrada to include flood control projects in the 2025 budget, from which Estrada allegedly got a P213.7-million kickback.
The Second Division earlier denied a motion by Ombudsman prosecutors to amend the information to discharge Bonoan.
Discharged a free man
After the arraignment, the court proceeded to pretrial, overruling a manifestation from Ong who argued that her client was “not yet ready,” since he had yet to submit his pretrial brief.

On Friday morning, Bonoan, 81, was discharged a free man from the Philippine National Police General Hospital in Camp Crame, where he had been confined for treatment of ailments since his surrender in June.
He did not face the media. /cb

articles.title: Rome pushing back vs golf cart ‘invasion’
articles.summary: ROME, Italy — Beneath its splendor of monuments and ruins, the Eternal City is taking aim at a modern-day chariot: the golf cart. Even rolling along at a moderate speed, these golf carts have so far…

blocks.text: ROME, Italy — Beneath its splendor of monuments and ruins, the Eternal City is taking aim at a modern-day chariot: the golf cart.
Even rolling along at a moderate speed, these golf carts have so far outpaced regulation—with hundreds of them carrying tourists through Rome’s historic center. But the city is mounting a crackdown.
For critics, the carts are running amok, parking illegally, worsening congestion and unlocking another level of overtourism.
Some local media invoke sensational language, calling it an “invasion” and saying Rome is being “held hostage by golf carts.”
But advocates argue the carts are silent, occupy less space than tourist vans and buses, and don’t choke the air with exhaust that also stains historic monuments.
Enmity on the road
The Associated Press (AP) got a taste of the enmity during a late August ride when a black, eight-seater van pulled up alongside.
“You’re in the middle of the road!” its driver barked. “Move it!”
“Always the same! The road isn’t yours!” the golf cart driver shouted back. Both gesticulated angrily with their free hands, following a time-honored Roman traffic tradition.
Carts like this zip through Rome’s cobblestone alleys, past tourists eating spaghetti carbonara from checkered tablecloths and shops hawking tote bags stamped with clichés (“Ciao Bella!”).
“We don’t have a proper stop for golf carts, so we park where we can—as legal as possible,” driver Martin Halili said.
Little room for parking

Even before the golf cart boom, parking was a pain. Cars, vans, Vespas and motorcycles are stationed atop curbs, crosswalks and medians. Trucks double-park while unloading. Plus, an average 50,000 vehicles enter daily.

Unsurprisingly, some residents are unhappy. “This was the last straw because, unfortunately, there has already been traffic here for a long time, since there are too many categories of vehicles authorized,” Luigi la Licata, head of the Monti neighborhood association, told AP. “The golf cart is the most obvious one—and the latest—but there are many others.”
Golf cart bookings this summer grew 147 percent from 2024, according to TripAdvisor, whose subsidiary Viator is the biggest source of passengers.
Rome has as many as 500 carts, with one-fifth belonging to the Metur association of tour operators, established last December to seek common ground with locals and the city.

“Overtourism is a real problem, and we’re not denying it. And maybe we’re also part of it in a way. But if we’re part of it, then at least be part of it in a smart way,” Pascal van Duijnhoven, the association’s president, said. “We believe, especially for Rome, that it’s a solution. And we really hope that people start looking at it like this.”
EVs, carts of all types
Eugenio Patanè, Rome’s deputy mayor for sustainable mobility and transport, is striving to restore order and reduce traffic—not just golf carts.
In July, electric vehicles (EVs) started paying for admission to the historic center—a strategic shift from cutting emissions to tackling congestion.
The number of authorized vehicles is now down about one-quarter, to 350,000, and Patanè still aims to halve the number of daily entrants.
But it hasn’t been so simple to put the brakes on golf carts. For one thing, not all carts are created equal—technical specifications mean some fall under existing rules while others can roam freely.
Patanè aims to present regulation that would establish fixed tour routes, cap the number of carts of all types and create a system to select operators.
“Cities where this golf cart phenomenon is expanding truly have very few weapons,” he said, adding that “this phenomenon that has now become rampant and, in some cases, even worrisome.” /cb

articles.title: Ex-safety manager given 19 months’ prison over five-year-old’s hyperbaric chamber fire death
articles.summary:
Jeffrey Mosteller pleaded no contest to charges relating to burning death of Thomas Cooper in Michigan

A former safety manager has been sentenced to one year and seven months in prison in…

blocks.text: A former safety manager has been sentenced to one year and seven months in prison in connection with the death of a five-year-old Michigan boy who was killed in a fiery January 2025 explosion inside a hyperbaric oxygen chamber.
Jeffrey Mosteller, 66, received that sentence after pleading no contest to involuntary manslaughter in Oakland county circuit court in Michigan on Monday.

He worked as the safety manager at the Oxford Center, an alternative healthcare facility that treats children with a range of health conditions – including autism, ADHD and autoimmune diseases – using hyperbaric oxygen therapy.
Mosteller faced up to 15 years in prison before being handed his 19-month sentence.

Five-year-old Thomas Cooper, of Royal Oak, Michigan, was undergoing treatment for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and sleep apnea at the Oxford Center in the Detroit suburb of Troy when a fire erupted inside the hyperbaric chamber. That triggered an explosion which killed Cooper.

According to an expert who viewed video of the case, the child had squirmed enough to pull the sheet off a mattress inside the chamber, causing a spark of static electricity. That spark became a flash fire that incinerated him within seconds because of the oxygen-rich environment surrounding him.
Cooper’s mother was badly burned on her arms and chest while desperately trying to open the tank.
Mosteller is one of four former Oxford Center employees charged in connection with Thomas’s death. The other three were still awaiting trial at the time of his sentence.

The Oxford Center founder and chief executive, Tamela Peterson, 58, was charged with second-degree murder. Facility manager Gary Marken, 65, was charged with second-degree murder and involuntary manslaughter. And Aleta Moffitt, 60, who was operating the chamber when it exploded, was charged with involuntary manslaughter and intentionally placing false medical information on a medical records chart.

The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared hyperbaric chambers to be marketed as safe and effective for 13 disorders, including severe burns, decompression sickness and non-healing wounds. The therapy works by delivering pure oxygen to a person’s body inside a pressurized chamber.

Despite its FDA approval in certain cases, hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) has been a growing source of controversy as the safety of these chambers have been called into question. Many allies of Trump administration health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr have endorsed HBOT, but many others have expressed skepticism towards the treatment’s increasing push into the healthcare mainstream.
Cooper’s parents filed a $100m wrongful death lawsuit against the clinic and the chamber’s manufacturer over their son’s death.

articles.title: Trump says Witkoff, Kushner heading abroad in latest U.S. effort to end Ukraine war
articles.summary: U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, Donald Trump's son-in-law, are heading abroad to attempt to forge a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine, ‌the U.S. president told reporters on…

image.caption: U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters on Friday that he is sending Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner abroad in the latest American effort to forge a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine. (Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, Donald Trump's son-in-law, are heading abroad to attempt to forge a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine, ‌the U.S. president told reporters on Friday.
Zelenskyy says U.S. envoys will arrive in Ukraine Sunday after going to Moscow first

During comments in the Oval Office, Trump suggested the U.S. had a fresh concrete proposal aimed at ending the war, which is now in its fifth year. He ​did not, however, elaborate on what that proposal would ​be, nor did he say if Witkoff and Kushner would be travelling to Ukraine, Russia or both countries.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy ​on Friday said the two men would fly to Ukraine on Sunday ⁠after visiting Moscow.
"We ⁠have an idea for peace," Trump ‌said.

"I sent Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, two great negotiators. They've done a great job, and we sent them over to see whether or not we can get something done. And there may be a good ⁠chance that we'll do it."
Itinerary has been in flux: sources

The duo had been planning to travel to Moscow over the weekend followed by a visit to Kyiv, two sources previously told Reuters. However, the ‌itinerary has been in flux in recent days, and the Kyiv section of the journey was still not completely certain, one of the sources said on Friday.
The Trump administration's attempts to settle the war in Ukraine have largely ​come to nothing, and negotiations stalled out in recent months.

In late August, Central Intelligence Agency Director John Ratcliffe ⁠travelled to Moscow in part to press counterparts there to consider a settlement, Reuters ⁠and several other media outlets reported.

Most Western intelligence officials doubt Russian President Vladimir Putin ⁠is ⁠interested in a short-term deal, ​while Ukrainian intelligence believes he is in fact likely to escalate, rather than de-escalate the war ​in the near term.
Intelligence warns Putin is preparing escalation in Ukraine
A ⁠Russian drone hit the headquarters of Ukraine's SBU security service in Kyiv on Friday in one of the most high-profile targets struck during the war.
Witkoff, who is effectively the lead U.S. negotiator with respect to the war in Ukraine, has travelled to Moscow ⁠numerous times but has not yet ‌visited Ukraine.

articles.title: NLEx traffic eases, nears normal after 8-hour gridlock
articles.summary: PULILAN, BULACAN, Philippines — Traffic along flood-hit sections of the North Luzon Expressway (NLEx) began to normalize, with motorists now facing only about 11 minutes of slow-moving traffic in the…

blocks.text: PULILAN, BULACAN, Philippines — Traffic along flood-hit sections of the North Luzon Expressway (NLEx) began to normalize, with motorists now facing only about 11 minutes of slow-moving traffic in the affected portions of Pampanga, NLEx Corp. said on Friday.

This was a significant improvement from Aug. 29, when motorists were stranded for nearly eight hours as floodwaters from upstream Nueva Ecija cascaded toward Pampanga and inundated portions of the expressway.
The 20-kilometer stretch from Pulilan, Bulacan, to San Fernando City, Pampanga, now takes about 40 minutes to traverse, compared with the usual 20 to 25 minutes.
In the Tulaoc area, Lanes 1 and 2 have dried up, while the remaining lanes still have about 1 inch of water southbound and 5 inches northbound.
In San Simon, about 3 inches of water remained on Lane 1 in both directions. The deepest portions had about 8 inches of water northbound and 11 inches southbound.
Barriers
NLEx Corp. continued to install flood barriers and lay sandbags while conducting water siphoning and other flood mitigation measures along the expressway.
As part of its long-term measures, the company said it would again raise the pavement along the northbound and southbound sections of Tulaoc.
NLEx previously raised the pavement by about 0.7 meters in 2023 to improve the expressway’s resilience against flooding.
In 2025, the Department of Public Works and Highways began elevating the Tulaoc Overpass Bridge to provide the vertical clearance needed.
The company also provided toll rebates to motorists affected by last weekend’s gridlock.
The rebate took effect at noon on Wednesday for motorists using the San Fernando-Pulilan stretch in both directions and will remain in effect until all lanes are passable to all vehicle classes.
Class 1 vehicles will receive a P113 rebate.

“We understand the difficulties experienced by motorists affected by the flooding in San Simon and Tulaoc, which is part of a wider emergency across Pampanga arising from the continuous Habagat rains resulting in elevated water levels at the Pampanga River,” the company said.
NLEx Corp. said the latest flooding was aggravated by the overflow of the Pampanga River, which affected the area’s ability to discharge excess water. /cb

articles.title: Passi City under state of calamity amid pest infestation
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY, Philippines — Passi City in Iloilo province was placed under a state of calamity on Friday as the red-striped soft scale insect (RSSI) infestation continued to spread, making it the…

blocks.text: ILOILO CITY, Philippines — Passi City in Iloilo province was placed under a state of calamity on Friday as the red-striped soft scale insect (RSSI) infestation continued to spread, making it the latest area to take the measure as the pest threatens sugarcane plantations across major producing areas of the country.
Passi City joins Negros Occidental and Negros Oriental provinces, Bais City and Bacolod City in Negros and Capiz province, which have also declared states of calamity over the RSSI infestation.

The declaration was made through City Council Resolution No. 2026-179 because of what the city government described as the “widespread and progressive infestation” of the pest and its impact on the local sugarcane industry and affected farmers.

The city government said it was coordinating with the Department of Agriculture, Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA), Iloilo provincial government and other concerned agencies to strengthen monitoring and containment measures.
It also said it was committed to assisting affected farmers and protecting the city’s sugarcane industry.
The declaration came as the SRA reported that the infestation had expanded dramatically nationwide.

As of Tuesday, some 134,386.10 hectares (ha) of sugarcane plantations nationwide had been reported affected by RSSI, equivalent to about 32 percent of the country’s sugarcane areas, according to records obtained by the Inquirer.
Worst-hit area
This represented an increase of about 40,000 ha in just a month. Outside Negros Island, 16,890.74 ha of sugarcane plantations in other parts of Western Visayas were reported infested.

Negros Occidental remained the country’s worst-hit province, with 95,140.92 ha affected, while Negros Oriental had 19,444 ha. Together, the two provinces accounted for about 85 percent of the country’s reported RSSI-infested sugarcane areas.
The SRA has warned that the approaching dry spell and the movement of sugarcane planting materials could accelerate the spread of the pest.

RSSI damages sugarcane by sucking sap from the plant and promoting the growth of black sooty mold. If uncontrolled, an infestation could reduce the sugar content of affected cane by as much as 50 percent, according to the SRA.
The pest problem had already been spreading in Iloilo months before Passi City’s calamity declaration.
In July, infestations were reported in Anilao, Dingle, Passi City, and northern Iloilo. /cb

articles.title: Air quality improves in Cebu but haze stays
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Classes remained suspended in several parts of Cebu on Friday as haze continued to blanket parts of Central Visayas, with Metro Cebu recording “very unhealthy” air quality…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Classes remained suspended in several parts of Cebu on Friday as haze continued to blanket parts of Central Visayas, with Metro Cebu recording “very unhealthy” air quality despite a slight improvement in pollution levels.

The Metro Cebu monitoring station recorded an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 197 as of 11 a.m. on Friday, down from Thursday’s peak of 252, according to the Environmental Management Bureau in Central Visayas (EMB-7).

The reading remained within the “very unhealthy” range, prompting Cebu City, Talisay, Lapu-Lapu and Carcar cities, and the municipality of Minglanilla to extend the suspension of in-person classes for Friday. In-person classes were first suspended on Wednesday.

EMB-7 said it continued to monitor ambient air quality to determine the extent and potential health impacts of the haze, which authorities said may have been caused by smoke from wildfires in Indonesia’s Kalimantan and Sumatra regions carried toward the Philippines by prevailing winds.

The Department of Health in Central Visayas (DOH-7) placed the region on heightened alert and directed hospitals to prepare for a possible increase in patients with respiratory complaints. Hospitals were also instructed to maintain priority lanes and adequate supplies of respiratory medicines, including bronchodilators.
No haze-related respiratory illnesses had been reported in Central Visayas as of Friday, health officials said.
Bohol situation

In Bohol, the municipal government of Bilar suspended classes in kindergarten, elementary and secondary schools, both public and private, starting Sept. 3 until further notice because of worsening air quality.
The Tagbilaran City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office earlier reported a PM2.5 reading of 48.7 as of 7:45 a.m. on Sept. 3, placing the city in a cautionary zone.
Residents were advised to avoid heavy-traffic areas, wear protective masks and postpone unnecessary trips. Those with heart and respiratory conditions were encouraged to stay indoors.

The EMB-Central Office said that, as of noon on Friday, air quality had improved in most areas of the Visayas and Mindanao. However, Iloilo City and La Castellana in Negros Occidental, Iligan City and Butuan City remained at levels considered “unhealthy for sensitive groups.”
“Very unhealthy” conditions were recorded in Talisay City, Cebu; Koronadal City, South Cotabato; and Cabadbaran City, Agusan del Norte.
Impact
Meanwhile, the Department of Education (DepEd) said it was closely monitoring the impact of the haze on schools, learners and personnel nationwide.
DepEd’s Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Service was coordinating with field offices and conducting validation in areas where elevated PM2.5 levels could pose health risks.

Schools were advised to limit prolonged outdoor activities, reduce outdoor exposure of vulnerable learners and personnel, and require well-fitting N95 masks or equivalent protection when outdoor activities could not be avoided.
They were also told to keep doors and windows closed when haze was noticeable and monitor official advisories from the Department of Environment and Natural Resources-EMB and DOH.
DepEd clarified that a “very unhealthy” AQI of 151 to 200 does not automatically trigger class suspension. Localized measures may be adopted depending on actual conditions.

Suspension of in-person classes becomes a decision of the local chief executive when air quality reaches the “acutely unhealthy” range of 201 to 300. Automatic suspension applies when pollution reaches the “emergency” level of 301 to 500.

The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council has directed concerned agencies to continue monitoring and implement precautionary measures based on local conditions. —WITH REPORTS FROM HAZEL P. VILLA, AND LEO UDTOHAN

articles.title: QC court orders Sara Duterte’s arrest in ‘threats’ case
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Two months into her Senate impeachment trial, Vice President Sara Duterte is now facing a second battle—this time in a regular court. The Quezon City Regional Trial Court (RTC)…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Two months into her Senate impeachment trial, Vice President Sara Duterte is now facing a second battle—this time in a regular court.

The Quezon City Regional Trial Court (RTC) on Friday issued an arrest warrant for the Vice President over the alleged assassination threats she made against her former ally, President Marcos, paving the way for the case to proceed to trial.

The case stemmed from the profanity-laced statements she made against the President, first lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former Speaker Martin Romualdez, a cousin of Marcos, at an online press briefing two years ago.

A copy of the arrest warrant dated Sept. 4 and signed by Presiding Judge Maria Angelica De Ramos showed that the court had set bail at P120,000 for each of the three counts of grave threats in violation of Section 6 of Republic Act No. 10175, or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.
De Ramos’ order indicated Duterte’s office address to be at Robinsons Cybergate Plaza along Edsa in Mandaluyong City, where the warrant may be served.

Duterte has yet to post bail at press time, though her lawyer, Paul Lawrence Lim, said in a statement earlier in the day that she “has no intention of evading the law and will continue to exercise all her legal remedies.”
Prosecutors at the Department of Justice (DOJ) charged Duterte last month with grave threats, citing the late-night news briefing on Nov. 23, 2024, where she said:

“‘Wag kang mag-alala sa security ko kasi may kinausap na ko na tao. Sinabi ko sa kaniya, ‘‘pag pinatay ako, patayin mo si BBM, si Liza Araneta, at si Martin Romualdez.’ No joke, no joke (Do not worry about my security because I already spoke to someone. I said, ‘If I am killed, kill BBM, Liza Araneta, and Martin Romualdez.’ No joke, no joke).”
Proceed to trial

The Vice President was then fuming over the detention of her chief of staff, Zuleika Lopez, by the House of Representatives, where lawmakers earlier cited Lopez in contempt during a committee inquiry into Sara’s alleged misuse of confidential funds.

The threats later constituted one of the four main charges in the articles of impeachment adopted by the House against the Vice President, which the Senate is currently hearing as an impeachment court.
House prosecutors devoted the first trial sessions to the presentation of evidence and witnesses regarding the threats, covered under Article 4, in nine hearings from July 7 to July 22.

Among the key witnesses presented were officials of the National Bureau of Investigation, who were asked to authenticate the livestream recording of the briefing and also expound on the threats as a national security concern since they were directed at the President.

DOJ spokesperson Polo Martinez said a separate resolution issued by Branch 98 of the Quezon City RTC dismissed the motion earlier filed by Duterte’s lawyers to defer or recall the issuance of the arrest warrant against her.

“The case shall now proceed to trial,” Martinez said in a message to reporters. “As a matter of procedure, warrants of arrest are transmitted directly by the court to the appropriate law enforcement agencies for implementation.”
“The department respects the court’s ruling and reaffirms its commitment to the rule of law,” he added.
Challenge before CA

The DOJ reiterated its earlier position that immunity rests solely on the President as the Chief Executive. “Which is why the DOJ filed the case against the accused (Vice President),” Martinez stressed.

The alleged assassination threat forms a crucial element of Duterte’s ongoing impeachment trial, where a guilty verdict would see her removed from office and spell an end to a planned run for president in 2028. Duterte first announced her candidacy in February.
Under Philippine laws, a criminal conviction on the charge of grave threats would carry a jail term of up to six months.
Paolo Tamase, associate dean at the University of the Philippines College of Law, told Agence France-Presse (AFP) that the warrant could yet be challenged at a higher court.
“She can potentially question the issuance of the warrant of arrest, which means she would go up to the Court of Appeals (CA) or potentially the Supreme Court,” he said.
DOJ officials have rejected arguments by the Vice President’s legal team that she cannot be prosecuted for offenses that are also tied to her impeachment.
Duterte was impeached in May by the House of Representatives on charges that also included graft and corruption.
Bicol Saro Rep. Terry Ridon said the criminal case is separate from Duterte’s impeachment proceedings, noting that the prosecution panel will continue to press on.

Ridon, a member of the House prosecution panel in the impeachment trial, said the arrest warrant is “not, by itself, a determination of guilt.” He also said the Vice President “will have every opportunity to present her defenses before the proper court.”

“The impeachment proceedings are a separate constitutional accountability process. The Senate Impeachment Court will independently determine the matters properly before it,” Ridon said in a statement on Friday.
“For its part, the House prosecution panel will continue performing its constitutional mandate and prosecute the impeachment case until its conclusion,” he added.
Probable cause
Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong said the warrant has also reminded the public that courts do not make such decisions without finding probable cause.

“The issuance of an arrest warrant is not a finding of guilt. Due process must be observed at every stage,” Adiong said in a statement on Friday. “A court, however, does not issue a warrant without probable cause. That determination has now been made.”

He added that every legal remedy must be made available to Duterte, but she should avail of those remedies within the court and not outside it. —WITH REPORTS FROM AFP, GABRIEL PABICO LALU, AND LUISA CABATO

articles.title: Hamilton NHL prospect Matthew Mayich 'needs a miracle' after training collapse, family lawyer says
articles.summary: Hamilton-born NHL prospect Matthew Mayich 'needs a miracle' in hospital after he collapsed during a 'brutal' workout at Arizona State University last month, according to his family's lawyer. Rob…

image.caption: Matthew Mayich is pictured in a St. Louis Blues jersey in a photo the team shared August. 26. (St. Louis Blues)

blocks.text: Hamilton

Hamilton-born NHL prospect Matthew Mayich 'needs a miracle' in hospital after he collapsed during a 'brutal' workout at Arizona State University last month, according to his family's lawyer. Rob Carey is calling for the university to investigate the incident.
Lawyer for St. Louis Blues draftee calls for investigation into 'brutal' workout at Arizona State University
Hamilton-born NHL prospect Matthew Mayich "needs a miracle" after being hospitalized following a training incident at Arizona State University last month, his family's lawyer has said.

Attorney Rob Carey spoke to CBC Hamilton on behalf of Mayich's family on Friday, saying the 21-year-old's parents, who live in Hamilton's Stoney Creek area, are staying near the hospital to be with their son each day.
"They really appreciate the love and the prayers and the support they've received from their Canadian friends," the partner with U.S. law firm Hagens Berman Sobol Shapiro LLP said.

The St. Louis Blues draft pick collapsed following a morning workout at Arizona State University (ASU), Carey said. He said Mayich suffered exertional heatstroke causing a lack of oxygen to the brain.

A report in the journal BMJ Medicine describes exertional heatstroke as "the third leading cause of mortality in athletes during physical activity." It says data indicate mortality rates of about 27 per cent, with long-term negative health consequences for survivors.

items: Hamilton-born NHL prospect Matthew Mayich in Arizona hospital after 'training incident,' OHL says

blocks.text: University says senior vice-president reviewing incident
ASU confirmed a student on the hockey team collapsed during an Aug. 20 training session but has not named them, citing privacy obligations.

"The morning outdoor workout was a team event at which coaches and training staff were present along with a third party who had previously worked with the ASU Hockey team," the university said in a Sept. 3 statement.
ASU vice-president James Rund is leading a review, the school said, looking at "the workout and related university policies, procedures and training protocols."
The review will be conducted in a manner respectful of "the student-athlete, his family, his teammates and ASU’s privacy obligations," ASU said.
Mayich endured 'brutal' workout: lawyer

The university has been "tight-lipped" about what occurred, Carey said, but based on his own investigation, he believes Mayich endured a "military-style, brutal, grueling workout," with no breaks and no water for over an hour.

"You have an elite NHL-drafted athlete showing up on the first coach-led workout, the very first day the team could organize formally, and he left the field with no chance of recovery," Carey said. "Obviously there's something wrong."
When Mayich collapsed, the lawyer said that no one immediately immersed him in cool water, contrary to best practices for treating heat stroke.

It was about 31 C in Tempe, a college town just east of Phoenix, as of 7:51 a.m. on Aug. 20, according to Weather Underground. University police received a call about the hockey player's collapse around 8:30 a.m., ASU said.

items: Extreme heat is a global killer — and worse for our health than previously thought, new research shows

blocks.text: CBC asked ASU to respond to Carey's allegations and to provide details about its own investigation.
A spokesperson said they had no further information beyond the Sept. 3 statement.
The university has guidelines for heat illness, as well as for for how third parties interact with ASU athletes, the statement said.
Questions about the workout are part of ASU's review, it added.
Family's questions unanswered

"The goal right now is just to get evidence about what happened," Carey said. "We don't know why [the workout] was set up, who set it up, what was really designed for the day, what safety precautions were taken, and who made a decision not to have safety precautions ready."
The family wants a fair and complete investigation, involving witness interviews, security video and digital communications, he said.
"If it's not happening, then either we need a proper police department to investigate it or we will do it when we have the ability with a civil lawsuit," Carey said.
CBC asked the University of Arizona Police Department if it's investigating but did not receive a response.

items: Without a single heat threshold defining unsafe work, workers in B.C. say they're at risk and burnt out

blocks.text: Mayich mentored younger players in Hamilton
Mayich played minor hockey with the Hamilton Huskies between 2016 and 2020 then with the Ottawa 67's before the St. Louis Blues drafted the defenceman in the sixth round of the 2023 NHL draft.

During his six seasons with the Huskies and one as a member of the Hamilton Jr. Bulldogs, Mayich established "himself as a tremendous hockey player and, more importantly, an outstanding person both on and off the ice," the Hamilton Steel Hockey Club, formerly the Huskies, said.

The statement was sent to CBC Hamilton on behalf of the organization, former Huskies president Mike Spadafora and former Huskies head coach Chris Travale. Spadafora is currently the councillor for Hamilton's Ward 14, running for re-election.

"Without fail, whenever [Mayich] is asked, he comes back every year to speak and skate with a new crop of young kids," Travale said. "His message is always about so much more than hockey — it’s about relationships, friendships, and the experiences you have along the hockey journey.

"From everyone at Hamilton Steel Hockey Club, the Hamilton Huskies family, Hamilton Jr. Bulldogs and the Hamilton hockey community — Matthew remains in our thoughts and prayers, and our hearts are with him and the entire Mayich family."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Justin Chandler is a CBC News reporter in Hamilton. He covers stories of all kinds from places including picket lines, court rooms, council meetings and research labs. Justin has a special interest in how public policy affects people, and loves a quirky human-interest story. Before CBC Hamilton, he worked for TVO and on a variety of CBC teams and programs. He co-hosted Radio Free Krypton on Met Radio.
