articles.title: Families get aid after whirlwind damages houses in Ilocos Sur
articles.summary: SAN ILDEFONSO, ILOCOS SUR, Philippines — Families whose homes were damaged by a recent whirlwind in Masingal town received housing materials from the municipal government to help them repair their…

blocks.text: SAN ILDEFONSO, ILOCOS SUR, Philippines — Families whose homes were damaged by a recent whirlwind in Masingal town received housing materials from the municipal government to help them repair their houses and recover from the weather-related incident.
The local government unit of Magsingal distributed the materials to affected families from several barangays as part of its recovery and rehabilitation efforts.
At least 60 houses in the province were either damaged or destroyed by strong winds, government records showed.

The assistance came as tornadoes or tornado-like winds battered several parts of Ilocos Sur over Aug. 31 and Sept. 1, damaging houses and other structures and sending roofing materials and debris flying.
In San Ildefonso, a tornado struck Barangay Pudoc Norte at about 12:10 a.m. on Sept. 1, tearing off the roof of a house. No injuries were reported.
Tornado-like winds were also reported in nearby Caoayan, while strong winds damaged houses and structures in Cabugao, Sinait and Narvacan.
In Cabugao, strong winds swept through the town at about 5 p.m. on Aug. 31, with videos shared by residents showing roofing materials and debris being lifted by the winds.
A similar incident was reported in Barangay Zapat in Sinait, while five beach cottages in Barangay Sulvec, Narvacan, were damaged.

In Bantay, the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office conducted inspections and clearing operations in areas affected by the reported tornado. Response teams removed debris and other obstructions and monitored conditions to ensure public safety and keep roads and public areas accessible.
The incidents occurred amid the prevailing southwest monsoon, or “habagat,” which has been bringing periods of heavy rain and strong winds to parts of Northern Luzon.

Local authorities continued to assess the extent of the damage in affected communities. No fatalities or injuries had been reported from the tornado-related incidents as of the latest reports. —KENNETH P. TABIN/CONTRIBUTOR

articles.title: Motorcycle rider injured by falling tree branch in Pampanga
articles.summary: MABALACAT CITY, PAMPANGA, Philippines — A motorcycle rider was injured after a large tree branch fell on him while he was traveling along MacArthur Highway in Barangay Telabastagan, City of San…

blocks.text: MABALACAT CITY, PAMPANGA, Philippines — A motorcycle rider was injured after a large tree branch fell on him while he was traveling along MacArthur Highway in Barangay Telabastagan, City of San Fernando, on Friday morning, Sept. 4.

In a text message to the INQUIRER, the city’s Public Order and Safety Coordinating Office (CPOSCO) said the rider suffered a broken arm and was rushed to Jose B. Lingad Memorial General Hospital for treatment.
The victim’s damaged motorcycle was brought to Police Station 4 for documentation, CPOSCO said.

Traffic slowed in the area until shortly before noon, when the fallen branch was cleared. Electricity was also temporarily shut off in parts of Barangay Telabastagan while clearing operations were underway.

The incident renewed calls from some netizens for the trimming or removal of decades-old trees along the MacArthur Highway, citing the risks they pose to motorists during bad weather and strong winds.

“I was also involved in an accident caused by the branches of those trees; unfortunately, I now have a metal implant in my collarbone,” a netizen commented on a Facebook post about the incident. “What I simply don’t understand is why you haven’t removed them yet—they are a huge nuisance!”
Environmental groups, however, have opposed the removal of Acacia and other mature trees along the highway, particularly in connection with road-widening projects.
The trees were planted more than 50 years ago, when the national road was still a two-lane highway with shoulders on both sides.

In July 2010, an official of the Pampanga Chamber of Commerce and Industry called for the removal of trees along the highway, citing motorists’ and commuters’ safety. The call followed an incident in which an old Camachile tree fell on a public utility jeepney, injuring several passengers.

Those opposing the removal of the trees have argued that the mature trees provide shade, absorb carbon, and help manage heavy rainfall. They have also called for better infrastructure without sacrificing the environment. /cb

articles.title: Families of victim, minors involved in Baguio bullying reach settlement
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY, Philippines — The family of a student involved in a reported bullying incident in Barangay Pinget has reached an amicable settlement with the families of the other involved minors, one…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY, Philippines — The family of a student involved in a reported bullying incident in Barangay Pinget has reached an amicable settlement with the families of the other involved minors, one week after the incident.
The settlement was reached Friday, Sept. 4, following a series of discussions between the two sides in the presence of barangay officials.
Under the agreement, the family of minors involved will share P800,000 in fines, with the amount divided based on their respective participation in the incident.
The agreement also requires the minors to issue a public apology before the student’s family, barangay officials and police officers.
In their apologies, the minors acknowledged that what they did was wrong and asked forgiveness from the student, his family and the elders who helped resolve the matter.
They also promised not to repeat the incident and said they would report similar incidents in the future instead of participating in them.
The student’s mother appealed to the public to respect the family’s decision to settle the matter.

She said she consulted her child, who experienced trauma following the incident, before deciding whether to pursue a case. Her child, she said, chose to continue with their studies and forgive those involved, while she also considered the minors’ futures.
According to the mother, she hoped the minors would learn from the incident and that the settlement would allow everyone involved to move forward.
The student, meanwhile, said he had forgiven those involved and hoped that a similar incident would not happen again, either to him or to other students at Pinget.

The victim’s family also appealed to the public to stop circulating the incident on social media and to respect their decision to settle the matter. They expressed hope that all conditions of the agreement would be fulfilled.
The incident earlier drew public attention after a video involving the students circulated on social media.

Pinget National High School had appealed to the public to stop sharing, reposting or further circulating the video because minors were involved. The school said continued circulation could expose the children to public shaming, online harassment, cyberthreats and further trauma. —MAUREEN MATAYEW/CONTRIBUTOR

articles.title: UN votes to adopt new world map to reflect Africa's true size
articles.summary: The Togo-sponsored resolution was backed by 164 nations - the US the only nation to vote against it.

blocks.text: The Mercator map was designed in 1569 by the Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator to help European explorers navigate across the world.
The distortion of his map is a result of the fact that it is impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.
Whenever a map of the world is drawn, compromises need to be made.
The Mercator map shows the curvature of the Earth by making countries near the equator seem smaller than they are, with countries nearer the poles appearing bigger.
In an effort to correct this, a team of cartographers in 2018 created an equal area map they called the Equal Earth projection.
In February, the AU's 54 member states adopted it, saying it "more accurately represents the sizes of all continents, particularly Africa".
Ahead of Friday's vote, Togolese Foreign Minister Robert Dussey told the Reuters news agency: "A fair world begins with a fair map."
Earlier he had told a UN briefing: "A map is never neutral. It shapes perceptions, influences how the place of peoples and continents in the world is understood."
The UN vote is non-binding but will see changes to the maps used by institutions around the world.

articles.title: Argentine couple to return Nazi-looted painting to rightful owner
articles.summary: The late-baroque Portrait of a Lady was lost for 80 years until it was spotted in photographs of a house for sale near Buenos Aires.

blocks.text: A painting which was stolen by the Nazis and only recovered in Argentina last year must now be returned to the heir of its rightful owner, a court has ruled.
The late-baroque Portrait of a Lady was lost for 80 years until it was spotted in photographs of a house for sale near Buenos Aires.

The house belonged to Patricia Kadgien, the daughter of a Nazi fugitive who had fled there after the Second World War, and she has now agreed to return the painting in exchange for not being prosecuted for concealing it from the authorities.
Portrait of a Lady was among over 1,000 artworks looted from the collection of Jewish art dealer Jacques Goudstikker after the Nazi invasion of the Netherlands in 1940.

His daughter-in-law and sole heir Marei von Saher intends for the painting to be exhibited on a temporary loan at the Holocaust Museum of Buenos Aires to spread awareness of the issue, Argentine newspaper Clarin reports.
Von Saher has previously said her family "aims to bring back every single artwork robbed from Jacques' collection, and to restore his legacy".
This painting was first recognised in August 2025 by the Dutch Algemeen Dagblad (AD) newspaper on an estate agent's website of a property in the coastal town of Mar del Plata.

It was hanging above a green sofa in the living room of Patricia Kadgien, whose father Friedrich Kadgien had been a top adviser to Hermann Goring, Adolf Hitler's deputy. Goring plundered thousands of works across Europe.

articles.title: Helicopter search suspended for Squamish, B.C., mountain runner missing on Matterhorn
articles.summary: The helicopter search for Canadian mountain runner Kalie McCrystal, who was last seen on Tuesday above the Jean-Antoine Carrel hut of the Matterhorn, has been suspended after repeated aerial sweeps…

image.caption: The Matterhorn mountain is seen in the background at Zermatt, Switzerland, in 2019. Canadian mountain runner Kalie McCrystal was last seen on Tuesday near the Jean-Antoine Carrel hut of the Matterhorn. (Catherine Muzolf/Reuters)

blocks.text: World

The helicopter search for Canadian mountain runner Kalie McCrystal, who was last seen on Tuesday above the Jean-Antoine Carrel hut of the Matterhorn, has been suspended after repeated aerial sweeps of the Italian side of the mountain.
Kalie McCrystal last seen Tuesday heading toward the summit of the mountain on the Swiss-Italian border

The helicopter search for Canadian mountain runner Kalie McCrystal has been suspended after repeated aerial sweeps of the Italian side of the Matterhorn failed to locate the 38-year-old athlete and lawyer from Squamish, B.C.
The dedicated helicopter operation was called off after a full day of aerial searches on Thursday turned up no trace of her.
McCrystal was last seen on Tuesday above the Jean-Antoine Carrel hut, at roughly 3,830 metres, making her way toward the summit.
Rescuers initially deployed a large air ambulance helicopter before switching to a smaller aircraft able to manoeuvre closer to the mountain's sheer rock faces and narrow gullies.
"We moved to a much smaller helicopter that can go closer to the cliffs and see in the couloirs," Valerio Segor of the Valle d'Aosta mountain rescue service told CBC. "They didn't see anything."
The last confirmed encounter came when a mountain guide crossed paths with McCrystal above the Carrel hut.
"She saw her still going up, quite quickly, and [McCrystal] told the guide she was training because she wanted to try the record," Segor said. "No one saw her since then."
One of the most recognizable peaks of the Alps, the Matterhorn straddles Italy and Switzerland, standing 4,478 metres tall.
Helicopter search efforts

McCrystal had been based in the Cervinia area of northwestern Italy preparing for an attempt to climb and descend the Matterhorn in less than five hours via the Lion Ridge, the main route from the Italian side.
Her disappearance prompted an extensive reconnaissance of the mountain. Crews searched steep gullies, cliff bands and sections of the route on both the Italian and Swiss sides.

Segor said they also used a helicopter-mounted RECCO detector, a radar system capable of locating compatible reflectors incorporated into some outdoor clothing and equipment. A friend had told authorities McCrystal's backpack might contain one.
"We tried with the antenna that was mounted on the helicopter," he said. "And we didn't get any sign of anything such as a RECCO beacon" on either the Italian or Swiss side.
Attempts to establish a signal from McCrystal's cellphone also failed.
Past skyrunning experience
McCrystal is one of Canada's leading skyrunners, athletes who compete over steep, treacherous mountain terrain at high altitude.
Earlier this year, she won Argentina's 4 Refugios Non-Stop, covering roughly 40 kilometres and 3,350 metres of elevation gain.

She had also recently tested herself on the Matterhorn. On Aug. 14, McCrystal completed a solo ascent and descent from Zermatt via the Swiss Hörnli Ridge in six hours, 47 minutes and 33 seconds, according to the Fastest Known Time database.
Ten days later, she competed in Italy's Trofeo Kima, one of the international skyrunning circuit's most technically demanding races.
Although the dedicated helicopter operation has been halted, the search is not entirely off.
"We've got the mountain guides that climb that mountain nearly every day," Segor said. "They are looking. If they see something, of course they will tell us."
Rescuers are now awaiting additional information from police that could provide a fresh lead and allow them to resume a more targeted search.
CBC News reached out to Global Affairs Canada; a spokesperson said the agency would respond as soon as it could.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Megan Williams has been covering all things Italian, from politics and the Vatican, to food and culture, to the plight of migrants in the Mediterranean, for more than two decades. Based in Rome, Megan has also told stories from other parts of Europe and the world and won many international prizes for her reporting, including a James Beard Award. Her radio documentaries can be heard on Ideas and The Current. Megan is also a regular guest host on CBC national radio shows.

articles.title: Mining firm pushes to halt Kalinga copper-gold project sale
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A mining firm said it is pushing for legal remedies to stop the planned auction of 40 percent of its Copper-Gold Project in Kalinga on Sept. 8 amid an ongoing legal dispute. The…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A mining firm said it is pushing for legal remedies to stop the planned auction of 40 percent of its Copper-Gold Project in Kalinga on Sept. 8 amid an ongoing legal dispute.
The Celsius Resources Limited, a mining exploration company in the country, said it intends to file a motion for reconsideration by the end of the week to halt the scheduled sale.
This came after a Regional Trial Court in Makati denied its petition to seek interim protection to prevent the foreclosure or disposition of the Makilala Mining Company Inc. (MMCI) interests.
The MMCI holds the stakes associated with the Maalinao-Caigutan-Biyog Copper-Gold Project in Kalinga.

The court found the petition of Makilala Holding Limited (MHL), subsidiary of Celsius, insufficient in establishing “irreparable injury,” as the potential loss from the foreclosure was merely economic and can still be addressed through arbitration.

However, according to Celsius, the Makati court expressed “that its ruling was not a determination that an Event of Default occurred, that any alleged default was incurable, or that Equinaire is entitled to foreclose.”

Moreover, the court added that it “recognized that the interpretation of the OLSA (Omnibus Loan and Security Agreement), the alleged defaults and Equinaire’s enforcement rights remain open for determination by an arbitral tribunal.”
Celsius stressed that if the motion for reconsideration is denied, the MHL will appeal to the Court of Appeals.

The dispute centered between Celsius and Equinaire Holdings Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of an Indian chemical manufacturing company, over a disputed loan and security agreement heading toward arbitration.

“Equinaire has cited several alleged defaults, including the Notice of Relinquishment issued by Makilala Holding Limited to Sodor Inc., certain information-security incidents involving MMCI, and MHL’s efforts to obtain a Temporary Order of Protection from the Makati court,” Celsius said.
The conflict further escalated after Celsius’ temporary order of protection previously granted by the Makati court was lifted upon Equinaire’s payment of a P201-million counterbond.
According to Celsius, it is also revising its notice of arbitration to fully determine the merits of the dispute, as well as the “validity of the alleged defaults and Equinaire’s enforcement rights”.

The mining company, moreover, said that even if the auction pushes through, it would still pursue other legal action during the period of its tax-clearance process, which “takes at least 27 working days, or approximately six to eight weeks”.
“For the Philippine mining sector, the dispute places renewed attention on the ownership and financing arrangements surrounding MMCI,” Celsius said. /cb

articles.title: Can Vice President Sara Duterte be arrested?
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — On Friday, Sept. 4, a warrant of arrest was issued against Vice President Sara Duterte. But can the second-highest elected official of the land be arrested? In a phone interview…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — On Friday, Sept. 4, a warrant of arrest was issued against Vice President Sara Duterte.
But can the second-highest elected official of the land be arrested?

In a phone interview with the INQUIRER, University of the Philippines College of Law Assistant Dean and Professor of Constitutional Law Paolo Emmanuel Tamase said there is nothing in the Constitution that exempts the Vice President from being sued.
“There’s no basis in Philippine constitutional law for the immunity of a Vice President from any type of suit, including a criminal suit,” he said.
Unlike the President, who enjoys immunity from suit while in office, the Vice President does not have the same protection.
Tamase explained that the immunity is based on the need to allow the President to function as the country’s sole executive without facing multiple legal challenges during the term.
That rationale, according to the Law professor, does not apply to the Vice President, who is “constitutionally a spare tire.”
Duterte’s arrest, mugshot, and bail
As for Duterte’s actual arrest, Tamase said this remains significant given Duterte’s position as the country’s second-highest elected official.
“There is no other point in the entire Philippine history. This is the highest public officer who is currently sitting who has been subject to a criminal prosecution and arrest,” he said.
“So, that itself is dramatic. But on the whole, the bail process is actually quite dry and run of the mill.”
Tamase said the process may be “less dramatic” than what the public has seen in other high-profile cases, because her case is bailable.

Under current criminal procedure, the accused does not necessarily have to be physically present when posting bail, as another person may do so on her behalf as long as the other requirements are met, he explained.
According to Tamase, these may include an affidavit of residency, a barangay certification showing where she lives, and the bond required by the court.
As for Duterte’s mugshot, Tamase said Duterte would still have one.
“Those mugshots, she will take herself. She will just attach them to her application for bail when she posts,” he said.
Impeachability vs immunity
Tamase also pointed to what he described as a confusion between being impeachable and being immune from suit.

“Impeachability only relates to the mode of removing a public officer whereas a criminal case doesn’t seek to remove a public officer but only hold her accountable for violating criminal acts,” he said.
He also warned that extending presidential immunity to all impeachable officials would create a large gap in accountability.

“If that argument were to be respected or to be given weight, you would have… at least 30 officers who are impeachable and therefore cannot be sued,” he said. “Which is absurd because it creates a huge gap in accountability among public officers in the Philippines.”

The arrest warrant against Duterte was issued after the court found probable cause to hold her for trial on all three counts of grave threats. Bail was set at P120,000 for each count, or a total of P360,000.

The case stemmed from Duterte’s statement during an online press conference on Nov. 23, 2024, when she said she had arranged an assassination plot with a hitman to target President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., first lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez.
The same alleged threats also form part of the Articles of Impeachment against Duterte, whose trial is currently ongoing.
Effect on impeachment trial

While the criminal case and Duterte’s impeachment trial are separate proceedings and do not affect one another, Tamase said the arrest warrant could affect public perception of the ongoing impeachment proceedings.

Asked whether it will have an impact on how the public may view the ongoing impeachment proceedings, Tamase said, “My sense is it is likely to have an impact, but the direction is not sure, is not certain.”
On one hand, the criminal prosecution could be viewed as confirmation that Duterte’s statements during a November 2024 press conference constituted grave threats, he said.
“It seems to confirm on multiple fronts the fact that there was a crime committed and therefore supports the grounds for impeachment against her,” Tamase explained.
But he also pointed out that the development could also strengthen the narrative among Duterte’s supporters that the legal system is being weaponized against her.
“My own sense is that it’s important to hold all public officers accountable, but if trust in government is low, then you can’t help people that suspect whether there are ulterior motives,” he said.
Public trust, independent institutions
Asked whether the case may still possibly be viewed as being pursued on legitimate grounds, Tamase said the public should look to the strength and independence of institutions handling the case.

He said the Department of Justice, although under the executive branch, has “historically operated with functional independence from the President,” particularly in prosecutors’ evaluation of whether criminal cases should proceed.
“It’s also important for people to have faith in the courts,” Tamase said.
While court cases are not always easily accessible, he said monitoring by the media and academe may help ensure that the process is conducted fairly.
“Over and above the strength of institutions, it’s important for the process to be a little more transparent to the public,” he reiterated. /cb

articles.title: Prosecution drops Madriaga, Lachica, Nolasco as witnesses in impeachment trial
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel said Friday it would no longer present Ramil Madriaga, Col. Raymund Lachica, and Col. Dennis Nolasco as witnesses in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

blocks.text: Published September 5, 2026 12:03am
The House prosecution panel said Friday it would no longer present Ramil Madriaga, Col. Raymund Lachica, and Col. Dennis Nolasco as witnesses in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

“We won’t present Lachica. It is not necessary because the previous witnesses’ testimony already substantiates our allegations,” prosecution panel adviser Robert Ace Barbers said in an online press conference.
Manila Rep. Benny Abante agreed, saying fielding more witnesses who are not employees of the OVP would be an “overkill.”
“We have more than enough with Ms. Gina Acosta’s testimony. Can you imagine the Vice President ordering the transfer of P125 million every quarter to one person, who is Lachica?" Abante said.

Lachica and Nolasco served as chief and deputy chief of the Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group, respectively. They allegedly disbursed the confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President and the Department of Education, then concurrently headed by Duterte.

According to a separate "24 Oras" report by Tina Panganiban-Perez, Madriaga, Duterte's alleged bagman, faced a House investigation where he bared that in 2022, he delivered millions of pesos to different persons on the Vice President's orders.
Lachina, Nolasco and Madriaga were among the witnesses in the list of the prosecution to be presented during the trial.

"With the witnesses that the prosecution panel has presented, we have already proven that, and it's now in the hands of our senator-judges to weigh the witnesses and evidence we have presented, so there is no need for these additional witnesses - Col. Nolasco, Col. Lachica and Madriaga," Barbers said.
Abante said it is now time to call Duterte, who is the impeachable official.
"Let's subpoena the Vice President...let's go to the jugular," Abante said.
But House impeachment prosecutor Jeol Chua said, "We have the option to call her, but we can't force her."
House prosecution panel head Gerville Luistro said the list of witnesses in the remaining articles are being "reevaluated."
The panel aims to conclude the presentation of witnesses for the article of impeachment on the use of confidential funds on September 9. —Llanesca Panti/LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Canadian 'banking' company linked to sanctioned money-laundering network
articles.summary: CBC’s visual investigations team and the Centre for Information Resilience reveals who is behind a Canadian 'revolutionary banking' company with ties to a sanctioned money-laundering network serving…

image.caption: Latvians Andrejs Carenoks and Janis Zvigulis are behind a B.C. company linked to a Russian money-laundering operation. Carenoks was sanctioned in 2024 by the U.S. for his role in the TGR network. (Illustration: Froilan Untalasco/CBC, LinkedIn, Instagram, Maple Finance, CBC)

blocks.text: Maple Digital Financial Solutions describes itself as a "revolutionary banking" company, with an address in a skyscraper in the heart of Vancouver's financial district.
On paper, the company is registered with Canada’s financial intelligence agency, and offers "fast and easy" global currency transfers and "convenient banking" with the click of a button.
In practice, however, it’s a shell company. Its website offers no option to open an account and provides no employee names, while phone calls go straight to voicemail and emails go unanswered.

A CBC News visual investigation, in collaboration with the Centre for Information Resilience (CIR), reveals this shell company is closely linked to the TGR network, accused by international law enforcement of laundering billions of dollars for ransomware gangs, drug cartels and wealthy Russians.

"Red lights are flashing, there are a number of red flags here," said Denis Meunier, former deputy director at the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), who reviewed the findings.
A report by CIR, a U.K.-based research organization, used digital clues to connect Maple Digital Financial Solutions with a series of companies called The OneGate and the TGR network.

CBC shared its findings with multiple legal and financial experts, and each had a similar takeaway: Maple Digital Financial Solutions, also known as Maple Finance, is at "high risk" for suspicious activity.

Unlike traditional banks, money services businesses (MSB) such as Maple Finance already pose a threat of laundering illicit funds due to a lack of transparency and the fact that they don’t require an operating licence in many provinces.
This, coupled with ties to a sanctioned network and individuals known for money laundering, should put authorities in Canada on alert, said Meunier.
TGR network: transnational money-laundering

The CIR report and the experts CBC News spoke to acknowledge there's no definitive proof of money laundering. But there are substantial digital clues that connect Maple to TGR — primarily Andrejs Carenoks, a Latvian sanctioned by the U.S. in 2024 for his role in a sophisticated money-laundering operation allegedly led by Yury Maksakov, a Ukrainian national born in Russia.
Carenoks, according to corporate records, was a director at Maple Finance in 2021.
The current director is Janis Zvigulis. He is also director of The OneGate and a registered director of TGR Wealth Solutions in the U.K., which was sanctioned in 2024.
Zvigulis has not been sanctioned.

Authorities in the U.S. and U.K. described TGR as a full-service shadow financial hub, offering unregistered crypto exchanges, prepaid credit cards and sanctions evasion services, helping cybercriminals and drug traffickers.

For example, if a Russian cybercrime group held $1 million US in cryptocurrency paid by the victim of a ransomware attack and a drug gang in the U.K. had a similar amount in cash that needed to be laundered, TGR would arrange for the U.K. drug gang to be paid in crypto in exchange for their cash. The cash would then be laundered through a network of international business accounts.
Investigators at the U.K.’s National Crime Agency (NCA) have seen similar exchanges where cash handovers were followed almost immediately by the movement of a similar denomination of crypto.
Both Carenoks and Maksakov are accused of playing major roles in the TGR network, according to authorities in the U.K. and U.S.

"TGR is massive. It's really, really huge," said Elise Thomas, senior open-source investigator at CIR and author of the OneGate report. "To have Carenoks’s name on the actual company documents [for Maple Digital Financial Solutions], I think it's some really strong connections to TGR."
CBC tried reaching out to Maple Finance and The OneGate through email and phone but did not receive a response.
The registered Vancouver address on the Maple Finance website led to Canadian business law firm Osler, Hoskin & Harcourt LLP.

In a call, Osler lawyer and partner Matthew Burgoyne said, "the Law Society code of conduct doesn't let us disclose who our clients are and who they're not. So, unfortunately, I wouldn't even be able to tell you if we acted for them or not."
CBC followed up via email requesting that the lawyer ask Maple Finance for comment on this story. The firm wrote in an email, "we cannot help with your story."

"I think it sort of underscores that this is not a normal business. Because normally, when you call the business, they answer," said Thomas. "And when you try to contact them through the channels that they've given to be contacted by customers, they would respond."
'Silent director'
CBC News reached out to Careneks, Zvigulis and Maksakov but did not receive a response.
Attempts were also made to reach former directors of Maple Digital Financial Solutions.

One of those former directors, Elen Kazarian, is based in Ontario. In an email, she told CBC News she was appointed as a "silent director" because the “owner and CEO of this company are foreigners I was told by my cousin — who knew these owners to help them to register this Corporation."
She said she didn’t do anything during her tenure as a director and wasn't paid.
Maple Digital Financial Solutions is part of a group of companies connected to The OneGate.

The financial network offers products such as virtual and physical payment cards, and services such as cryptocurrency trading through shell companies spread across at least seven jurisdictions, from the U.S. to Switzerland to Hong Kong.

"OneGate seems to be presenting [itself as a] payments service company that provides a number of different financial products and services," Thomas said. "Under the hood, there are all these deep historical connections to TGR, which obviously is accused of being a transnational money-laundering ring."

The TGR network was disrupted in 2024 after a three-year international probe led by the NCA codenamed Operation Destabilise. It was a global effort to dismantle a multibillion-dollar shadow banking and cryptocurrency network that laundered proceeds for violent drug cartels, ransomware gangs and Russian intelligence operations.
It resulted in 128 arrests worldwide and the seizure of more than $44 million Cdn in cash and digital assets.
The OneGate network was operating in parallel to TGR and started with a virtual office in Vancouver when Maple Finance was still called Fexcool Payments.
The CIR report further detailed the digital forensic connections. When it changed its name to Maple Digital Financial Solutions, it registered a website: maplefinance.ca.
Andrejs Carenoks was the one who registered that domain.
At the same time, Carenoks was the director of a TGR entity later sanctioned by the U.S.
The overlap between Maple Finance and TGR went beyond Carenoks. Archived records of that website show that Maple Finance listed a Toronto-area phone number also used by TGR Partners.
Maple Finance provided clients with a branded payment card issued by OneCard — a service in part operated by TGR at the time.
In 2023, Maple Finance became the acting primary legal entity behind The OneGate. Its customer portal was fully merged into the main OneGate domain a short time after.

TGR Partners also actively recruited staff for Maple Finance online, including posting job listings for an IT project manager to work out of TGR's physical office in Podgorica, Montenegro, under a TGR human resources manager.

PDF files created for Maple’s privacy agreements contained metadata listing the author as "Max Travel," a likely digital trace left by TGR leader Yury Maksakov, who uses the username "Max Traveller" on Facebook.

The digital clues and overlaps between Maple Finance and TGR are consistent with "illicit financial activities," said Peter Dent, a former forensic services lead for global professional services firm Deloitte who is also part of the Vancouver Anti-Corruption Institute.

"I'm certainly concerned," said Dent. "They share a common directorship, they share a phone number with another entity that has been alleged to be involved in illicit financial activity. They don't even have a phone number in Canada."
FINTRAC registration
Following the global crackdown on the TGR Network in December 2024, Maple Finance was scrubbed from the active provider list on The OneGate website, as its FINTRAC registration expired.
The FINTRAC registration has since been renewed and Maple Finance now advertises itself as an "innovative financial ecosystem for modern business owners to manage their finances on their own terms."

"If I was the government authority in charge of money-laundering enforcement, like FINTRAC here in Canada, I think I'd be looking at this report," said William Pellerin, international trade lawyer at McMillan LLP, who also reviewed the report and CBC’s findings.
"You have known actors that have been under investigation in other jurisdictions … in conjunction with everything else, maybe this is something we ought to dig into."

articles.title: Lachica, Madriaga out as witnesses
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel has dropped as witnesses two of Vice President Sara Duterte’s former security officers and her alleged former bagman, Ramil Madriaga, saying evidence already…

blocks.text: September 5, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The House prosecution panel has dropped as witnesses two of Vice President Sara Duterte’s former security officers and her alleged former bagman, Ramil Madriaga, saying evidence already presented is sufficient to establish allegations of misuse, misappropriation and irregular liquidation of P612.5 million in confidential funds.

Prosecution adviser and spokesman Ace Barbers said Col. Raymund Dante Lachica and Col. Dennis Nolasco, who have both figured in testimony on the handling of Duterte’s confidential funds in the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and Department of Education (DepEd), will no longer be called to the witness stand.

“For the prosecution panel, with the witnesses presented, we have already proven that. So, there is no need for additional witnesses like Col. Lachica, Col. Nolasco and Madriaga,” Barbers said yesterday in an online press briefing.
Manila Rep. Benny Abante Jr. said presenting Lachica would already be “overkill,” given the testimony of former OVP special disbursing officer (SDO) Gina Acosta.
Acosta testified as a hostile prosecution witness that Duterte instructed her to turn over four P125-million tranches, or a total of P500 million in OVP confidential funds, to Lachica.
She claimed she has no personal knowledge of how the money was distributed after turning it over to him.
Nolasco, meanwhile, was linked to DepEd’s confidential funds through the earlier House testimony of former DepEd SDO Edward Fajarda.

Fajarda testified during House proceedings that he turned over three P37.5-million confidential fund releases, totaling P112.5 million, to Nolasco upon Duterte’s instruction when she was education secretary.
Madriaga had been considered a potentially significant prosecution witness after identifying himself during House impeachment proceedings as Duterte’s former aide and alleged bagman.
Madriaga had claimed that he personally handled and distributed the first P125 million in OVP confidential funds released in December 2022 and disposed of the entire amount in less than 24 hours.

He alleged that he delivered bags containing millions of pesos to several locations upon Duterte’s instruction, and implicated Lachica and Nolasco in the alleged movement of the money. Duterte has denied Madriaga’s allegations.

Despite Madriaga’s earlier inclusion among prospective witnesses, Barbers said the prosecution now believes his testimony, along with those of Lachica and Nolasco, would no longer be necessary given the evidence already on record.
The prosecution will instead proceed with its remaining witnesses as it seeks to complete its presentation of evidence on the confidential fund charge.

The witnesses are Fajarda and his wife, DepEd Assistant Secretary Sunshine Charry Fajarda; Philippine Statistics Authority assistant national statistician Marizza Grande; police Maj. Jovelyn Magay and Commission on Audit official Bresilio Sabaldan.
The Senate impeachment court has issued subpoenas for the five to appear as prosecution witnesses in the Sept. 7 to 9 trial proceedings.

The prosecution, however, said it could also dispense with Edward Fajarda’s personal appearance if the prosecution and defense agree to stipulate on the matters his testimony is intended to establish.
Voting threshold

Several senator-judges yesterday denied or remained tight-lipped about formal discussions to lower the 16-vote conviction threshold in the Duterte impeachment trial, following the disclosure of Majority Leader Juan Miguel Zubiri of discussions regarding the matter.
Sen. JV Ejercito clarified that the issue was not formally tackled during their recent all-senator caucus, noting that their meeting was strictly confined to the trial’s schedule.
Senators Panfilo Lacson and Raffy Tulfo echoed Ejercito’s remarks.
Their statements came after Zubiri announced on Thursday that the threshold issue had been raised by some members during a Wednesday caucus.

The Senate is currently operating with only 20 active members, as Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta are currently detained on plunder charges, Sen. Ronald dela Rosa is a fugitive evading an International Criminal Court warrant and Sen. Loren Legarda is abroad on an extended medical leave.

Ejercito deferred to Zubiri regarding the sentiment of the chamber, but suggested that altering the threshold might be a constitutional question best resolved by the Supreme Court. — Neil Jayson Servallos

articles.title: PCG: Chinese ship monitored in Panatag for weeks
articles.summary: While the Philippines was busy grappling with heavy monsoon rains and flooding, a Chinese survey vessel illegally operated within Panatag or Scarborough Shoal, the Philippine Coast Guard said…

blocks.text: September 5, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — While the Philippines was busy grappling with heavy monsoon rains and flooding, a Chinese survey vessel illegally operated within Panatag or Scarborough Shoal, the Philippine Coast Guard said yesterday.

“For 25 days, the 76-meter Chinese survey vessel Haiyang Dizhi Shihao has been operating inside our exclusive economic zone – three weeks of it inside the 12 nautical miles territorial sea of Bajo de Masinloc,” PCG spokesman for the West Philippine Sea Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela reported, referring to Panatag.
Tarriela said this was spotted with the help of Canada’s Dark Vessel Detection program. He noted that the ship switched off its automatic identification system to avoid detection at sea.
The research vessel, operated by the Guangzhou Marine Geological Survey, is equipped for deep-sea drilling and drilled 302.07 meters beneath the seafloor in 2023, Tarriela said.
“This is the same vessel that spent seven weeks surveying inside Indonesia’s EEZ in the North Natuna Sea in 2021,” he added.
The ship was escorted by the China Coast Guard before it withdrew from the waters ahead of the ASEAN summit, he added.
Tarriela also flagged the timing of the vessel deployment, as it operated when the Philippines was dealing with severe weather conditions.

“While the Philippines has been battered by typhoons and the monsoon these past weeks, China moved its survey vessel in at precisely the moment our vessels were least able to intercept it,” the PCG spokesman said.
According to Tarriela, the Department of Foreign Affairs confirmed that there was no permit for the vessel to conduct its marine scientific research.
Meanwhile, the Department of National Defense denounced yesterday China’s latest efforts to sow disinformation and again claim that Batanes is part of China.
In a statement, DND spokesman Arsenio Andolong said Batanes is not and has never been part of Chinese territory.
China, through its so-called academic scholars, first claimed two months ago that Batanes belongs to China by way of Taiwan.
Through an opinion piece published by state-run Global Times on Thursday, the argument was repeated.

Relatedly, Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro Jr. met with retired Supreme Court justice Antonio Carpio and retired Philippine Navy rear admiral Rommel Jude Ong yesterday for a discussion on the Law of the Sea and the assertion of Philippine maritime rights.

articles.title: Duterte camp seeks stricter ICC rules for digital evidence
articles.summary: Citing the proliferation of misinformation online, the defense team of former president Rodrigo Duterte has asked the International Criminal Court (ICC) to adopt stricter protocols for verifying…

blocks.text: September 5, 2026 | 12:00am
Undated photo shows facade of the International Criminal Court in the Hague, Netherlands.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — Citing the proliferation of misinformation online, the defense team of former president Rodrigo Duterte has asked the International Criminal Court (ICC) to adopt stricter protocols for verifying digital materials.
In a 12-page request dated Aug. 31 and released on Friday, defense lawyer Peter Haynes asked ICC Trial Chamber III to amend its e-Court Protocol to include an “expert verification” field.
The defense said a URL (uniform resource locator), or the web address where a material is found, is insufficient to establish its authenticity or reliability.
“The URL merely records the web location from which a piece of online content was collected; it cannot indicate its source,” the filing read.
Haynes added that extra caution is necessary to ensure evidence is properly verified before being submitted to the court.
“The current case operates in a uniquely challenging information ecosystem, in which a large volume of misinformation or ‘fake news’ has circulated, and will continue to circulate, online,” he wrote.
The proposed “expert verification” field would indicate whether an item submitted as evidence would be accompanied by an expert report.
It would also operate similarly to witness fields in the E-Court Protocol, which list metadata to be provided throughout the trial.

According to the defense, an expert report should detail the source of the material, its chain of custody, whether it is an original or copy, its metadata and other technical aspects. It should also identify steps taken to verify the material and determine whether it had been edited or manipulated.
The report should further include the qualifications and experience of the person who conducted the verification and the methodology used.
“Without this information, it would be very difficult for the Chamber to come to a view on the evidence’s relevance and admissibility,” Haynes said.
The prosecution has yet to comment on the request.
Duterte’s trial is expected to begin on Nov. 30.

articles.title: NBI to file trafficking raps vs Leviste, 6 others
articles.summary: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is set to file qualified human trafficking charges against Batangas 1st District Rep. Leandro Leviste, former lawmaker Jacinto Paras and five others over an…

blocks.text: September 5, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is set to file qualified human trafficking charges against Batangas 1st District Rep. Leandro Leviste, former lawmaker Jacinto Paras and five others over an alleged honey trap plot targeting Executive Secretary Ralph Recto.
NBI Director Melvin Matibag said yesterday that the complaint would be filed with the Department of Justice after the bureau’s investigation found elements of qualified human trafficking.
“We are filing a violation of the Anti-Human Trafficking Law, so qualified human trafficking is what we will file against the seven individuals,” Matibag told reporters in a chance interview.
“Our findings indicate that they supposedly committed qualified human trafficking. All the elements are present,” he added.

The investigation stemmed from an entrapment operation at a hotel in Malate, Manila on July 28, where NBI agents rescued five people allegedly recruited as part of a plan to fabricate a story and affidavit linking Recto to a scandal in exchange for payment.
The NBI earlier subpoenaed Leviste, Paras and four lawyers in connection with the case.
Leviste’s camp has denied involvement in the alleged scheme.

Paras’ lawyers, Mark Tolentino and Ferdinand Topacio, also denied the accusations, saying their client did not recruit or hire the women allegedly involved. They said the women had voluntarily approached Paras to offer statements about an incident in 2025.
Tolentino and Topacio appeared before the NBI-National Capital Region in Pasay and submitted a notarized affidavit denying allegations against Paras.
Leviste had earlier left the country for France with his mother, Sen. Loren Legarda, before the NBI served him the subpoena, according to Matibag.
The NBI is confident with the qualified human trafficking complaint that it filed against Leviste, Paras and others.
Leviste, however, said the NBI, which he called the National Bureau of Imbento, is only “making up allegations.”

“Nag-iimbento ng kalokohan gamit ang buwis habang lubog ang bayan. Nakakaawa ang nangyayari sa ating bansa,” he said in a Facebook post, accusing the NBI of inventing foolishness while the country is in bad shape.
Speaking to “Storycon” on One News, Matibag said they have enough evidence to secure a conviction against the respondents.

“We have complete evidence here. We have testimonial and documentary evidence, CCTV footage and even the accused’s own pronouncements,” he said. “Qualified human trafficking is a non-bailable offense.”

The DOJ will still have to conduct a preliminary investigation into the complaint. During this phase, the respondents will be given the opportunity to address the allegations. A warrant will only be issued once the case is filed in court.
Matibag said they also intend to file a disbarment case next week. He did not provide details, but said this is in relation to the qualified human trafficking complaint.
Several lawyers were previously tagged as involved in the alleged scheme.
Meanwhile, the NBI director also confirmed that another high-profile case would be filed before the DOJ next week.
He did not provide details, but said it involves a national government official. — Janvic Mateo, Daphne Galvez

articles.title: MMDA sends flood barriers, mobile pumps to NLEX
articles.summary: The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority is continuing to help ease flooding in San Simon, Pampanga along the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) by deploying mobile pumps and L-shaped barriers,…

blocks.text: September 5, 2026 | 12:00am
Residents of San Simon, Pampanga wade through floodwaters as intermittent rain continues in the area.
Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority is continuing to help ease flooding in San Simon, Pampanga along the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) by deploying mobile pumps and L-shaped barriers, according to MMDA Chairman Don Artes.
The deployment since Aug. 31 was made to address the gridlock along NLEX caused by impassable sections due to floodwaters.

“We also have mobile pumping stations dispatched. Our mobile trucks have a capacity to pump one cubic meter per second from the roads,” MMDA general manager Nicolas Torre III said yesterday at a press conference.
The barriers, along with sandbags, were placed in critical sections of NLEX San Simon to control the flood from spilling over wider sections of the thoroughfare, MMDA explained.
NLEX personnel also deployed rapid flood barriers to contain the floodwater at the interchange.
Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon said that the heavy downpour from the enhanced monsoon led to the flooding, which in turn resulted in the massive traffic jam.
The sandbags and plastic barriers scattered at the NLEX San Simon exit were not swept by floodwater, the NLEX Corp. clarified yesterday.

“The said materials were on standby. Those were excess materials from the first phase on the flood-mitigating works. The said materials were not left as after-works mess and are still being used in the ongoing flood-mitigating works in the area,” the tollway company told The STAR.
A report said the barriers and sandbags were seen scattered and displaced as motorists navigated the flooded section of the expressway.

The tollway company said that as of 1:05 p.m. yesterday, Lane 1 and 2 in Tulaoc, San Simon portion of the expressway were passable to all types of vehicles while Lane 3 was not passable. Traffic was light.

At the San Simon Interchange, Lane 1 was passable to all types of vehicles and Lane 2 was passable only to Class 2 and 3 vehicles and Lane 3 was not passable. It also has approximately one kilometer of traffic build-up.
Blocked waterways
In Bulacan, the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (PDRRMO) has initially identified five areas in the province that are being affected by floodwater due to blocked waterways.

During a coordination meeting with the governor on Thursday, PDRRMO head Manuel Lukban Jr. reported that the flooding in Barangays Longos and Bulihan in Malolos, Malis in Guiguinto, Panginay in Balagtas, Masuso in Pandi and Saluysoy in Meycauayan were caused by the obstruction of natural waterways caused by trees and vegetation; encroachment of informal settlers; heavily silted rivers and creeks; improper garbage disposal and obstructed, damaged or low-positioned culverts.
Other factors that led to blocked waterways were the absence or gaps in existing dikes and river walls, inadequate or sub-standard water pumps, narrow floodways and unmaintained floodgates.

The Bulacan PDRRMO is set to conduct a series of studies and assessments in other flood-prone barangays to determine their specific causes of flooding and identify the appropriate mitigation measures. — Ramon Efren Lazaro

articles.title: Ombudsman urged:Substantiate Allegations vs CA
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has urged Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla or any concerned party to substantiate allegations of partiality, misconduct and corruption against the Court of Appeals (CA), saying it…

blocks.text: September 5, 2026 | 12:00am
An undated photo of the Ombudsman office.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Supreme Court has urged Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla or any concerned party to substantiate allegations of partiality, misconduct and corruption against the Court of Appeals (CA), saying it can only act on such accusations through proper complaints and supporting evidence.
SC spokesperson Camille Ting said the high court takes such allegations seriously, but cannot act on “broad allegations against an entire appellate court based on public statements.”
She urged Remulla or any concerned party to file the proper complaint and submit supporting evidence, giving the judges or justices concerned an opportunity to respond.
“This will allow the Court to determine the facts and, when warranted, exercise its disciplinary authority,” Ting said in a statement.
The SC issued the statement after Remulla urged the judiciary to undergo “soul-searching” over an alleged “trend” of ombudsman decisions being reversed by the CA.

During a Senate finance committee hearing on the ombudsman’s proposed 2027 budget, Remulla said he had raised his concerns with Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen over cases in which ombudsman decisions were reversed by the CA.
He described the reversals as a “problem” that only discourages the ombudsman’s office to “conduct all these activities only to be reversed by the CA decision that came out of nowhere.”
Remulla said the judiciary “has to be examined closely by everybody in government.”

The SC said it welcomes fair criticism of the judiciary and its decisions, but stressed that serious accusations against judges and courts should be raised through proper processes so these can be fairly investigated and resolved.
The Integrated Bar of the Philippines echoed the SC’s call, saying allegations of corruption against the courts need to be substantiated.

IBP national president Allan Panolong said the organization condemns corruption in all government institutions, particularly in the judiciary, but agreed with the SC that serious allegations should be pursued through proper channels.

articles.title: P4-P5/liter oil price hike seen next week
articles.summary: After recent price cuts, domestic oil firms are expected to raise pump prices by up to P5 per liter next week amid fears of further supply disruptions in the Middle East.

blocks.text: September 5, 2026 | 12:00am

Industry estimates point to a potential price hike of P4.50 to P5 per liter for diesel and P4 to P4.50 per liter for gasoline, based on four-day movements in the Mean of Platts Singapore and foreign exchange rates.
The STAR / Miguel de Guzman
MANILA, Philippines — After recent price cuts, domestic oil firms are expected to raise pump prices by up to P5 per liter next week amid fears of further supply disruptions in the Middle East.

Jetti Petroleum president Leo Bellas said prices rose following the resumption of hostilities between the United States and Iran over mining in the Strait of Hormuz, a key trade route for oil and gas shipments.
The renewed tensions have heightened concerns over more disruptions to energy flows from the Middle East, where the Philippines has historically sourced the majority of its crude oil supplies.

“The US strike on Larak, Iran’s missile response against US interests in the Middle East and US President Trump’s renewed threats against Kharg Island have created renewed risk of escalation in the region after more than a month of relative calm,” Bellas said.

Global diesel markets stay on edge amid refinery disruptions around the world, which further squeeze already-tight inventories. At the same time, weaker flows through the Strait of Hormuz exerted upward pressure on prices.
“Gasoline fundamentals remain firm, supported by low inventories and resilient demand and the uncertainty over supply security continues to support Asian gasoline prices,” Bellas said.
The final adjustments, which are expected to be announced on Monday, will still depend on the outcome of the last trading day.
Last Tuesday, fuel retailers rolled back gasoline prices by around P0.30 per liter, while the cost of diesel and kerosene declined by nearly P4 per liter.

articles.title: DA: P20/kilo rice market price now out of reach
articles.summary: The P20-per-kilo market price for rice promised by President Marcos during his 2022 campaign is now out of reach as rising fertilizer, transport and fuel costs continue to drive up rice production…

blocks.text: September 5, 2026 | 12:00am
DA Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. said Thursday that government subsidies would be needed to make rice at P20 a kilo available.

MANILA, Philippines — The P20-per-kilo market price for rice promised by President Marcos during his 2022 campaign is now out of reach as rising fertilizer, transport and fuel costs continue to drive up rice production expenses, according to the Department of Agriculture.
“We really can’t reach P20 per kilo for rice, we will have to subsidize it,” Tiu Laurel said over One News’ “Storycon.”
He said urea prices, which were around P700 per sack when Marcos made the promise, have risen to almost P2,600.

“In today’s global situation, I don’t really think so because everything has gone up,” Tiu Laurel said. “Now, it’s almost P2,600, so it’s the fertilizer that’s actually the problem, and we cannot control it.”

Urea prices had reached as high as P3,000 per 50-kilogram bag before Marcos took office in June 2022 amid the Russia-Ukraine war. Fertilizer prices have since risen again due to the Middle East crisis.
The price of locally produced regular-milled rice averaged P44.94 per kilo from Aug. 24 to 30, based on DA data. Well-milled rice averaged P47.73 per kilo while premium rice averaged P52.76 per kilo.

Tiu Laurel said Marcos is aware that rice market prices are unlikely to reach P20 per kilo. The Marcos administration has instead implemented the subsidized “Benteng Bigas, Meron Na!” program through Kadiwa outlets.
The DA said 800 outlets nationwide were participating, with more than 12 million Filipinos benefiting as of July.
The agency distributes 10,000 to 20,000 metric tons of P20 rice monthly, with the volume expected to reach 40,000 metric tons by the end of the year.
He said the program uses the P9 billion allocated to the National Food Authority (NFA) to procure rice from local farmers, along with funds specifically set aside for the program.
The subsidy program is scheduled to run until June 30, 2028.
Tiu Laurel said the country is not facing a rice supply shortage.
Of the 75,000 hectares of farmland affected by the southwest monsoon, about 67,000 hectares were planted with rice.
Tiu Laurel assured the public that the government had frontloaded sufficient rice stocks in NFA warehouses and expects to replenish them by the end of the year.
He said the government would import rice after the harvest season to prepare for the expected severe El Niño.
The DA expects El Niño to reduce local rice production by about 700,000 metric tons. — Adrian Kenneth Halili

articles.title: Russia hits Ukrainian security headquarters in drone attack, Zelensky says
articles.summary: The unmanned aerial vehicle struck without warning in the heart of the Ukrainian capital.

blocks.text: Russia hits Ukrainian security headquarters in drone attack, Zelensky says
Image source, Reuters
A Russian drone has hit the headquarters of the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) during a strike in the heart of Kyiv, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
The unmanned aerial vehicle crashed into the SBU headquarters on Friday afternoon, targeting a room used by security chief Oleksandr Poklad.
It is not clear whether Poklad was in the building, but Zelensky said he had since spoken to him to order an "appropriate, tangible response".

"The drone was aimed directly at the office of the Head of the Security Service in that building," Zelensky confirmed. It suggests Russia's new drones are growing in accuracy and signals Moscow could step up strikes before possible US mediation talks this weekend.
"All emergency services are on the scene. Everyone affected will receive the necessary assistance," Zelensky added in a message on Telegram.

"I instructed Poklad to deliver an appropriate, tangible response and, where possible, one that mirrors this strike, to the Russians once everything is ready. Our military will support this response."
Images of the office widely shared online showed black smoke pouring from two windows on the front of the building.
Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha said the attack was a "major escalation that demands resolute responses".
"Moscow launched this strike during a renewed push for peace - laying bare its true rejection of diplomacy," he added.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said five people had been hurt in the SBU attack, but did not elaborate on whether they were inside the offices.
The Russian defence ministry also said on Friday it had struck a cargo vessel in the Ukrainian port of Chornomorsk and a tanker near Odesa.
In recent weeks Russia has escalated its daytime strikes on Ukrainian targets.
In many instances it has employed jet-powered drones which are faster and harder to intercept. It is not yet known which type of munition was used in this latest attack.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Firefighters work to put out fires in the building following the Russian drone strike

blocks.text: Firefighters work to put out fires in the building following the Russian drone strike
The strike on the SBU building is a rare example of Russia successfully hitting a government building.
Previously Ukrainian offices have remained unscathed despite attempts from the Kremlin to stifle defences to its advances.
The SBU - which is just over the road from the St Sophia cathedral, the oldest building in Kyiv - is a key part of Ukraine's war efforts as it conducts deep strikes to damage Russian infrastructure.
The drone came during yet another air raid alert. There was a brief whine before an explosion echoed across the roof tops and smoke rose into the sky.
Despite the ongoing exchanges, US mediators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will visit Russia and Ukraine this weekend, reports say, as efforts to end the war continue.
The envoys will meet Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday in Moscow, and then will hold talks with Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky on Sunday in Kyiv, Axios said, citing US officials.
Witkoff and Kushner have led US President Donald Trump's efforts to broker a peace deal, without a breakthrough so far.

articles.title: Russia strikes Ukraine intelligence HQ in ‘major escalation’
articles.summary:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy says he has told SBU to deliver ‘appropriate, tangible response’ to Kyiv strike

The head office of Ukraine’s SBU intelligence agency has been hit in a Russian drone…

blocks.text: The head office of Ukraine’s SBU intelligence agency has been hit in a Russian drone attack, sending plumes of black smoke rising into the air in the heart of Kyiv.

Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said he had instructed the SBU to deliver an “appropriate, tangible response” to the strike, while the foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, described it as a “major escalation”.
The streets around the SBU headquarters were cordoned off shortly after Friday’s attack, with armed officers patrolling the area.
Numerous ambulances and emergency services vehicles were stationed around the site, which is close to St Sophia Cathedral, a Unesco world heritage site.

“Unfortunately, a Russian drone hit the central building of the SBU on Volodymyrska Street in Kyiv, opposite the St Sophia Cathedral,” Zelenskyy said in a post on Telegram. “The drone was aimed directly at the office of the Head of the Security Service in that building.”
Kyiv has been under a barrage of daily drone and missile attacks from Russia for over a week.

The country is facing a critical shortage of US-made Patriot interceptors which can shoot down incoming threats. Many of the recent Russian strikes have been by new-model jet-powered drones which can reach speeds of 250mph, making them hard to intercept.

It is rare for government buildings in central Kyiv to be reached by Russian strikes, especially in broad daylight. The explosion from the hit on the SBU building could be heard from several blocks away.

The incident is likely to intensify the escalating attacks that Moscow and Kyiv have been launching at each other in recent weeks in efforts to destroy each other’s resilience and morale. It will also raise questions about Kyiv’s ability to defend its key infrastructure against Russia.
Sybiha said the attack was “a major escalation that demands resolute responses” and called on international partners to “unequivocally condemn these actions and step up pressure on the Putin regime”.
At least nine people were injured in Friday’s strike, according to Kyiv’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko.
Stanislav Zavertailo, the co-owner of the nearby Zavertailo cafe, said one of his customers was injured in the strike, which sent shockwaves through his premises, shattering all the windows.
“It’s a normal cafe,” he said. The customer was “eating one of our famous poppy seed rolls” when the attack occurred, he added.

Staff and customers rushed into an underground shelter after the strike, fearing a double-tap attack, a tactic which Russia has employed, in which a second drone is sent in soon after the first, hitting emergency service workers.
An hour later, there had been no second strike, but Zavertailo said he did not feel at ease. “We are all waiting for another attack,” he said.
The SBU is responsible for coordinating complex operations against Russia, including last year’s Operation Spiderweb which destroyed aircraft worth billions of pounds inside Russia.
Friday’s hit was “awful” said a Zavertailo cafe employee who had recently emerged from the underground shelter. As “a person who lives in Ukraine for all this time, it’s just hard”.
The strike came two days before Donald Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner were expected to visit Kyiv for the first time.
US-led diplomatic efforts to end Russia’s four-and-a-half-year invasion have stalled in recent months as the US has shifted its focus towards the war with Iran.
Additional reporting by Illia Dyadik

articles.title: Nigeria: Suspected oil thieves dead after inhaling fumes
articles.summary: A Nigerian environmental group says that at least 37 people died trying to siphon crude oil off a ship illegally. Police acknowledged a fatal incident but gave fewer details, saying investigations…

image.caption: Ships often dock to load and discharge produce at refineries in oil-rich Nigeria, in thie case at the Dangote refinery in Lagos in April 2026Image: Sodiq Adelakun/REUTERS

blocks.text: A Nigerian environmental NGO says that at least 37 people died in an attempt to tap oil from a loading vessel in the south of the country illegally.
Most of them died as a result of inhaling hazardous fumes, the Youth and Advocacy Centre said.
Nigerian authorities were yet to issue a death toll but had acknowledged a fatal incident in which people were killed, apparently while trying to steal crude oil.
What do we know about the case?
The incident took place overnight on Thursday in Okrika in Rivers State in the oil-rich Niger Delta in the south of the country.

The environmental group said it happened at a jetty as a vessel was loading oil from the Indorama Eleme Petrochemical through the Port Harcourt Refinery. The people who died were "suspected oil thieves" trying to siphon the commodity off into boats at an "illegal tapping point."
The Youth and Advocacy Centre NGO said that other people were still missing, potentially lost in the water, quoting a network of volunteers.
Police acknowledged an incident but said they continued to investigate the details.
"The Rivers State Police Command can confirm the deaths. The victims were allegedly attempting to steal crude oil," said spokesperson Blessing Agbabe.
Africa's fuel crisis: Is Dangote the answer?
Oil theft is fairly common in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria, Africa's biggest oil producer, with oil mining areas hotspots for poverty and environmental degradation.
The Nigerian government estimates that oil theft causes losses worth several billion dollars annually and has been trying to clamp down on the practice.
The tapping process can also cause leaks and environmental damage.
If confirmed this would be the worst fatal accident on record connected to attempted oil theft since at least October 2023.
However the Nigeria Security and Civil Defense Corps said that the casualty figures circulating remained unverified, saying it was working with other security agencies to clarify the details.

articles.title: Germany urges EU to cut Russians’ holiday visas after sabotage attacks
articles.summary: Belarusian said to have had tourist visa issued by Italy is investigated over alleged attempt to attack Leipzig airport
articles.byline: Kate Connolly in Berlin, Lorenzo Tondo and Pjotr Sauer

blocks.text: Germany is urging its European partners to introduce tighter limitations on Russian citizens entering the EU on tourist visas, after recent sabotage attacks which Berlin has blamed on Moscow.
German authorities are investigating a Belarusian national, who also holds a Russian passport, over the alleged attempt to attack Leipzig airport using drones and explosives.

The man is alleged to have entered the Schengen area on a tourist visa issued by the Italian embassy in Minsk, the capital of Belarus. Security sources said he did not appear to have ever travelled through Italy.
Germany’s foreign ministry has complained that too many visas were being issued to Russians.
“The number of visas issued for Russian nationals for holidays in the European Union is too high,” a spokesperson said.

Sources close to the government say the sheer number of visas being issued to Russians goes against the spirit of sanctions related to the Ukraine war, and make it impossible to know who is entering the EU and for what purpose.

Figures show that Italy issued more Schengen visas than any other country in the bloc in 2025; between them, Italy, France and Spain received three-quarters of all visa applications from Russians, according to Euractiv.

Italy issued more visas to Belarusians than any other EU country last year, and the number has risen sharply since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. According to European Commission statistics analysed by the Italian news website Linkiesta, Italy issued just 2,968 visas to Belarusian citizens in 2021, compared with 50,709 last year.
A similar trend can be seen with Russia. Italian visas issued to Russian citizens rose from 63,894 in 2021 to more than 165,000 in 2025, almost tripling despite the war.

Germany’s government this week announced measures to hit back at the Kremlin, after it said Russian intelligence was likely to have been behind the alleged Leipzig plot. These included closing the Russian consulate in Bonn, summoning the Russian ambassador to the foreign ministry, and tightening the monitoring of Russia’s shadow fleet of illegal vessels carrying oil in the Baltic Sea.
The EU also announced a 22nd package of sanctions, and said it was expanding its list of Russians who would not be allowed to enter the EU.
Italy’s foreign minister, Antonio Tajani, has ordered checks on the visa issued to the Belarusian suspect in the Leipzig case.

“There is a process for granting visas, because certain requirements have to be met,” Tajani said. “If people meet those requirements and there is no alert concerning them individually, the visa is granted. If that is what happened, we will try to understand why that visa was issued.”

Estonia, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland and the Czech Republic have all but stopped issuing visas to Russian citizens, adopting national restrictions that go beyond EU measures. But several other member states have continued granting large numbers of visas, in some cases increasing them.

“Countries closer to Russia geographically, or with sizeable Russian minorities, are shutting their borders altogether or sharply reducing the number of visas they issue, including to students,” said Eleonora Tafuro Ambrosetti, a senior research fellow and co-head of the Russia, Caucasus and Central Asia Centre at the Italian Institute for International Political Studies (ISPI).
after newsletter promotion

Roderich Kiesewetter, a leading foreign and security policy expert for the governing CDU in the Bundestag, called on the EU to immediately suspend its tourist visa programme for Russians, calling it “untenable” from both a security and moral perspective.
Kiesewetter said the security risk posed was “enormous”. The ability for Russians to move freely within the EU with a visa was being “exploited for espionage and sabotage”, he said.
He urged the EU to restrict giving visas to Russians “to the absolute minimum”.

“This excessive issuance of tourist visas to Russians contradicts the European strategy of isolating Russia,” he said. “It creates a false impression of normalisation for wealthy Russians, precisely those who benefit from the Kremlin’s reign of terror.” He said it was not right that Russia “wages daily a brutal war of aggression and annihilation against Ukraine while Russians continue to holiday without a care in the EU”.
Some anti-war Russian activists in Europe have argued that tightening visa controls for all Russian citizens may do little to curb Moscow’s sabotage campaign.

They point to a shift in tactics by Russian intelligence services, which increasingly rely not on professional operatives sent across Europe but on people recruited remotely, often through Telegram channels and paid in cryptocurrency to carry out individual tasks.

This allows the Russian intelligence officers directing the operations to remain safely at home. In several recent cases prosecuted in Germany and Lithuania, the alleged recruits were Ukrainian or Baltic citizens rather than Russians.

articles.title: Labor groups hit steel plant raids as hundreds lose jobs
articles.summary: Labor groups have decried the displacement of hundreds of workers following a series of raids on steel plants in Luzon and Mindanao.

blocks.text: Published September 4, 2026 11:11pm
Labor groups have decried the displacement of hundreds of workers following a series of raids on steel plants in Luzon and Mindanao.

The Federation of Free Workers (FFW) and the Kilusang Mayo Uno-Southern Mindanao Region (KMU-SMR) slammed the raids conducted by the Department of National Defense (DND), Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC), and National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), which they said left about 900 workers jobless.

In a statement, FFW president Sonny Matula said that if the primary concern behind the raids was the presence of undocumented workers, officials from the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) should have been part of the government operations.
KMU-SMR also decried the displacement of more than 300 workers at Davao Mighty Steel following a raid on its steel plant in Barangay Ilang, Bunawan.
“If this was truly a rescue operation, where is the rescue for workers who now face unemployment, uncertainty and the prospect of feeding their families without a steady income?” it asked.

“We stand in solidarity with the displaced Davao Mighty Steel workers and demand immediate assistance, protection of their rights, and accountability from the agencies responsible for the operation and its aftermath.”
Operatives earlier ordered the shutdown of Chuangxing Steel Inc., a steel manufacturing plant in Magalang, Pampanga, resulting in job losses for 347 Filipino workers and 37 Chinese nationals.
A similar raid was conducted in May at a steel manufacturing plant in Tagoloan, Misamis Oriental, displacing up to 316 workers.

The grounds for the raids included the presence of undocumented workers, mostly Chinese nationals; the possession and use of industrial materials containing radioactive substances; and the production of substandard steel products.
The PAOCC has since defended the series of raids on steel plants, saying it was merely carrying out its mandate to enforce the law.
The law enforcement operations were aimed at addressing alleged violations of nuclear safety and consumer protection laws.
Amid the series of raids and resulting job displacements, the NBI identified 20 factories that allegedly sell and distribute substandard and radioactive steel products. — VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Australia’s housing prices are trending down. See which suburbs have had the biggest falls
articles.summary:
Cotality says prices have declined in most capital cities over winter. Search the data to see how they have changed in your area

  • Get our

blocks.text: Australia’s property market is facing a rare price correction, as rising interest rates and less favourable tax settings for investors accelerate a downturn.

Most capital cities recorded winter price falls, according to Cotality data, with Sydney leading the decline. That weakness is expected to continue, as higher inflation could lead to further interest rate hikes, denting demand.
But the recent price falls are not uniform.

In general, suburbs that previously recorded the biggest price increases also cooled the fastest. More affordable homes are also more likely to hold their value, given they are in demand by first home buyers aided by the government’s low-deposit scheme.
Those who have owned their properties for longer are also likely to be sitting on significant gains, even after the recent falls.
In some cities, including Brisbane, Perth and Darwin, home values are still up more than 10% over the past 12 months.
And the falls have not done much to make Australian homes more affordable for prospective homeowners, given rising mortgage repayment rates have cut borrowing capacity.

AMP notes that while home prices have fallen recently, “it’s just a flick off the top after a 50% surge since the pandemic”.
