articles.title: 1 Million Trees for Cebu: Aboitiz, GCash Team Up
articles.summary: Aboitiz Foundation and GCash are joining forces to restore 1, 200 hectares of forest and coastal areas in Balamban, Cebu through the CarbonPH x GForest Project, a five-year initiative that aims to…

blocks.text: Aboitiz Foundation and GCash are joining forces to restore 1, 200 hectares of forest and coastal areas in Balamban, Cebu through the CarbonPH x GForest Project, a five-year initiative that aims to plant and grow one million trees while restoring ecosystems, supporting communities, and strengthening climate resilience.
CarbonPH is about looking beyond the number of trees we plant. It is about restoring entire ecosystems and making sure they continue to provide value to people and communities for generations.
— Ginggay Hontiveros-Malvar
President of Aboitiz Foundation

The partnership brings together two long-term environmental commitments: CarbonPH and GCash GForest. CarbonPH is Aboitiz Foundation’s nature-based climate action program focused on reforestation, watershed management, biodiversity conservation, and ecosystem restoration. It represents a 40-year commitment to protect and restore forest landscapes in Cebu, with a long-term ambition covering over 40,000 to 71,000 hectares, primarily within the Central Cebu Protected Landscape (CCPL) and surrounding areas.

blocks.caption: Five-year GForest partnership will help restore 1,200 hectares in Balamban as part of Aboitiz Foundation’s 40-year nature-based climate action commitment. From Left to Right: Aboitiz Foundation Impact Lead for Climate Action Fred Dalumpines, Aboitiz Foundation President Ginggay Hontiveros-Malvar,…

blocks.text: Building on the 4.9 million actual trees already planted through GForest, this partnership will add 1 million more actual trees, bringing GCash closer to its goal of 10 million actual trees by 2030. The five-year initiative will help restore biodiversity, support local communities, and strengthen climate resilience.

GCash GForest, meanwhile, uses technology to make it easier for millions of Filipinos to take part in caring for the environment. Through the GCash app, users can earn green energy points from everyday digital activities and use them to support tree-planting initiatives that also help local communities earn a living. With the support of its partners, GForest turns users’ digital actions into real and meaningful environmental impact.

By bringing CarbonPH and GForest together, the partnership goes beyond planting trees. It combines on-the-ground nature-based solutions with digital participation to support the long-term restoration and protection of ecosystems while addressing interconnected challenges such as forest degradation, biodiversity loss, water security, and climate resilience.

blocks.caption: Members of the Singsing Tilapia Growers and Farmers Association are preparing to help kick off CarbonPH in Balamban, Cebu, following an orientation by Baltazar Tribunalo, head of the local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office, on nursery establishment and project convergence — equipping…

blocks.text: “CarbonPH is about looking beyond the number of trees we plant. It is about restoring entire ecosystems and making sure they continue to provide value to people and communities for generations,” said Ginggay Hontiveros-Malvar, President of Aboitiz Foundation. “Our partnership with GCash GForest brings together the strengths of the private sector, technology, and communities to turn this long-term commitment into action. One million trees in Balamban is an important step toward our larger ambition of restoring Cebu’s forests, watersheds, and biodiversity.”

Over five years, the CarbonPH x GForest Project will establish a mix of agroforestry, indigenous and native trees, and mangroves across identified areas in Balamban. The approach recognizes that restoring landscapes requires more than planting trees; it requires selecting interventions that respond to the needs of the environment and the communities that depend on it.

For Michelle Fernandez, Mynt Head of Corporate Sustainability and Communications, the partnership reflects a shared vision of turning everyday actions into meaningful, lasting impact for people and the planet.

“We believe sustainability becomes more meaningful when it is made part of the everyday actions people already take, rather than something that requires them to change their routines. GForest puts this principle into practice by transforming the green energy points earned by GCash users into tangible environmental outcomes through tree planting and ecosystem restoration with Aboitiz Foundation. In this way, technology becomes more than an enabler of convenience. It becomes a bridge between everyday behavior, collective action, and long-term environmental stewardship,” Fernandez said.
Beyond planting trees
The CarbonPH x GForest Project takes a broader approach to restoration by matching its interventions with the needs of the landscape and the communities that rely on it.

Agroforestry will combine tree-growing with opportunities to support sustainable livelihoods. Indigenous and native trees will help restore forest ecosystems and biodiversity, while mangrove rehabilitation will contribute to healthier coastal ecosystems and strengthen natural protection against climate-related risks.

Local communities will be key partners throughout the project, from planting and maintenance to the long-term protection of restored areas. This community-based approach aims to help ensure that restoration efforts are sustained and that the benefits of healthier ecosystems are shared by the people who depend on them.

These efforts contribute to CarbonPH’s broader goal of creating healthier and more resilient landscapes that can improve water security, protect biodiversity, capture carbon, strengthen climate resilience, and support sustainable livelihoods.

Through the partnership, Aboitiz Foundation and GCash aim to showcase how businesses, technology, communities, and nature can work together to turn long-term climate commitments into measurable and lasting action.

The one million trees across 1,200 hectares in Balamban represent an important part of CarbonPH’s larger journey, a 40-year commitment to restoring Cebu’s natural landscapes and helping build a more climate-resilient future for generations to come.

articles.title: MWIS cuts water losses at PEZA-Cavite by 1.7 million liters daily
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Manila Water Infratech Solutions (MWIS) said it recovered about 1.7 million liters of water per day after completing a four-month non-revenue water optimization program for the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Manila Water Infratech Solutions (MWIS) said it recovered about 1.7 million liters of water per day after completing a four-month non-revenue water optimization program for the Philippine Economic Zone Authority-Cavite (PEZA-Cavite).

MWIS, an operating unit of Manila Water’s Non-East Zone, said the program sought to improve water system efficiency, operational reliability and resource sustainability across PEZA-Cavite’s facilities.
The program involved network diagnostics, hydraulic engineering and field investigations to assess PEZA-Cavite’s water production, transmission and distribution facilities.
MWIS also established two district metered areas, or DMAs, to provide greater visibility into water movement across the network and allow more precise monitoring of consumption and system losses.
The DMAs enabled MWIS to isolate service zones, improve water balance analysis and identify areas requiring operational intervention.
The company also conducted step-testing and acoustic leak detection activities to identify hidden leaks and other inefficiencies in the distribution system.
MWIS replaced critical gate valves to improve network control, zone isolation and operational flexibility during maintenance and repairs.
These measures allowed the program to recover about 1.7 million liters of water per day, reducing losses and improving system efficiency during the four-month implementation period.
MWIS also developed and calibrated a hydraulic model of the network to simulate water flow and pressure under different operating conditions.
According to the company, the model was used to optimize water distribution, identify operational bottlenecks and evaluate possible infrastructure improvements.
The hydraulic simulations also guided operational adjustments aimed at improving network efficiency and reducing reliance on energy-intensive facilities.

“At MWIS, we believe that effective water management begins with a clear understanding of system performance. Through a combination of data-driven analysis, hydraulic modeling, and targeted field interventions, we were able to help PEZA-Cavite recover significant water losses and improve overall network efficiency,” MWIS General Manager Adrian Bryan Magallanes said.
“This project demonstrates how innovative NRW management strategies can strengthen operational reliability while supporting long-term resource sustainability,” he added.
Magallanes said MWIS was also committed to helping PEZA-Cavite improve the efficiency and resilience of its water distribution system.

“We are proud to partner with PEZA-Cavite in enhancing the efficiency and resilience of its water distribution system. We remain committed to delivering solutions that drive efficiency, sustainability, and operational excellence for our partners,” he said.

PEZA-Cavite, also known as the Cavite Export Processing Zone, is a 275-hectare industrial park in Rosario and General Trias City in Cavite. It hosts hundreds of export-oriented manufacturing, electronics, logistics and warehousing companies.

articles.title: Seeds of hope: how a local farming project is offering a lifeline to Gaza
articles.summary:
Family-run Al-Qarara Seed Bank is striving to help Palestinians gain sovereignty over their food security

Salama Ayesh Muhanna still remembers the first seeds he planted on his family’s land…

blocks.text: Salama Ayesh Muhanna still remembers the first seeds he planted on his family’s land in al-Qarara, Gaza. At just 17, Muhanna had proudly sprouted cucumbers.
“I was very happy because I saw the results,” Muhanna says. “We were farmers at heart.”
Now 71, he is an agronomist, a community leader and the founder of the Al-Qarara Seed Bank.

The original project, founded in 2017, was situated near the eastern border of Gaza in al-Qarara, an area now completely flattened and inaccessible. Muhanna had a large home back then, olive trees, land of his own, and a successful seed bank operation with dedicated storage and equipment. Everything was destroyed early on during Israel’s brutal military campaign, but after being displaced to Deir al-Balah in 2024, Muhanna and his daughter Hanadi, 38, are now hard at work, regrowing seed collections at Gaza’s only seed bank.

Outside the tent where they currently live in a displacement camp, summer temperatures climb to almost 35C. Another tent houses their small but growing collection of open-pollinated, non-GMO seeds, including local wheat and vegetables such as okra and spinach.

blocks.caption: Salama Muhanna with his daughter Hanadi inside the seed bank. Photograph: Mahmoud Issa/Reuters

blocks.text: Each day, Muhanna rises early to check on the project, a 200-metre-wide plot of land where the family lives, collects seeds, and experiments with new crops. He inspects the seeds to assess their quality, waters crops and checks on seedlings. As the manager of the seed bank, Hanadi deals with local farmers and oversees the growing seed collection – all while studying agriculture and food sovereignty online via a programme partially tied to Coventry University and the Gaza Urban Agriculture Forum. Muhanna jokes that his hard-working daughter will be “managing her father” by next year.

The aim of the project is two-fold; firstly to collect and preserve the seeds of local plants that may thrive better in this landscape. “The war forced farmers to resort to local seeds,” explains Hanadi, because of the ongoing blockades on seed imports, sky-rocketing food prices and growing hunger across Gaza. Yet it appears that a focus on local seed varieties – “baladi” seeds – may prove more effective. That, Muhanna says, is because “local seeds are resistant to drought, fungi, and pests”.
“During the war, they’ve been our lifeline,” he adds.

The projects other aim is to create a node for seed distribution for farmers who need to save every possible penny. The seeds, once collected, are distributed among Palestinian farmers and families in Deir al-Balah who then return the same amount after harvest. Approximately 200 farmers have so far benefited thanks to Muhanna and Hanadi’s seeds, with support from the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). And beyond multiplying seed collections, it is helping Palestinian farmers reclaim agricultural agency and self-reliance – providing for families despite devastating restrictions on resources including vital humanitarian aid.

blocks.caption: Muhanna says the seeds could be key to future food sovereignty in Gaza. Photograph: Mahmoud Issa/Reuters

blocks.text: The seeds are deeply connected to memories of the Palestinian land Muhanna has always called home – and could, he hopes, be key to future food sovereignty in Gaza. “The pumpkin plant reminds me of my father and mother,” he says. “It grew on the vineyard where we lived when I was little.”

The needs have never been more urgent. At least 1.2 million people in Gaza now face acute food insecurity amid an escalating humanitarian crisis, according to a new report by the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC). Despite growing alarm among humanitarian organisations, Israel continues to block access to agricultural land, the imports of seeds and organic fertiliser. Meanwhile, dwindling water supplies, degraded soil and deadly remnants of explosives make farming a treacherous practice.
“Walking in the streets is unsafe, and walking on the land is unsafe,” Muhanna adds, admitting the psychological impact affects their work. “The war destroyed my hope.”

Despite immense challenges, the family know their seeds are helping the community while preserving indigenous seeds against agricultural monopolies, and safeguarding Palestine’s agricultural heritage.
As Muhanna puts it, seeds are “my identity, my patriotism, my nationality”.

“This is about agency. It’s about dignity. It’s about being less dependent on what is or is not allowed to enter Gaza,” says Pat Griffiths, ICRC spokesperson in Jerusalem. “As the occupying power, Israel has an obligation to make sure that Palestinians in Gaza have access to the food, goods and items that they need to live.”
There’s still a long way to go in returning the seed bank to its former size. Muhanna says that before the war, they had about 42 types of local seeds. “Now we have about 28.”
There is also another looming challenge that could affect the seed bank’s future.

blocks.caption: Salama Muhanna inside the seed bank: ‘During the war, they’ve been our lifeline.’ Photograph: Mahmoud Issa/Reuters

blocks.text: “Climate change is what controls us,” Muhanna says as he sips on his tea and shelters inside from the sun. “When the weather is hot, the seeds spoil.” Sometimes he has to plant almost a month later than normal, delaying harvests in a race against time to gather resilient seeds for the future. Still they keep going, experimenting in their fields to see which local seeds produce the best yields. And with almost 2.5 tonnes of seeds collected so far – better than last year – there are signs that the efforts are working.
With each seed, there is hope in Gaza that sovereignty over food security can soon take root.
“Any country in the world that doesn’t have sovereignty over food security isn’t a country,” Muhanna says. “If we establish sovereignty over food security, then we’ll be a real country.”

articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines— Defending champion PLDT got the brunt of criticism on social media after absorbing back-to-back losses in the PVL Invitational Conference. After sweeping 13 games en route to…

blocks.text: Savi Davison and the PLDT High Speed Hitters during a game vs Farm Fresh Foxies in the 2026 PVL Invitational Conference. –MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net
MANILA, Philippines— Defending champion PLDT got the brunt of criticism on social media after absorbing back-to-back losses in the PVL Invitational Conference.
After sweeping 13 games en route to back-to-back titles in the PVL on Tour and Invitational last year, PLDT lost two of its first three games in its title defense.

Savi Davison, however, came to the rescue, dropping 32 points as the High Speed Hitters revived their title hopes with a 25-16, 25-22, 23-25, 25-20 win over Farm Fresh on Friday at Smart Araneta Coliseum.
Aware of the outside noise, coach Rald Ricafort is trying to ease the pressure by focusing on one game at a time rather than defending their title.

“The defending champion tag isn’t really relevant to us this conference because it just adds hype and becomes a distraction,” said PLDT coach Rald Ricafort in Filipino. “What’s more important for us is how we responded after the losses to Nxled and Vietnam, which were really tough for us, especially because we didn’t have much time to recover mentally.”

“I told them before the game that if that’s the lesson we’re going to get from this conference, then we have to maximize it. There are so many distractions outside of the game, but this is our job, so we really have to stay focused,” he added.

blocks.caption: PLDT High Speed Hitters' Savi Davison during a game vs Farm Fresh Foxies in the 2026 PVL Invitational Conference.

blocks.text: PLDT High Speed Hitters’ Savi Davison during a game vs Farm Fresh Foxies in the 2026 PVL Invitational Conference. –MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net
Team captain Kath Arado, who had 24 digs, said the High Speed Hitters have also learned to lean on one another amid the criticism.

“Honestly, you can’t really avoid it because social media is huge now and fans are really invested in volleyball. Personally, I’m not really active on social media, so that helps me avoid the noise,” said Arado in Filipino.
“It also helps that we have our coaches handling the technical side. We check on each other whenever we see each other and ask, ‘How are you?’ From there, we can tell if everyone is doing okay.”

“But what we really want to build is our relationship as a team. Whatever we hear outside or whatever happens within the team, we need to stay together. We’ll just listen to what the coaches tell us because that’s what will help us grow as a team,” she added.
Ricafort also credited the squad’s growth after three seasons together, particularly in handling adversity.
Kath Arado and Savi Davison on PLDT’s final elimination game against Creamline. #PVL2026 @inquirersports pic.twitter.com/H4bdXo4WT8 — Lance Agcaoili (@LanceAgcaoilINQ) September 4, 2026

“The team is definitely growing, and credit to all the teams because the games have been really tough. I think the biggest growth I’ve seen from us is that we’re now able to pinpoint the technical things we need to fix. Before, there were still a lot of differences among the players, but now we’re more solid even when we lose,” the PLDT coach said.

“We’re already at the point where we need to focus on growing as volleyball players. We really want this conference, but because of what happened, we weren’t able to get the games and results we wanted. It’s not over yet, though. We still have to fight until Tuesday,” he added.
PLDT hopes to stay in finals contention against Creamline on Sunday.

“They’re champions, they’ve been together for a long time, and they know each other really well. They’re a tough team to play against, but that’s our job. If we want to win, we have to work harder and stay focused,” Arado said.

“Creamline won’t give us an easy win. It’s not going to be like previous conferences where we could just expect to win. We have to think that we’re back to zero. We won today, but now we’re back to zero. We have to keep working and study them.”

articles.title: Majority of Germans see Russia as a threat
articles.summary: More than half of German citizens believe that Germany's security is threatened by Russia, according to the latest ARD Deutschlandtrend survey.

image.caption: The German government has accused Russia of hybrid attacksImage: Florian Gaertner/photothek/picture alliance

blocks.text: In the past few weeks, Germany has seen a drone attack on Leipzig Airport and an arson attack near defense contractors in Bavaria, while explosive devices and pyrotechnics were found at two substations in Brandenburg and North Rhine-Westphalia.
As the country enters a September featuring three vital state elections, attacks on critical infrastructure appear to be on the rise, and defense contractors are apparently in the crosshairs.

After some initial hesitation, the German government has now publicly blamed Russia for the Leipzig attack, but could the Kremlin also be behind the other attacks? "We are not at war, but we are no longer at peace either," said Chancellor Friedrich Merz of the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU).

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, of the Bavaria's conservatives, the Christian Social Union (CSU), has also warned that Germany has now become a "daily target of hybrid warfare," referring to measures that are not military, but are nonetheless meant to destabilize a country and unsettle the population — including cyberattacks, espionage, propaganda, disinformation, and acts of sabotage.

The developments seem to have alarmed the German people. Some 56% of the eligible voters polled now see Germany's security as threatened by Russia, according to the latest Deutschlandtrend, for which the polling firm infratest-dimap conducted a representative survey of 1,319 German voters for public broadcaster ARD between August 31 and September 2.
East Germans are significantly less concerned

But not all Germans feel this way. Nearly half of citizens in eastern Germany, for instance, feel only slightly threatened, or not at all, by Russia. The same goes for supporters of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), some of whose prominent figures have expressed support for Russia. The survey found that two-thirds of AfD supporters consider the threat from Russia to be low.

The same divisions in the German population emerge on the question of arms exports to Ukraine. Just over half of Germans consider the country's military support for Ukraine appropriate, or think it should even be expanded, but for just over four in ten Germans, that support goes too far. Opposition to sending weapons to Ukraine predominates in eastern Germany and among AfD supporters.
AfD holds steady lead nationwide

The eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt will elect a new state parliament on Sunday, and the AfD continues to be way ahead in the polls and could even win an absolute majority — usually unheard of in German elections.

The party also continues to enjoy strong support at the national level. The new poll suggests that if a general election were held this coming Sunday, the AfD would receive 27% of the vote, one point less than in August, which would make it the largest party in the lower house of parliament, the Bundestag.

The CDU/CSU, meanwhile, remains in second place at 21%, well below the 28.5% it managed in the Bundestag election in February 2025. The Greens would receive 15%, while the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) and the socialist Left Party have seen slight improvements compared to August, reaching 13% and 12%, respectively (+1 each). All other parties would fail to clear the 5% threshold.
Unpopular government, unpopular chancellor
The latest poll also suggests that the current governing coalition of the CDU/CSU and the Social Democrats would no longer have a majority if an election were held now.

Only 15% of those surveyed are satisfied with the government's performance, and even among supporters of the governing parties themselves, a majority is disappointed with the incumbent coalition's performance. Chancellor and CDU leader Friedrich Merz fares even worse: Only 13% approve of his work.
This is consistent with how citizens assess the CDU/CSU's competence.

Also notable is that significantly fewer voters believe the CDU/CSU is capable of finding solutions in key policy areas. While just over a year ago, 31% still considered those parties competent to ensure peace in Europe, that figure has now dropped to just 23%.
A similar loss of confidence in the CDU/CSU is apparent elsewhere: On asylum and refugee policy, on pension reform, and on climate and environmental policy.
On the topic of the economy, the CDU/CSU still enjoys the highest level of public confidence at 24%, but here too, the figure has dropped significantly from 31% in February 2026.
In eastern Germany, the AfD is now the party in which citizens place the most confidence across all policy areas surveyed, with the exception of climate and environmental policy.
Is Germany's weak economy boosting the right-wing AfD?
Economy causing concern

For many months now, Germans have viewed the economic situation as the most pressing problem to be solved. As many as 79% of respondents in the ARD Deutschlandtrend survey say the economy is doing poorly or very poorly. Here, too, however, there are significant differences depending on party affiliation.

As many as 41% of SPD supporters view the economic situation as good or very good, and 37% of Green Party supporters say the same. In contrast, only 3% of AfD supporters share this view — they are much more pessimistic, with 96% saying the economy is poor or very poor.
This article was translated from German.

articles.title: VP Sara's 2 ex-security officers, alleged bagman dropped as witnesses
articles.summary: MANILA- The House prosecution has dropped plans to present two of Vice President Sara Duterte’s former security officers and alleged former bagman Ramil Madriaga as witnesses in her impeachment…

blocks.text: MANILA- The House prosecution has dropped plans to present two of Vice President Sara Duterte’s former security officers and alleged former bagman Ramil Madriaga as witnesses in her impeachment trial, saying evidence already presented is sufficient to support allegations of misuse, misappropriation and irregular liquidation of P612.5 million in confidential funds.

House impeachment team adviser and spokesperson Ace Barbers identified the two former security officers as Col. Raymund Dante Lachica and Col. Dennis Nolasco, who have both figured in testimonies on the handling of Duterte’s confidential funds at the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and Department of Education (DepEd).

“The three allegations in this article have already been substantiated by the previous witnesses na iniharap, ‘yun nga ’yung sinasabi natin sa misuse, misappropriation, at saka irregular liquidation (presented on the misuse, misappropriation and irregular liquidation of confidential funds),” Barbers said during an online press briefing Friday.

“Sa prosecution panel, with the witnesses na iniharap, napatunayan na po natin ’yan (The prosecution panel had already proven that with the witnesses already presented) … So there is no need for additional witnesses like Col. Lachica, Col. Nolasco, and Madriaga,” he added.
Acosta testified as a hostile prosecution witness that Duterte instructed her to turn over four PHP125-million tranches, or a total of PHP500 million in OVP confidential funds, to Lachica.
She also disclaimed personal knowledge of how the money was ultimately distributed after turning it over to him.
Nolasco, meanwhile, was linked to DepEd’s confidential funds through the earlier House testimony of former DepEd SDO Edward Fajarda.

Fajarda testified during House proceedings that he turned over three PHP37.5-million confidential fund releases, totaling PHP112.5 million, to Nolasco upon Duterte’s instruction when she was education secretary.
Madriaga had been considered a potentially significant prosecution witness after identifying himself during House impeachment proceedings as Duterte’s former aide and alleged bagman.

In a sworn testimony before the House Committee on Justice in April, Madriaga claimed that he personally handled and distributed the first PHP125 million in OVP confidential funds released in December 2022 and disposed of the entire amount in less than 24 hours.

He alleged that he delivered bags containing millions of pesos to several locations upon Duterte’s instruction and implicated Lachica and Nolasco in the alleged movement of the money. Duterte has denied Madriaga’s allegations.

Despite Madriaga’s earlier inclusion among prospective witnesses, Barbers said the prosecution now believes his testimony, along with those of Lachica and Nolasco, would no longer be necessary given the evidence already on record.
The prosecution will instead proceed with its remaining witnesses as it seeks to complete its presentation of evidence on the confidential fund charge.

The witnesses are Fajarda and his wife, DepEd Assistant Secretary Sunshine Charry Fajarda; Philippine Statistics Authority Assistant National Statistician Marizza Grande; Police Maj. Jovelyn Magay; and Commission on Audit official Bresilio Sabaldan.
The Senate impeachment court has issued subpoenas for the five to appear as prosecution witnesses in the Sept. 7 to 9 trial proceedings.

Edward Fajarda’s personal appearance, however, could still be dispensed with because of his medical condition if the prosecution and defense agree to stipulate on the matters his testimony is intended to establish.

The prosecution is targeting Sept. 9 to finish presenting evidence on Article I, which covers the alleged misuse, misappropriation and irregular liquidation of PHP612.5 million in confidential funds. (PNA)

articles.title: Nick Kyrgios gets month ban for cocaine, enters treatment program
articles.summary: SYDNEY–Australia’s Nick Kyrgios was cleared Friday to return to tennis after accepting a one-month ban for using cocaine and entering a treatment program. The 31-year-old, who reached the final…

blocks.text: FILE–Australia’s Nick Kyrgios reacts during the Australian Open first-round (AO1) singles match at Rod Laver Arena in Melbourne on January 14, 2026. (Photo by DAVID GRAY / AFP)
SYDNEY–Australia’s Nick Kyrgios was cleared Friday to return to tennis after accepting a one-month ban for using cocaine and entering a treatment program.
The 31-year-old, who reached the final at Wimbledon in 2022, failed a doping test during an ATP event in Mallorca on June 22.
He was provisionally suspended on August 4 by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA), admitting he made “a huge mistake”.
In a statement Friday, the doping agency said Kyrgios had explained his use of the drug occurred socially during a night out before he was due to play in Mallorca.
The ITIA consulted an independent scientific expert at a World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)-accredited laboratory, who found his explanation was consistent with the level of cocaine found in his sample.
“As a result, the ITIA accepted that Kyrgios’ use of cocaine was outside of competition,” the ITIA said.
Under WADA rules, the default suspension for a breach of this type is three months, which can be reduced to one month if an individual commits to a treatment program.
“Kyrgios has entered into a treatment programme,” the ITIA added.
“As such, the player’s suspension will end on September 3, 2026, subject to completion of the program. Prize-money and ranking points from the Mallorca event will be forfeited.”
Boasting a big serve and booming ground strokes, Kyrgios has won seven singles titles on the ATP Tour and rose to a high of 13 in the world in 2016. He is now ranked 918.
His finest performance was on the grass at Wimbledon in 2022, when he reached the championship match, losing in four sets to Novak Djokovic.
Despite his natural talents that is as good as it got, with a series of injuries taking their toll.
He has had numerous surgeries, the most serious a complete reconstruction of his right wrist in 2024.
The Australian last played as a wildcard entry in the men’s doubles at Wimbledon in July this year, when he and partner Alexander Bublik lost in the first round.
Kyrgios was contrite when the news of his cocaine use emerged last month.
“I recently failed a drug test in Mallorca after testing positive for cocaine,” he posted on Instagram at the time. “I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it.
“I’m sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors and everyone close to me. Above all, I’m sorry to the kids who follow me.
“I know the example this sets and I’m deeply disappointed in myself.”

articles.title: PVL: Nxled fends off Ho Chi Minh City to stay in race to final
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Nxled turned back Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City, 25-20, 31-33, 25-17, 25-22, to stay in finals contention in the PVL Invitational Conference on Friday at Smart Araneta Coliseum.…

blocks.text: Nxled Chameleons’ Jonah Sabete-Escamillan rises for a hit during a game vs Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City in the PVL Invitational Conference. –MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net
MANILA, Philippines — Nxled turned back Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City, 25-20, 31-33, 25-17, 25-22, to stay in finals contention in the PVL Invitational Conference on Friday at Smart Araneta Coliseum.

Jonah Sabete-Escamillan continued to display an all-around game with 18 points, 20 excellent receptions, and 15 digs. Myla Pablo also scored 18, highlighted by five blocks, while MJ Phillips chipped in 17 points.
Gel Cayuna dished out 35 excellent sets, as EJ Laure-Cariño had 16 points and 24 excellent receptions, while Jackie Acuña added 12, as Nxled tied PLDT at 2-2.
Nxled, which battles Farm Fresh on Sunday at 1:30 p.m., holds the tie-break advantage with seven points ahead of PLDT’s six.

Hours after a five-set meltdown to EST Cola on Thursday night when they blew a 20-12 lead in the fourth set, the Chameleons squandered another big lead against the Vietnamese, who erased their 19-10 margin and cut it down to one, 22-21, after Dang Thi Kim Thanh’s kill.

blocks.caption: Nxled Chameleons during a game vs Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City in the PVL Invitational Conference.

blocks.text: Nxled Chameleons during a game vs Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City in the PVL Invitational Conference. –MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net
Phillips and Escamillan refused to suffer the same heartbreak, closing out the game with three points including two quick attacks from the former.

“We love to fight because the last game was a five set and it was only a few hours ago. It was really tough and we wanted immediately to show that we never back down, we are not broken, we will never be broken after a losing match and we are ready to fight,” said Nxled coach Ettore Guidetti.

“Obviously, there are bad things and good things. The good thing is this one: we never give up. The bad thing is that we are developing the side out, but we can do even better because sometimes, I joke about this, our side out is kind of bipolar or we play like a super great team or we get scared and under pressure and nothing works, and so it’s a part of the mental game that we have to really develop.”
Dang led the Vietnamese with 15 points and 15 digs. The 16-year-old Ho Thi Bich Diep had 13 points, while Dao Thi Nhung added 11.
Ho Chi Minh bombed out of finals contention with a 1-3 record.

articles.title: Dalaguete vegetable farmer on motorbike shot, killed
articles.summary: A 29-year-old farmer was shot dead in a violent ambush while driving his motorcycle loaded with baskets of fresh vegetables on Thursday evening, September 3, in Barangay Nalhub, Dalaguete, Cebu....…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A 29-year-old farmer was shot dead in a violent ambush while driving his motorcycle loaded with baskets of fresh vegetables on Thursday evening, September 3, in Barangay Nalhub, Dalaguete, Cebu.

Police identified the victim as alias “JR,” a farmer and resident of Barangay Nalhub. Investigators confirmed that the victim died instantly at the scene after sustaining multiple gunshot wounds to various parts of his body.
The incident occurred around 7:15 p.m. while the victim was transporting his produce along the road.
The Dalaguete Municipal Police Station immediately launched an investigation after receiving a call from the Barangay Chairman of Nalhub reporting the shooting.
Initial police findings revealed that the victim was actively maneuvering his motorcycle—which was carrying vegetable baskets (locally known as bukag)—when he was fired upon.
Probe in progress
At the crime scene, forensic investigators recovered two empty shell casings believed to be from a .45 caliber handgun, as well as two misfired rounds of ammunition.
The perpetrator remains unidentified and fled the scene following the attack.
The Dalaguete Police are continuing their investigation to determine the motive and trace the whereabouts of the suspect.

articles.title: Cebuana Lhuillier turns purposeful communication into impact at the Philippine Quill Awards
articles.summary: Cebuana Lhuillier is demonstrating how strategic communication can go beyond telling a company’s story to creating value for the people it reaches. Through its workplace, financial education,…

blocks.text: Cebuana Lhuillier is demonstrating how strategic communication can go beyond telling a company’s story to creating value for the people it reaches. Through its workplace, financial education, entrepreneurship, and advocacy platforms, the company uses communication to address real needs, create opportunities, and encourage people to learn, participate, and take action.

This approach earned the company Merit recognition at the 22nd Philippine Quill Awards across four areas: Internal Communication for Amazing KaCebuana; Corporate Social Responsibility for Money Guro and Happiest Pinoy; Government Relations and Public Affairs for its range of Business Support solutions; and Social Media for Money Guro.

For Cebuana Lhuillier President and CEO Jean Henri Lhuillier, effective communication should create value for the people it reaches. “At Cebuana Lhuillier, communication is not just about telling people what we do. It is about creating something useful for the people we serve,” said Lhuillier. “When communication helps an employee feel valued, gives a Filipino knowledge to make better decisions, equips an entrepreneur to grow, or gives people a reason to believe in themselves and each other, then it has done its job.”
Purpose Across Every Platform
That principle is reflected in each of the company’s recognized initiatives, with every platform built around a distinct audience need.

Within the organization, Amazing KaCebu integrates employee engagement into the everyday work experience. Through platforms such as Workvivo and the Corporate News Ngayon newsletter, which connects thousands of employees across the country, along with the Brillo Awards, leadership programs, and the REBEL wellbeing app, employees have more ways to stay informed, be recognized, be heard, and feel supported.

For navigating everyday financial decisions, Money Guro makes financial education more accessible and relatable by turning complex concepts into practical conversations. Through social media, student engagements, workshops, and even Roblox, it brings financial education closer to Filipinos.

Happiest Pinoy takes a different approach, using storytelling to reflect the Filipino experience. Its 2025 campaign moved beyond the search for a single “happiest” Filipino and opened the platform to stories of hope, recovery, and resilience, giving people space to share experiences and find connection through a shared sense of community.

For entrepreneurs, Cebuana Lhuillier’s suite of business support solutions recognizes that capital is only one part of what MSMEs need to grow. Its digital-first ecosystem brings together business education, expert guidance, tools, mentoring, entrepreneur stories, and financial services to help business owners make better decisions and build capability at every stage of their journey.
What connects these initiatives is a simple approach: start with what people need, then find the right way to reach them.

“What makes these initiatives stand out is how each one starts with a clear audience need and translates it into a communication approach that people can relate to and act on,” said Emirosco Michael Sena, First Vice President and Chief Marketing and Communications Officer of Cebuana Lhuillier. “Whether we are engaging our employees, simplifying financial concepts, supporting entrepreneurs, or telling stories of resilience, we look at the right message, platform, and format for each audience. The Merit Awards validate that approach and the work of our teams in turning strong ideas into programs that deliver results.”
Communication That Moves People

Organized by the International Association of Business Communicators (IABC) Philippines, the Philippine Quill Awards recognize excellence in business communication, including strategic thinking, creative execution, and results.

For Cebuana Lhuillier, the recognition reinforces the role communication can play beyond corporate messaging. Done with purpose, it can help employees feel connected, make knowledge more accessible, strengthen entrepreneurs, and create space for stories that matter.
Ultimately, the goal is not simply to be heard. It is to create communication that leaves people with something they can use, act on, or carry forward.
ADVT.
