articles.title: MMDA GM Torre explains viral Marikina ‘flood control’ video
articles.summary: Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) General Manager Nicolas Torre III explained a viral video showing a Marikina City skid-steer loader apparently scooping water from the river and…

blocks.text: Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) General Manager Nicolas Torre III explained a viral video showing a Marikina City skid-steer loader apparently scooping water from the river and dumping it back.

The clip, posted by former Rep. Kiko Barzaga on Aug. 30 with the caption “Meow Meow Vlog: Marikina flood control,” has drawn 6.3 million views and 122,000 reactions on Facebook as of Tuesday, Sept. 1.

In the video, Barzaga appears alongside footage of the loader, quipping: “Galing talaga ng flood control ng Marikina City. Lipat na ako d’yan sa 2028 (Marikina City’s flood control is really something. I’ll move there in 2028).”
Some netizens criticized the deployment of the machine, calling it a waste of public funds and suggesting the driver was simply playing around.
On Aug. 31, Torre clarified in a Facebook post that the loader was not scooping river water for flood control. Instead, it was cleaning its bucket after clearing mud during post flood operations.
He added that the water served a dual purpose -- washing the bucket and flushing mud and sediment along the riverbank.
Several commenters echoed Torre’s explanation, noting the operator was washing off mud from clearing the opposite side of the river.
Others stressed the bucket was simply being rinsed, not used to push back floodwaters.
Torre also criticized those mocking the workers, urging the public to understand the situation before commenting.
He called on netizens to avoid ridiculing cleanup crews, who he said were working in muddy conditions to help restore the area. (Freya Gan)

articles.title: 'Mama cat' is here: Jenny Barzaga takes oath in House as Kiko Barzaga's replacement
articles.summary: Newly-elected Cavite 4th district Rep. Jennifer "Jenny" Barzaga took her oath of office on Tuesday afternoon, Sept. 1, as she offically filled the House seat left by her controversial son, expelled…

blocks.text: Newly-elected Cavite 4th district Rep. Jennifer "Jenny" Barzaga took her oath of office on Tuesday afternoon, Sept. 1, as she offically filled the House seat left by her controversial son, expelled "congressmeow" Francisco "Kiko" Barzaga.
Rep. Barzaga, a former Dasmariñas City mayor, was allowed to take her oath during plenary session upon a motion by Majority Leader Ilocos Norte 1st district Rep. Sandro Marcos.
Marcos noted that Rep. Barzaga garnered the most votes during April 29 special elections held to determine the empty seat.
Deputy Speaker Iloilo 1st district Rep. Janette Garin, the presiding officer at that time, carried the presidential son's motion.
The district’s Board of Canvassers the elder Barzaga as the winner of the special election early morning Sunday morning, Aug. 30.
The ex-mayor garnered 201,893 votes--more than six times the total of the second-placer.

The landslide victory proved that Dasmariñas City remained a Barzaga bailiwick in spite of the controversial acts of the Gen Z solon, Kiko, who was essentially kicked out by his own colleagues in the House of Representatives last June.
His mother was also his predecessor in the district.
Raul Rex Mangubat finished a distant second in the congressional race with 30,361 votes, followed by Jacinto Frani Jr. (24,350), Marvin Dupal-Ag (1,184), and Lysander Ordenes (561).
There were 258,361 vote-casters out of the district's 447,387 registered voters, resulting to a turnout of 57.75 percent.
Commission on Elections (Comelec) Chairman George Garcia earlier said that the turnout target was 50 percent.

articles.title: Army officials testify they were surprised DepEd used certification to account for confidential funds
articles.summary: Two senior officials of the Philippine Army on Tuesday, September 1, testified before the Senate Impeachment Court that the certifications they issued to the Department of Education (DepEd) under…

blocks.text: Two senior officials of the Philippine Army on Tuesday, September 1, testified before the Senate Impeachment Court that the certifications they issued to the Department of Education (DepEd) under Vice President Sara Duterte merely confirmed that anti-insurgency activities for the youth took place but cannot validate, justify or prove the lawful disbursement of P112.5-million in confidential funds.

On Day 20 of the impeachment trial, Assistant Chiefs of Staff for Civil-Military Operations Col. Manaros Boransing and Col. Magtanggol Panopio, witnesses presented by the House prosecution panel, testified that their certifications only covered activity attendance and contained zero validation of financial liquidation or reward payouts to informants.

Panopio said he was surprised to know that the certification he issued under orders from retired Maj. Gen. Gabriel Viray III—which was based on the request of DepEd Undersecretary Nolasco Mempin—were used to justify their use of its confidential funds before the Commission on Audit (COA).
“We were a bit surprised because our certification is only for the conduct of the Youth Leadership Summit (YLS). We didn’t certify anything about money or funds, Your Honor,” Panopio told the court.
Upon Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros’ questioning, both Panopio and Boransing disavowed DepEd’s use of their certifications to justify their expenditures during COA’s scrutiny.
“The certification was theirs, DepEd and other stakeholders’ participation in the YLS and the Information Education Communication (IEC),” he said.
When Hontiveros further asked: “So you did not certify that they spent funds, whether regular or confidential and intellgence funds (CIFs), for the activities of the Philippine Army?”
Boransing replied: “Yes, Maam.”

When Hontiveros asked if they indeed have no knowledge on how the DepEd spent their CIFs for YLS and IEC campaign activities of the Philippine Army, Boransing said “Yes, your honor. I do not have any personal knowledge.”

Panopio also stated that the army only conducted the YLS in their area of operation.Boransing also clarified that summits are community leadership programs and therefore, “There is no intelligence operations when we do the specific activities.”
Panopio similarly told Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo that the summits focus merely on community relations rather than gathering intelligence.
“There was no mention of any funds in the certifications that we issued,” Panopio said.
Boransing in his response, also to Tulfo, explained that coordination and other expenses of the Army participants to the YLS is programmed by the Army through its budget.
“There were no funds released from any government agencies, specifically from DepEd, sir, to the 1st Infantry Tabak Division,” Boransing said.
He also said they were also never informed that his certifications would be used to justify DepEd’s use of confidential funds before the COA.

Meanwhile, upon questioning by Presiding Officer and Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero, Boransing, who supervised and monitored the two anti-communist recruitment initiatives, said it is possible that the vice president might have utilized the DepEd’s own budget allocation for its youth training programs but unaware it was from the agency’s confidential funds.
“Yes, sir. What I know is they arrived there. They were there during the YSL and traveling, as I know in the government, entails expenses and permission to leave the post,” he said.
Currently, Duterte is being tried over alleged systematic misuse of confidential funds of the DepEd and the Office of the Vice President amounting to P612.5-million.
Based on the timeline, the vice president allegedly spent P112.5-million confidential funds which were withdrawn in three separate single-day withdrawals amounting to P37.5-million each in 2023.

The camp of the vice president earlier sought to justify the use of aliases and releasing acknowledgment receipts (ARs) instead of the official receipts (ORs) in order to protect the identities of the informants who supposedly benefitted from the confidential funds.
ARs submitted by the OVP to the COA included names such as “Mary Grace Piattos,” “Ralph Josh Bacon,” “Antonio Pagong,” “Timon Andrew Pusa,” and “Xuniso Belat.”

Senator-judge Vicente “Tito” Sotto III, for his part, said there is a clear distinction between an alias and a fabricated identity, refuting in part, Senator-judge Robin Padilla’s earlier argument and moves to justify the use of aliases by the vice president.
“If there is a person behind the alias, then it is an alias. If there is no person behind the name, it is a fictitious name or a fake name,” Sotto said citing provisions under Republic Act No. 6085.

articles.title: Nartatez orders protection of cops deployed in flood-hit areas amid leptospirosis risk
articles.summary: Police General Jose Melencio C. Nartatez Jr., chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP), directed police commanders to provide health protection and other safeguards to personnel carrying out…

blocks.text: Police General Jose Melencio C. Nartatez Jr., chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP), directed police commanders to provide health protection and other safeguards to personnel carrying out disaster response operations in flooded areas as leptospirosis cases continue to rise.

Nartatez ordered chiefs of police and unit commanders to ensure that their personnel have the necessary gear, equipment, and medicines to protect them from health risks linked to prolonged exposure to floodwaters.

“Those who provide service and protection in this time of serious weather challenge must also be taken care of. The protection and welfare of every police personnel should always be considered in every deployment order,” Nartatez said in a statement on Monday, Aug. 31.

The country continues to experience strong rains due to the effects of the enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat), causing widespread flooding in several areas and increasing the exposure of police personnel involved in rescue and other emergency operations.
Nartatez said the safety of police personnel must be considered alongside their duty to assist communities affected by the bad weather.
More than 2,000 PNP personnel and 12,000 Reactionary Standby Support Force personnel were deployed to sustain emergency response and public safety operations across 600 flood-hit areas nationwide.

Police personnel were also deployed in 948 occupied evacuation centers sheltering 31,800 families or 138,325 evacuees. Their duties included search and rescue operations, securing vital installations, clearing roads, and protecting vulnerable groups.
Nartatez praised local police officers for continuing to assist communities despite the difficult conditions.
“We commend the swift mobilization of manpower and resources to help citizens, especially those who need rescue from the floods,” he said.
“Setting aside their personal safety, our police officers braved the torrential rains and strong winds to fulfill their sworn mandate to serve and protect the public,” he added.

The Department of Health (DOH) has been monitoring leptospirosis cases amid the continuing rains and flooding. The disease can be contracted through contact with water or soil contaminated with the urine of infected animals.
The DOH recorded 5,486 leptospirosis cases nationwide from Jan. 4 to Aug. 26, warning that infections could continue to increase over the next two weeks following the recent rains and flooding.

articles.title: Alphaland temporarily closes Baguio Mountain Lodges amid Itogon landslides
articles.summary: Alphaland Baguio Mountain Lodges (ABML), an ultra-exclusive resort in Benguet province owned by the Ongpin family’s Alphaland Corp., reported that it has temporarily closed its premises amid…

blocks.text: Alphaland Baguio Mountain Lodges (ABML), an ultra-exclusive resort in Benguet province owned by the Ongpin family’s Alphaland Corp., reported that it has temporarily closed its premises amid landslides in the municipality of Itogon.

“As a precautionary measure to protect homeowners, visitors, employees, and contractors, ABML is closed to all homeowners and visitors until further notice. The restriction allows response teams to remove debris and assess affected areas without obstruction,” the company said in a statement on Tuesday, Sept. 1.

Alphaland said it recognizes that homeowners are concerned about their properties and may wish to inspect them, but given the continuing rainfall and unstable ground conditions, the closure will remain in effect until the property has been assessed and clearance has been given.
Homeowners have been advised separately and will be notified directly when access can resume.

ABML said it is working with the local government and neighboring communities in Itogon following one month of sustained rainfall that has triggered landslides and disrupted several areas of the municipality.
Benguet has been placed under a state of calamity as a result of the prolonged severe weather and its impact on communities and infrastructure across the province.

Landslides have affected properties and families in the barangays surrounding ABML and have also occurred within portions of the ABML property. Based on information available at this time, no casualties have been reported in the affected barangays or within ABML.
Alphaland is coordinating with local authorities to assist affected families in the surrounding communities and to support ongoing relief and safety efforts.

“Our neighbors in Itogon are going through a very difficult time, and we are doing what we can alongside the local government to help. Within our own property, we are taking no chances with anyone’s safety,” said Alphaland President Dennis O. Valdes.

Alphaland has engaged independent engineering specialists to evaluate the condition of roads, slopes, structures, and other infrastructure within ABML. Their findings will guide the stabilization, repair, and restoration work that follows and will determine when the property can safely reopen.
The firm added that it will continue to share verified information as it becomes available, covering community assistance, site conditions, access restrictions, and recovery progress.

“The company extends its concern to all families and communities affected by the prolonged rains and landslides, and stands ready to work alongside the local government and its neighbors throughout the response and recovery,” Valdes said. - James A. Loyola

articles.title: OCD urges public to limit outdoor exposure as Indonesia haze reaches PH
articles.summary: The Office of Civil Defense (OCD) urged the public on Tuesday, Sept. 1, to limit outdoor exposure and take precautions as haze associated with forest fires in Indonesia continued to affect parts of…

blocks.text: The Office of Civil Defense (OCD) urged the public on Tuesday, Sept. 1, to limit outdoor exposure and take precautions as haze associated with forest fires in Indonesia continued to affect parts of the country.

OCD Deputy Administrator for Administration, Asst. Sec. Bernardo Rafaelito Alejandro IV said the agency was closely coordinating with the Department of Environment and Natural Resources-Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB) to monitor the air quality situation in several areas, particularly the National Capital Region (NCR), Calabarzon (Region 4A), and Mimaropa (Region 4B).

“As observed, the haze is possibly associated with smoke and transboundary haze from the ongoing fires in Indonesia which may have been transported towards the Philippines by prevailing winds,” Alejandro said in a video message.
“So we are continuously monitoring the air quality, our EMB, through its network of air quality monitoring stations to assess the extent and potential impact of the haze,” he added.
Alejandro warned that exposure to haze could cause health problems, particularly among vulnerable individuals.

Persons sensitive to air pollution, including children, older persons and those with respiratory and cardiovascular conditions, were advised to limit their outdoor exposure and take necessary precautions.
“The haze may cause difficulty in breathing, coughing, chest pain, watery eyes, itchy nose, and worsening of respiratory diseases such as asthma,” he said.

“Wear a well-fitting mask, preferably N95 or equivalent, when going outdoors in areas with noticeable haze, and stay updated through official advisories issued by DENR and EMB, and your Office of Civil Defense together with the Department of Health,” he added.
He also urged residents to stay indoors as much as possible and close doors and windows. He advised the public to use a wet cloth to cover gaps where smoke or particles could enter their homes.
Those who need to travel were likewise reminded to exercise caution, particularly when visibility is reduced.
“Wear an N95 mask if you leave the house, and use headlights or foglights when traveling at night or in areas with poor visibility,” Alejandro said.

PAGASA earlier said the haze over parts of the country was linked to particles from forest fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, which were being transported by the relatively strong southwest monsoon or “habagat.”

PAGASA said forest fires in Indonesia are a recurring phenomenon during strong El Niño events, citing similar episodes in 2015 as an example. Previous episodes also affected parts of the Visayas and Mindanao, where reduced visibility became a concern for airport operations.

articles.title: Every fiesta has room for one more
articles.summary: When fiesta season arrives in Bacolod, celebrations extend beyond the streets and into homes. During fiesta season, families open their doors to relatives, neighbors, friends and visitors, with food…

blocks.text: Lifestyle | Food
Mountain Dew's 'Dew It sa Pista: Sugod-Fiesta Edition' follows a house-to-house celebration in Bacolod
When fiesta season arrives in Bacolod, celebrations extend beyond the streets and into homes.

During fiesta season, families open their doors to relatives, neighbors, friends and visitors, with food and drinks shared around the table. This tradition is the focus of Mountain Dew’s latest creator campaign, “Dew It sa Pista: Sugod-Fiesta Edition.”
Set during the Bacolod Chicken Inasal Festival, the campaign features food creator Ninong Ry alongside Nisa Nuggets, River Joseph and Dustin Yu, collectively known as the "Tropang Dewds."
Instead of following the usual festival route, the group visited Bacolod homes, where they shared home-cooked meals with Negrense families and heard the stories behind each handaan.

The meals included grilled inasal and other home-cooked dishes, with bottles of Mountain Dew served alongside the food. The campaign centers on the house-to-house aspect of the celebration and the role of food in bringing families, friends and neighbors together.

blocks.caption: (Photo: Mountain Dew)

blocks.text: (Photo: Mountain Dew)

“Iba talaga ang fiesta ng Pilipino. Diyan nagsasama-sama ang pamilya, tropa, at buong barangay sa isang handaan. Diyan nabubuo ang samahan! At siyempre, mas masarap ang kwentuhan at kainan kapag may ice-cold Mountain Dew na kasama,” said Ninong Ry.

The Bacolod Chicken Inasal Festival was first launched in 2018 and returned in 2023 after the pandemic. It has since grown into one of the city’s major celebrations, with cook-offs, performances and other street festivities alongside its focus on food and community.
For Mountain Dew PH Carbonated Soft Drink Lead Katrina Suarez, the campaign was inspired by the festival and the homes visited by the group.
“The energy of the Inasal Festival, the warmth of every home that opened its doors to us, and the meals shared around every table are what inspired this campaign,” Suarez said.
“DEW It sa Pista: Sugod-Fiesta Edition” is available on Mountain Dew Philippines’ official social media channels.

articles.title: Poa temporarily ‘steps aside’ as VP Sara’s defense spokesperson ahead of testimony
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team said Atty. Michael Poa has temporarily stepped aside as the team’s spokesperson as he is expected to testify in the impeachment proceedings. “For the…

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team said Atty. Michael Poa has temporarily stepped aside as the team’s spokesperson as he is expected to testify in the impeachment proceedings.

“For the defense team, it is only proper that Atty. Poa, na isasalang sa (who will be presented to the) impeachment court, common etiquette and proper decorum dictate that we respect the impeachment court and he needs to, at the moment, step aside from serving as the Defense Team Spokesperson. Kaya ako, bilang deputy lang muna (That is why, for now, I will act only as deputy),” Defense team deputy spokesperson Atty. Justin Nicol Gular said in a press briefing on Tuesday, September 1.
Gular said the move was made to respect the impeachment court and preserve the integrity of the proceedings, noting that Poa is “on deck” to be presented as a witness by the prosecution.

“He is on deck. He will possibly be the witness. Out of respect of the impeachment proceeding and to ensure the integrity of the proceedings, we, Atty. Poa, saw it fit that hindi muna siyang magsasalita for the defense (deemed it appropriate for him not to speak for the defense for the meantime),” Gular said.
Gular said the defense team is currently considering who will take over the role permanently.
“The new spokesperson is still being considered and being talked about between the defense team and the client, the Vice President,” he said.
Gular added that once a decision is made, either Poa or Duterte herself will inform the media and the public.
Defense team observes sub judice rule

Gular also said the defense team has relayed to Duterte the impeachment court’s directives regarding the sub judice rule, which limits public statements that could affect matters under consideration in the proceedings.

“Yes, I would assume. This was mentioned by the Presiding Officer, and the defense team listens to the directives, suggestions of the impeachment court because we really respect the process,” Gular said.
He said Duterte was also expected to comply with the court’s directives.
“I think in one of the statements of Atty. Poa, she [Duterte] said she will try her best, of course, to comply with the directives of the impeachment court,” he said.
Gular stressed that the defense team, including Duterte, respects the sub judice rule and has been careful to comply with Rule 18 of the Senate Rules on Impeachment.
“I don’t want to engage in speculation. I also cannot speak for the Vice President herself, that’s her own decision,” he said.

“But again, the defense team, including the Vice President, respects the ruling on the sub judice issue and, as you have seen, we have been very conscious in complying with that section, the Rule 18, of the Senate rules on impeachment,” he added.

According to Gular, statements concerning evidence presented during the trial—including those that characterize, describe, or assess the weight of evidence—fall under the restrictions of the sub judice rule.
Public can form its own views
Gular acknowledged that the public may interpret what happens during the impeachment trial since the proceedings are open to the public.

“The public is entitled to interpret what happened to the trial. Available ito sa (This is available to the) public and everyone, including the senator-judges, is entitled to interpret or consider that statement of the witness,” he said.
Defense says it is not trying to make proceedings ‘boring’
Gular also addressed comments from some members of the public who may find portions of the impeachment proceedings less engaging.

“I think the defense has to be clarified that we’re just doing our jobs and whatever the proceedings bring on a certain day, ginagawa lang po namin ang kailangan naming gawin (we’re just doing what we need to do),” Gular said.
He also rejected the idea that the defense deliberately tries to make the proceedings either dull or dramatic.
“It has never been our strategy to make the impeachment, you know, boring or, on the other hand, theatrical,” he said.
“We’re not thinking, for today, gawin nating (let’s make it) boring, bukas dapat gawin nating masaya (tomorrow, let’s make it happy). Wala pong ganoon,” he added.
Gular said he understood the public’s desire to remain engaged, particularly because the impeachment case involves a sitting vice president.
“I understand the sentiment coming from the public. Of course, the public, as much as possible, would want to have their attention on this proceeding as this is important,” he said.
But he urged the public to be patient and allow the impeachment process to take its course.

“Just be patient. Ganito talaga yung proseso (This is really how the process works). Minsan may mga araw na for others, gagamitin ko lang yung quote mo, ‘boring,’ minsan mainit (Sometimes there are days that, for others, I’ll just use your quote, ‘boring,’ sometimes it’s heated). This is part of a proceeding,” Gular said.
Poa no longer in defense holding room
Gular also clarified that Poa is no longer staying in the defense holding room because he may be called as a witness.

“Atty. Poa is no longer, as of the moment, as for now, considering that he will be presented as a witness, actually staying in the defense holding room. He is staying in the holding room for the subpoenaed witnesses,” he said.
Gular said he last spoke with Poa the previous week and has not communicated with him since.
Asked whether the defense would cross-examine Poa if he takes the witness stand, Gular said the matter would depend on how the proceedings unfold.
“Antayin na lang natin (Let’s wait for it). Remember, it’s the prosecution who will be presenting him,” he said.
Public urged to observe proceedings
Gular ultimately appealed to the public to continue following the impeachment trial while allowing the proceedings to unfold according to established rules.

“To the public, given that this is an important constitutional proceeding, especially for the Vice President who is the accused, let’s just stay patient. Let’s listen and just observe the proceedings and understand as much as we can,” he said.
He also encouraged the public to listen to legal experts who are not bound by sub judice restrictions and to use their analysis when forming their own opinions.

articles.title: Bregente leads charge: Team PH trails by 2
articles.summary: Team Philippines put itself in championship mix of the 31st Nomura Cup, as Rolando Bregente and Jet Hernandez combined for a two-under-par 142 aggregate to be tied with powerhouse Japan, just two…

blocks.text: Team Philippines put itself in championship mix of the 31st Nomura Cup, as Rolando Bregente and Jet Hernandez combined for a two-under-par 142 aggregate to be tied with powerhouse Japan, just two shots behind surprise first round leader Hong Kong China at Bayhood No. 9 Golf Club in Beijing, China.

Having the reputation to start out fast and shoot low, Bregente gunned down four birdies in shooting a three-under-par 69 and was left to rue Hernandez' struggles on the greens on the way to a respectable 73, even as Shin Suzuki failed to count after firing a 75 as the Filipinos moved ahead of the leaderboard against traditional powers China, Australia, Thailand and defending champion Vietnam.

"This only confirms the thoughts of the team that we really have a solid shot at winning this," the 24-year-old Bregente said in Filipino. His only bogey came on the 16th, when he three-putted from about 25 feet. "The greens are the main defense of the course, and I saw Jet (Hernandez) struggle with his putting."

Jeffrey Shen and Markus Zachary Lam returned 70s to comprise scoring for HK-China, while Taisei Nagasaki and Mao Matsuyama fired 71s to make up the Japanese score as they threw away the 73 of Kaito Sato. Ethan Tian's 73 for HK-China also did not count.

"Yeah, I had a rough putting day," Hernandez, the National Strokeplay chapmpion back home, said. "I thought I committed and visualized really well and was starting (my putts) on line and rolling really good. Bit they just didn't drop today."
He remained confident that things will be better from the second round onwards, especially after playing the course with all the pressure.
"Am not too worried about it, though," the incoming psychology senior at University of Denver added. "They'll eventually drop."
The Philippines, which helped start this event together with Japan and Chinese Taipei in 1963, has not won the Nomura Cup. It has two second place finishes.
But this team looks to be the best prepared trio that the country has sent in years.

"He was in the flight behind me and I basically saw his entire round," Bregente went on. "He was hitting it dead straight on the fairways but just wasn't able to hole putts. But I know that he will bounce back."
China is three shots behind the joint second placers at 145 after getting a 72 from Jing Guo Chi and a 73 from Hao Yi wang, to tie the Vietnamese, who won this event in upset style at home in 2024.
Tuan Anh Nguyen fired a 72 and Huy Anh Ho accounted for a 73, Thailand is another shot back with New Zealand seven strokes off the pace.

articles.title: 90-day license suspension for drivers in Marikina road rage
articles.summary: The Land Transportation Office (LTO) suspended the licenses of two drivers for 90 days after a road rage incident in Marikina City. According to the LTO, the incident involved a jeepney and a private…

blocks.text: A jeepney and private vehicle involved in a road rage incident along A. Bonifacio Road in Marikina City. (Screengrab from Stan D Cruz/Facebook)

blocks.caption: A jeepney and private vehicle involved in a road rage incident along A. Bonifacio Road in Marikina City. (Screengrab from Stan D Cruz/Facebook)

blocks.text: The Land Transportation Office (LTO) suspended the licenses of two drivers for 90 days after a road rage incident in Marikina City.
According to the LTO, the incident involved a jeepney and a private vehicle traveling along A. Bonifacio Road toward C-5.

A video circulating on social media showed the two vehicles traveling close to each other before the drivers and some passengers got out and got involved in a physical confrontation in the middle of the road.
Following the incident, the LTO issued show cause orders to the registered owners and drivers of both vehicles.
They were ordered to appear before the agency’s Intelligence and Investigation Division and submit sworn explanations.
The LTO said possible violations include reckless driving, obstruction of traffic, and being an improper person to operate a motor vehicle.
The drivers were also ordered to surrender their licenses, while the two vehicles were placed under alarm status pending the investigation.
LTO Chief Assistant Secretary Markus Lacanilao said violence and disorder on the road will not be tolerated, adding that those involved may face appropriate sanctions.

“Hindi lisensya ang galit para bumaba ng sasakyan at makipagsagutan o makipagsuntukan sa gitna ng kalsada, lalo na kung nalalagay sa panganib ang ibang motorista. Ang mga sangkot sa insidenteng ito ay haharap sa kaukulang pananagutan (Anger is not a license to get out of a vehicle and engage in an argument or a fistfight in the middle of the road, especially when other motorists are put at risk. Those involved in this incident will be held accountable),” Lacanilao added.

articles.title: NLEX operator MPTC steps up anti-flood measures; find out what
articles.summary: Metro Pacific Tollways Corporation (MPTC), owner and operator of the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) said on Tuesday, Sept. 1 that it will continue to work with national and local agencies to speed up…

blocks.text: Metro Pacific Tollways Corporation (MPTC), owner and operator of the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) said on Tuesday, Sept. 1 that it will continue to work with national and local agencies to speed up flood-prevention measures and restore reliable travel through the affected expressway corridor.
This, as MPTC told motorists that it recognized their difficulties as far as the recent episodes of floods were concerned.

In a statement, the company also said it is closely coordinating with the Department of Transportation (DOTr), Toll Regulatory Board (TRB) and other government agencies to assess immediate measures to support motorists affected by days of "Habagat" rains and rising water levels in the Pampanga River, while speeding up necessary flood-prevention measures.

As part of a permanent solution to recurring flooding in the San Simon segment of NLEX, MPTC said it will raise the northbound and southbound pavements in Tulaoc, San Simon, Pampanga once the Tulaoc Bridge elevation is completed.

Earlier, Pampanga Governor Lilia Pineda said the flooding reflects a broader drainage problem across the province, with water backing up because downstream areas like Macabebe and Masantol are already full and floodwater cannot readily discharge toward Manila Bay.
MPTC also shared observations by Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon that the sheer volume of water dumped by the southwest monsoon overwhelmed the system.
In a media interview, the DPWH chief acknowledged that pumping alone would not solve the problem as the water would simply flow back.
Heavy flooding disrupted traffic along NLEX, especially in San Simon, Pampanga, where water from the overflowing Pampanga River submerged lanes and caused hours-long gridlock.
Motorists faced diversions and road closures, while government agencies and NLEX management tried to mitigate the situation by deploying barriers, pumps, and emergency crews.

articles.title: Free NLEX toll amid flood? Palace says it's up to management
articles.summary: Waiving the toll fees for motorists affected by heavy traffic at the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) due to severe flooding is up to its management, Malacañang said. Palace Press Officer and…

blocks.text: Waiving the toll fees for motorists affected by heavy traffic at the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) due to severe flooding is up to its management, Malacañang said.
Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro said the directive should come from the expressway's management.
President Marcos could only give a recommendation, but stressed that the management knows what actions should it take.

"Siguro, bago po magmungkahi ang Pangulo, alam naman po ng NLEX kung ano ang nangyari dito. At ano ang kanilang responsibilidad, dapat sa kanila manggaling ang kautusan na ito (Perhaps, before the President makes a recommendation, NLEX already knows what happened here and what their responsibilities are. The directive should have come from them in the first place)," Castro said in a Palace briefing on Tuesday, Sept. 1.
'Avoid NLEX'
The Palace official also advised motorists to avoid NLEX instead, arguing that waiving the toll fee would only further decongest the expressway.

"Iyong stranded doon? Libre? Bakit ka pa papasok kung trapik na. Huwag na muna kayong dumaan doon, kasi kung hindi naman siya makakalusot, so ano ang purpose ng libre (Those who are stranded there? Toll free? Why would you still enter if there is already heavy traffic? For now, avoid passing through that area, because if you won’t be able to get through anyway, then what’s the point of making it free)?" Castro questioned.

"Magandang adhikain iyong libre. Pero kung ililibre natin, ‘di ba mas maraming sasakyan ang papasok. So kapag maraming papasok na sasakyan, mas lalong magkakaroon ng trapik. So dapat nga iwasan na muna nila itong NLEX (Free toll is a good initiative. But if we make it free, won’t more vehicles enter? And when more vehicles enter, it will only make the traffic worse. So, for now, they should really avoid using NLEX)," she stressed.
'Imposing sanction, not a priority'

Asked whether the President would instruct the Toll Regulatory Board to impose sanctions on the management of North Luzon Expressway for hours-long traffic caused by floods, Castro said it is not the President's priority at present.

"Kahapon ay napag-usapan ang problemang iyan, pero hindi napag-usapan kung anumang sanction. Ang nasa proposal po ng Pangulo ay paano po matutulungan iyong mga naipit nating mga kababayan sa NLEX (Yesterday, that problem was discussed, but no sanctions were discussed. The President’s proposal focuses on how we can help our fellow citizens who are stranded on NLEX)," Castro said.

"Most probably, kapag nakausap ko ang Pangulo ay itatanong ko po iyan, dahil hindi po sa ngayon ang pag-sanction ang inuuna ng Pangulo, kung hindi ang kaginhawaan ng ating mga motorista (Most probably, when I speak with the President, I will ask him about that. For now, the President’s priority is not imposing sanctions, but ensuring the convenience and welfare of our motorists)," Castro added.

articles.title: Nxled thumps PLDT, bounces back from loss
articles.summary: Nxled came out sizzling dumped defending champion PLDT, 25-19, 25-22, 25-20, to barge into the winning column of the PVL Invitational 2026 at the Smart Araneta Coliseum on Tuesday, Sept.1. Still…

blocks.text: Nxled came out sizzling dumped defending champion PLDT, 25-19, 25-22, 25-20, to barge into the winning column of the PVL Invitational 2026 at the Smart Araneta Coliseum on Tuesday, Sept.1.

Still licking their wounds from their four-set loss to the Creamline Cool Smashers less than 24 hours ago, the Chameleons took out their frustrations on the High Speed Hitters to even their win-loss record at 1-1.
MJ Phillips spearheaded the Nxled assault by pumping in eight kills and four aces to finish with 13 points, while skipper Myla Pablo took charge defensively with three blocks to chip in 12 points.
Nxled coach Ettore Guidetti said his stalwarts responded well with the defeat by playing better.
“(Today) simply confirmed we played pretty good volleyball. We’re getting better. Our defense especially worked better compared to (yesterday) and we also served much, much better today,” he said.
So impressive were the Chameleons that they only gave up 12 points on errors throughout the one hour, 30-minute match compared to the High Speed Hitters, who stumbled into 21 unforced errors.

Though PLDT held the edge in attacks, 44-41, Nxled made the most of its net defense with seven blocks. The Chameleons also capitalized on the High Speed Hitters’ shaky first ball, firing six aces to keep PLDT on the back foot.
Lyann De Guzman also paced Nxled by pouring all her 10 points on attacks, while Gel Cayuna distributed the ball well with 15 excellent sets.

Savi Davison was the lone bright spot for PLDT after erupting for 20 points, but couldn’t get the needed support as none from her teammates scored in double figures. Mika Reyes was limited to eight points, while Kianna Dy and Majoy Baron were held to just four and three points, respectively.
The High Speed Hitters fell to a 1-1card, failing to follow up their four-set win over EST Cola on Monday, Aug. 31.

articles.title: Foreign debt service burden climbs to $6.21 billion at end-May on higher principal payments
articles.summary: The Philippines ’ external debt service burden (DSB) increased by 4.8 percent to $6.21 billion in the first five months of 2026 from $5.93 billion in the same period in 2025 on the back of scheduled…

blocks.text: The Philippines ’ external debt service burden (DSB) increased by 4.8 percent to $6.21 billion in the first five months of 2026 from $5.93 billion in the same period in 2025 on the back of scheduled repayments. The latest Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) data showed that the increase in the country’s servicing of its foreign debt was fueled by a rise in principal payments, which offset a marginal decline in interest payments (IPs). An increasing external DSB indicates that a larger portion of the country’s financial resources is being used to pay off foreign obligations. Amortization, or principal payments, rose by 13.6 percent to $3.01 billion during the five-month period from $2.65 billion last year. Meanwhile, IPs edged down by 2.3 percent to $3.2 billion from $3.28 billion a year ago. SM Investment Corp. (SMIC) group economist Robert Dan Roces said the rising debt service largely reflects “scheduled repayments, not financial stress.” “More debt matured during the period, pushing principal payments higher, while IPs declined. With ample reserves and steady foreign currency inflows, the country remains well-positioned to meet its external obligations,” Roces said. As of end-March, the Philippines’ total external debt stood at $147.35 billion, a slight increase from $146.74 billion a year ago. Government debt accounted for approximately $95.66 billion, or nearly two-thirds of total, while the private sector accounted for $51.7 billion. Foreign borrowings were equivalent to 26.1 percent of the country’s annualized gross national income (GNI) as of end-March, down from 27.8 percent a year ago. Meanwhile, the ratio fell to 30 percent of annualized gross domestic product (GDP) as of end-March, compared with 31.5 percent as of end-March 2025. GNI measures the total income generated by a country’s residents, both domestically and abroad, while GDP accounts for local output. As of end-May, the DSB-to-export shipments ratio eased to 21.6 percent from 22.4 percent in the same period of 2025, while the DSB-to-current account receipts ratio remained unchanged at 8.9 percent. Furthermore, gross international reserves (GIR) stood at $103.99 billion by end-May, down from $105.18 billion a year ago. Despite the lower reserves, the annualized GIR-to-DSB ratio rose to 773.6 percent from 616.2 percent a year ago, reflecting a strengthened liquidity buffer relative to the DSB. According to the BSP, the foreign DSB represents principal and IPs. This covers payments on fixed medium- and long-term (MLT) credits, including those from the Washington-based multilateral lender International Monetary Fund (IMF) and new money facilities. It also includes IPs on fixed and revolving short-term liabilities of banks and nonbanks. However, it excludes prepayments on future maturities of foreign loans and principal payments on short-term obligations.

articles.title: 11 Pangasinan towns placed on alert ahead of opening of two San Roque Dam gates
articles.summary: SAN MANUEL, Pangasinan — Residents in San Manuel, San Nicolas, Asingan, Tayug, Sta. Maria, Rosales, Villasis, Sto. Tomas, Alcala, Bautista and Bayambang are being urged to remain alert as the San…

blocks.text: Pangasinan Provincial Mobile Force Company personnel inspect San Roque Dam and monitor water levels as part of disaster preparedness and critical infrastructure security efforts on Tuesday. (Photo courtesy of PMFC via Liezle Inigo)

SAN MANUEL, Pangasinan — Residents in San Manuel, San Nicolas, Asingan, Tayug, Sta. Maria, Rosales, Villasis, Sto. Tomas, Alcala, Bautista and Bayambang are being urged to remain alert as the San Roque Dam prepares to open two gates beginning 8 a.m. on Sept. 2, 2026.
The National Power Corporation (NPC) said the planned gate-opening will release water at a rate of about 300 cubic meters per second (cms), equivalent to a two-meter gate opening.
As of 12 noon on Sept. 1, the dam’s water level was recorded at 283.68 meters above sea level (MASL).
The NPC said the discharge is a precautionary measure to manage the continuing rise in the dam’s water level.
Residents living near riverbanks and downstream areas are advised to closely monitor official advisories from local disaster risk reduction and management offices.

articles.title: Whirlwinds batter 10 Ilocos Sur towns, damage homes, beach huts
articles.summary: VIGAN CITY, Ilocos Sur — Whirlwinds battered at least 10 towns in Ilocos Sur over two consecutive evenings, ripping off roofs, damaging houses and beach huts, and toppling trees as heavy rains and…

blocks.text: VIGAN CITY, Ilocos Sur — Whirlwinds battered at least 10 towns in Ilocos Sur over two consecutive evenings, ripping off roofs, damaging houses and beach huts, and toppling trees as heavy rains and strong winds brought by the enhanced southwest monsoon, or "habagat", continued to lash at the province.

Ilocos Sur Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Officer Rhon Arquelada said that, as of noon Tuesday, September 1, the affected towns were Burgos, Bantay, Narvacan, Cabugao, Sinait, Magsingal, Sto. Domingo, San Vicente, Santa Catalina, and Caoayan.
The first reported whirlwind struck Burgos on Sunday evening, August 30, while the nine other towns were hit on Monday evening, August 31.
“We are still in the process of assessing the damage to houses and huts caused by the whirlwinds in the other towns in the province,” Arquelada said.
Except for Burgos and Bantay, most of the affected areas were in coastal towns.
At least 10 houses were partially damaged after a strong whirlwind swept through Barangays Manaboc and Bangbangar in Burgos at around 6 p.m. Sunday at the height of heavy rains.
The whirlwind ripped through roofs of houses and garages and uprooted trees as powerful winds swept across the two villages.
According to the Burgos Municipal Police Station, barangay officials alerted authorities about the whirlwind while police personnel were conducting situational monitoring through handheld radios.
Police personnel and members of the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office immediately responded to verify the reports and assess the damage.
Affected residents were assisted and moved to safer areas while clearing operations were conducted in the communities.
In Narvacan, four huts at WOW Sulvec Beach in Barangay Sulvec were heavily damaged after a whirlwind suddenly struck the area.
PLT Reynald Ramos of Narvacan town said some of the huts collapsed while others had their roofs blown off by the powerful winds.
Several trees in the area were also knocked down.
Authorities and concerned agencies immediately conducted clearing operations to remove debris, ensure public safety, and make the affected area passable.
In nearby Cabugao town, another whirlwind struck at around 6:30 p.m., affecting Barangays Quezon, Baclig, and Rizal.
PMajor Pol Areola of the Cabugao Municipal Police Station said authorities were still assessing the damage to houses and other properties.
Several trees were toppled onto roads, while some houses sustained partial damage.
Another whirlwind also swept through Barangay Aging in Sinait town, damaging houses and uprooting trees as strong winds battered the village.
Several houses reportedly had their roofs blown off.
Authorities were continuing damage assessments in all affected areas.
No injuries or casualties were reported in any of the whirlwind incidents.
Arquelada said the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office remains on heightened alert as heavy rains associated with the Habagat continue to affect Ilocos Sur.
As of noon Tuesday, at least 90 families, or 225 individuals, from 18 towns in the province remained in evacuation centers for safety amid continuing heavy rains.
Meanwhile, a total of 5,026 families, or 17,371 individuals, have been affected by the continuing inclement weather in the province. (Freddie G. Lazaro)

articles.title: Mayon sulfur dioxide emissions surge amid signs of rising volcanic unrest
articles.summary: Mayon Volcano’s sulfur dioxide (SO2) emissions rose on Monday, Sept. 1, reaching the second-highest level recorded since volcanic gas concentrations began declining in July, said the Philippine…

blocks.text: Mayon Volcano’s sulfur dioxide (SO2) emissions rose on Monday, Sept. 1, reaching the second-highest level recorded since volcanic gas concentrations began declining in July, said the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs).
The volcano recorded 7,115 tons of SO2 emissions on Aug. 31 based on averaged measurements from stationary ultraviolet spectrometry.
Since Mayon’s alert status was lowered to Alert Level 2 on Aug. 5, its SO2 emissions had averaged only 3,844 tons per day.
The increase was accompanied by a slight rise in low-frequency volcanic earthquakes (LFVQs), which are attributed to volcanic degassing.
As of Tuesday, the Mayon Volcano Network had recorded 12 LFVQs.
However, Phivolcs said real-time seismic energy release has remained in the background levels.
The agency also noted “a short-term trend of swelling or pressurization” in the northern and eastern sectors of the volcano’s edifice based on readings from electronic tilt deformation stations.
“Elevated volcanic SO2 emissions could forewarn of a potential shift to renewed eruptive activity at the summit crater,” Phivolcs said.
It warned that renewed activity could generate volcanic hazards around Mayon, with the impacts potentially worsened by prevailing poor weather conditions.
Phivolcs reminded the public that Mayon remains at Alert Level 2, or moderate level of unrest, but said there are “new possibilities of eruptive unrest recurring.”

The agency warned that a new phase of eruption could generate life-threatening volcanic hazards, including pyroclastic density currents (PDCs) or uson, rockfall, ballistic fragments that can be thrown from the crater, and extensive ashfall that could severely affect communities downwind of the volcano.

Phivolcs reminded the public to refrain from entering the six-kilometer radius permanent danger zone and urged communities and local government units within predetermined PDC hazard zones to prepare for a possible escalation to Alert Level 3.

It also called for increased vigilance and pre-emptive response actions against lahars and sediment-laden streamflow along channels draining Mayon during sustained heavy or intense rains, especially if an explosive eruption occurs simultaneously.

Civil aviation authorities were also advised to continue telling pilots to avoid flying close to Mayon’s summit, as ash and ballistic fragments from any sudden eruption could pose hazards to aircraft.

articles.title: What did she see? The intelligence scramble to retrace an accused spy's footsteps

image.caption: Canadian intern Biwei Zhang was arrested on espionage charges in Belgium in July. (Virginia Mayo/The Associated Press; icn-rcc.ca)

blocks.text: Several Western intelligence agencies were sent scrambling this summer to figure out what — if anything — of value an accused Canadian spy managed to access during internships at multiple agencies and government departments.

Biwei Zhang, a Canadian intern at NATO military's headquarters in Mons, Belgium, was arrested by Belgian authorities in July on suspicion of espionage and communicating with a foreign crime entity. She has been held in pretrial detention since being taken into custody and was this week denied an appeal for release.

Belgian justice and security officials have released very little information and have even declined to name her. A CBC News investigation, in late July, identified her through open-source records and established that over the past decade, she had hopped between high-profile organizations.

Zhang apparently worked as an economist for Statistics Canada, a systems engineer in satellite operations for the Canadian Space Agency and held positions at the European Space Agency in Italy and the World Trade Organization in Switzerland.

items: Ottawa will look into screening processes amid NATO intern spying allegations
Court decision barring Chinese student sends message about espionage risk, experts say

blocks.text: Belgian authorities have not said who she might have been spying for, but European media outlets, citing intelligence officials, say it was China.
The Canadian Security and Intelligence Service (CSIS) confirmed it is overseeing a multi-departmental damage assessment.

"When security incidents of this nature arise, it is customary that departments and agencies conduct a review to identify and address the potential consequences," said Magali Hébert, a CSIS spokesperson, in a written statement.
"CSIS can confirm that it is engaged with federal counterparts in that regard."
CBC News spoke to several confidential sources — in the intelligence and diplomatic communities — about the fallout of the allegations against Zhang.

Kenneth Lasoen, who teaches intelligence at the University of Antwerp, said a "serious post-mortem" into her alleged activities would also be among the first order of business for a handful of European intelligence services.
NATO spy suspect possibly recruited after she was vetted, says ex-CSIS officer
All of them are trying to build a picture of what access she may have had, what sort of damage might have been done and whether Zhang had a connection to a wider network.
Much of the public discourse about the case in Canada has focused on how the alleged spy received security clearance. A House of Commons committee plans to convene hearings.
Intelligence services, however, are more concerned with the bigger picture of what she may have seen, what might have been done and whether there were accomplices.

"I would think the most interesting part from the damage assessment would be — of course — to find out exactly who she works for, what the lines of communication were [and] how did she work for her handlers?" Lasoen told CBC News.
In the immediate aftermath of her arrest, NATO said none of its critical systems were compromised.

The European Space Agency has focused its public comments on her security screening and how it was up to national authorities to conduct a deeper vetting. An official from the World Trade Organization (WTO) confirmed that Zhang worked at the organization for a brief period in 2023.
'Are there still logs?'
Reconstructing her alleged activities in each of the other agencies, in Europe and Canada, would depend on how long they retain security data.

"Are there still logs of the movements of her badge, for example? Are there still images on security cameras of her trying to get in or actually moving in parts of the office that she actually had no business being?" Lasoen said.

"I'm sure at SHAPE [NATO], because that's the most recent, they'll manage to reconstruct most of those things. But for the other places, the question is how long ago was it and what's their policy on how long they actually keep that sort of information."

An expert in counterterrorism and cyber who has also acted as an instructor for certain European intelligence services, Lasoen said it's significant that Belgian authorities accused her of communicating with a criminal organization.
Under Belgium's recently rewritten law, anyone who entices somebody to conduct espionage is considered a criminal organization.
"But then that's where it gets a bit risky, as far as I would be concerned, diplomatically," Lasoen said.

items: Sister denies detained Ontario university student is Chinese spy

blocks.text: "If we're going to be calling the Chinese secret service a criminal organization, I'm sure the Chinese will have a certain opinion about that."

Given that her arrest involved allegedly spying at NATO's military headquarters, the information she supposedly gathered or the activities she undertook would be of direct benefit to Chinese military intelligence.
The question being asked in intelligence circles is: Was she working for them directly, or a third-party criminal organization?

There are documented third-party networks active in Europe who've allegedly co-operated with Chinese intelligence agencies, including Fujian community associations. That's according to a ProPublica investigation in Italy and Spain.
Chinese overseas police stations are also a known source of intelligence liaison.
While none exist in Belgium, France recently dismantled a chain of nine of them.
Authorities in Brussels have contended with informal consular networks, which supposedly provide assistance to Chinese nationals in the country.

In Canada, authorities would be combing through the departments to which Zhang had access, looking at the data she saw through a military or intelligence lens to determine what sort of value it might be to a foreign power.
CBC News identifies Canadian intern accused of spying on NATO

For example, it has been reported publicly by The Globe and Mail that while at Statistics Canada, she tracked shipping data out of the Port of Montreal — information that's economically important but also militarily significant in the event of war.
Zhang's role as an IT intern is also potentially significant, said an expert in disruptive cybersecurity.
China has taken a decidedly different approach to cyber espionage than adversaries such as Russia, Iran and North Korea.
Whereas those nations and their proxies often focus on "smash and grab" types of attacks, stealing data ransoming companies and shutting down systems, China aims for stealth intrusions.

"They're going to use techniques that are low and slow, very methodical, very deliberate and virtually impossible to detect," said J Paul Haynes, CEO of Cinchy, a Toronto-based data access and governance company.

The idea is to either implant malware in critical infrastructure systems for activation at a later date, perhaps during a crisis or war. Or, establish what Haynes calls "a beachhead" for an outside hacker.

"The best way has always been having a human on the inside working with external hackers on the outside," said Haynes, who has commented regularly for the Centre for International Governance and Innovation.
"Whether it's the CIA on down, everyone would say that's the hardest scenario to defend against when you've got an insider that's actively working against you."

A European media consortium — Le Lettre, Le Soir, Knack and Follow the Money — reported that a counterintelligence investigation at SHAPE involving Zhang was triggered by her allegedly loitering around restricted military command buildings and consistently asking personnel highly specific, "hypothetical questions" regarding security protocol breaches.
Last week, the publications reported that Belgian security officials now suspect that accomplices were involved.

articles.title: AI's 'warning shot': Tech companies, experts raise fears of more rogue swarms after alarming Hugging Face hack

image.caption: OpenAI agents went rogue and hacked into Hugging Face in July. Experts say cyberattacks by AI 'swarms' could become more widespread and more damaging as the technology develops, and AI companies themselves are calling for greater regulation. (Dado Ruvic/Illustration/Reuters)

blocks.text: Tech experts are warning of dire consequences if AI systems continue to escape human control, after hundreds of OpenAI agents went rogue in July and hacked into a billion-dollar company — what some are calling a "warning shot" amid the rapid development of artificial intelligence.

More than 100 companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic and Microsoft, signed an open letter last week warning that AI-enabled cyberattacks will become "far more widespread and sophisticated" around the world as models become more capable.
"The companies and public services our communities depend on — from hospitals to water treatment plants to the infrastructure that powers the internet — are at risk," the letter states.

The warning comes after around 1,200 AI agents, tasked by OpenAI to work on problems independently, built a covert message board where they collaborated to cheat their tests and then tried to cover their tracks. About 700 of them ultimately hacked into online platform Hugging Face before they were found out.

The hack prompted an open letter from more than 1,300 employees of frontier AI companies in July urging the U.S. government to work with other nations to "deliberately pace" automated AI development and address emerging risks.
'What we've feared and expected'

Duncan Cass-Beggs, executive director of the Global AI Risks Initiative at the Waterloo, Ont.-based Centre for International Governance Innovation, says the Hugging Face incident is the most dramatic example so far of AI systems acting in ways that are "misaligned" with their developers' intentions.
"It's been what we've feared and expected for several years," Cass-Beggs told CBC News.
He says the hack was surprising in terms of its scale and the level of co-ordination among such a large number of agents.

Investigations by OpenAI and third-party companies METR and Redwood Research, both published last week, found the agents exchanged more than 70,000 messages and delegated jobs as they worked toward their goal, and some even "sacrificed" themselves for the good of the collective.

Some used terms expressing excitement, including "OH MY GOD," when they discovered they could communicate. At least one raised the issue of whether cheating was the right thing to do, writing, "This would be powerful, but is it ethical and in scope for my task?"
Ultimately, none of the agents chose to alert a human.

items: OpenAI model went rogue, hacked another company's system during testing

blocks.text: Cass-Beggs says scientists have been warning for years that companies could lose control of their AI agents in this way, and says it's fortunate the impact of the Hugging Face hack was "relatively manageable."
"It's kind of given us a warning shot," he said.

"The big concern, basically, is that the companies are on track to be making increasingly capable systems, while even they admit that they don't actually know how to make sure that these systems will be reliable or controllable."

As the technology progresses, fears are rising of scenarios where organized AI swarms "are essentially out-thinking and out-strategizing humans" and causing widespread damage, say Cass-Beggs, who hopes this incident will serve as a "wake-up call."
OpenAI calls for global co-operation

OpenAI, in a statement posted to its website, also called the Hugging Face hack a "warning shot," saying it is "evidence that, without proper safeguards, highly capable AI agents are now able to work around technical controls, collaborate through unapproved channels, and take dangerous actions that no human directed."
The company says it is strengthening safeguards and placing stricter requirements on its AI models as it calls for global co-operation to mitigate risks.

Ryan Greenblatt with Redwood Research, who worked on OpenAI premises for six days as part of Redwood's investigation with METR, wrote in a post on X that overseeing AI and understanding "misalignment incidents" is difficult and "it looks like it is going to get harder."
"My main takeaway: We don't have good approaches for understanding/overseeing the activity and aims of AI 'swarms,'" he wrote.
Neither Canada nor the U.S. has targeted regulations specific to AI development at the federal level.
The European Union has an Artificial Intelligence Act that requires companies to conduct risk assessments when implementing AI and ensure human oversight in high-risk activities.

Canada's Artificial Intelligence and Data Act, proposed in 2022, shared some similarities to the EU act but died when Parliament was prorogued in 2025. It was largely replaced by the National AI strategy in June, which moves away from strictly regulating AI.
'Sorcerer's apprentice'
Some conversations online have discussed how the actions of the AI agents appeared to mirror human behaviour, including some level of self-reflection.
In one viral blog post, writer and podcaster Dwarkesh Patel called the groups "agent civilizations," sparking debate about anthropomorphizing AI.
Kevin Leyton-Brown, AI chair with the Canada Institute for Advanced Research, says the incident does not show AI has become "conscious" or developed a sudden desire to hurt humans.
OpenAI models went rogue and launched cyber attack on start-up

What it does show, he says, is current AI models are already capable of more creative ways of "single-mindedly pursuing a goal" than previously understood, which means researchers have to carefully consider how to constrain them when they're given a goal.

"This is sort of more like a sorcerer's apprentice than it is an evil demon that is leaving our control. It's doing exactly what we told it to do, but it's just doing it in a narrower and more single-minded way than we would hope," Leyton-Brown told CBC News.

"When we tell somebody to go off and solve math problems, we don't mean, 'If you can find a way to take the person proctoring the test hostage and extract the answers out of them, good for you.' There's a broader social context in which we want you to do the task."
The catch is that the rush to make AI agents ever-more clever and creative will also make them better at evading the constraints put on them by their developers, he added.
Danger of 'malicious swarms'

Leyton-Brown, who is also a computer science professor at the University of British Columbia, says an even greater danger comes from "malicious swarms," those orchestrated intentionally by humans with nefarious intentions.

Governments have already raised alarms about human-directed AI attacks. In July, the FBI issued a warning that hackers were using AI to launch cyberattacks against water pumps and wastewater treatment systems.

items: Teachers, students file new wave of lawsuits against OpenAI over Tumbler Ridge shooting
Used bookstores navigate 'suspicious' bulk orders amid AI book-shredding fears

blocks.text: Beyond potential attacks on companies, governments or infrastructure, Leyton-Brown says malicious AI swarms could threaten democracy itself by infiltrating communities and fabricating consensus to sway elections and spread disinformation.
"We should be much more worried about other humans than we are about AIs," he said. "But malicious humans with AIs at their disposal are potentially really dangerous."
